topic: Mark Twain: The Boy From the River
zh: 馬克・吐溫：大河邊長大的作家
src: The Mark Twain House · The New York Times · NBC

a.title: A Writer Who Loved Adventure
text: Mark Twain was born on November 30, 1835, in the United States. His real name was Samuel Clemens.
He grew up in a small town next to the big Mississippi River. He loved watching the boats.
When he was a young man, he worked on a riverboat. 'Mark twain' is a call that boat workers used. It meant the water was deep enough and safe.
Later, he became a writer and used 'Mark Twain' as his pen name.
He wrote funny and exciting stories, like The Adventures of Tom Sawyer. In the book, Tom gets into trouble but always finds a clever way out.
Today, people all over the world still read his books.
tz: 馬克・吐溫 1835 年 11 月 30 日出生於美國。他的本名是山繆・克萊門斯。
他在大密西西比河旁的一個小鎮長大，很喜歡看河上的船。
年輕時，他在河船上工作。「Mark twain」是船員常喊的一句話，意思是水夠深、很安全。
後來他成為作家，就用「馬克・吐溫」當作筆名。
他寫了很多有趣又刺激的故事，例如《湯姆歷險記》。書裡的湯姆常惹上麻煩，但總能想出聰明的辦法脫身。
如今，全世界的人仍在讀他的書。

b.title: The Pen Name From the River
text: Samuel Clemens, born on November 30, 1835, in Missouri, became famous around the world as Mark Twain. He arrived in the same year that Halley's Comet appeared in the sky, and he joked that he expected to leave with it too.

He grew up in Hannibal, a river town on the Mississippi, and later trained as a riverboat pilot. Boatmen shouted 'mark twain' to show that the water was two fathoms, about 3.7 metres, deep, safe enough for a steamboat. Clemens borrowed the call as his pen name.

His novels The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn turned the river into a stage for American adventure. In Huckleberry Finn, a runaway boy and Jim, a man escaping slavery, travel down the river together, and Huck slowly learns to see Jim as a true friend.
Twain was also a sharp humorist who made fun of greed and hypocrisy.
Remarkably, his joke came true: he died in 1910, the year Halley's Comet returned.
tz: 山繆・克萊門斯 1835 年 11 月 30 日生於密蘇里州，後來以馬克・吐溫之名聞名世界。他出生那年正好是哈雷彗星出現在天空的年份，他還開玩笑說，自己也打算跟著彗星一起離開。
他在密西西比河畔的河港小鎮漢尼拔長大，後來受訓成為河船領航員。船員會喊「mark twain」，表示水深兩噚（約 3.7 公尺），對汽船來說夠安全。克萊門斯就借用這句喊聲當筆名。
他的小說《湯姆歷險記》和《哈克歷險記》，把這條河變成美國冒險故事的舞台。在《哈克歷險記》中，一個逃家的男孩和逃離奴隸制度的吉姆一起順流而下，哈克也漸漸學會把吉姆當成真正的朋友。
吐溫也是一位犀利的幽默作家，常嘲諷貪婪與虛偽。
不可思議的是，他的玩笑成真了：他在 1910 年去世，正好是哈雷彗星再次回來的那一年。

c.title: The River and the Mirror
text: Samuel Clemens, born on November 30, 1835, spent his boyhood in Hannibal, Missouri, watching steamboats on the Mississippi, and his adult life turning that river into one of literature's great symbols. As a young pilot he learned the leadsman's cry 'mark twain', two fathoms of safe water, and later adopted it as the name under which he would become America's most celebrated humorist.

His comedy was rarely merely comic. Beneath the tall tales lay a moralist's anger at greed, cruelty and pious hypocrisy, delivered with a deadpan timing that made readers laugh before they realised they were being judged.

Adventures of Huckleberry Finn remains his most influential and most contested work. Its vernacular narration changed American prose; Ernest Hemingway later claimed modern American literature began with it. Yet its frequent use of a racial slur has led some schools to drop it, even though the novel's moral climax is Huck's decision to help Jim escape, defying everything his society has taught him.
That tension is the book's power. Twain holds a mirror up to a racist society through a narrator who only partly understands what he sees, trusting readers to understand more.
Fittingly for a man of grand comic timing, he died in 1910, as Halley's Comet, which had blazed across the sky the year he was born, returned.
tz: 山繆・克萊門斯生於 1835 年 11 月 30 日，童年在密蘇里州漢尼拔看著密西西比河上的汽船長大，成年後則把那條河變成文學中最偉大的象徵之一。年輕時當領航員，他學會測深員喊的「mark twain」——兩噚深的安全水域——後來便以此為名，成為美國最受推崇的幽默作家。
他的喜劇很少只是搞笑。誇張故事底下，藏著道德家對貪婪、殘酷與偽善虔誠的憤怒；他以冷面的節奏說出來，讓讀者先笑了，才發現自己正被審視。
《哈克歷險記》至今仍是他最具影響力、也最具爭議的作品。它的口語敘事改變了美國散文；海明威後來甚至說，現代美國文學就是從這本書開始的。然而書中頻繁使用一個種族歧視字眼，使得一些學校把它從書單中移除——儘管小說的道德高潮，正是哈克決定幫助吉姆逃走，違抗社會教給他的一切。
這種張力正是本書的力量。吐溫透過一個只理解一部分眼前事物的敘事者，替種族歧視的社會舉起一面鏡子，並相信讀者能看懂更多。
對一個深諳喜劇節奏的人來說再貼切不過：他在 1910 年過世，正是他出生那年劃過天際的哈雷彗星再次回歸之時。

topic: The Day of the Dead
zh: 墨西哥亡靈節
src: National Geographic · The New York Times · BBC Culture

a.title: A Happy Day to Remember the Dead
text: In Mexico, there is a special holiday called the Day of the Dead. It happens on November 1 and 2.
It is not a sad day. Families celebrate the people they loved who have died, with music, food, and bright colours.
Each family builds an altar at home. They put up photos, candles, flowers, and the favourite foods of the person who died.
Orange flowers called marigolds are everywhere. People believe their strong smell helps guide the spirits home.
You will see smiling skulls made of sugar, and faces painted to look like friendly skeletons.
The idea is beautiful: as long as we remember people, they are never truly gone.

gt.en: In Mexico, there is a special holiday called the Day of the Dead.

gt.en: Families celebrate the people they loved who have died, with music, food, and bright colours.

tz: 墨西哥有一個特別的節日，叫做亡靈節，在 11 月 1 日和 2 日。
這不是一個悲傷的日子。家人們用音樂、美食和鮮豔的顏色，來紀念他們所愛、已經過世的人。
每個家庭都會在家裡布置一個祭壇，擺上照片、蠟燭、花，還有過世的人最喜歡的食物。
到處都是叫做萬壽菊的橘色花朵。人們相信它們濃濃的香味能幫助靈魂找到回家的路。
你會看到用糖做成、面帶微笑的骷髏頭，還有被畫成友善骷髏模樣的臉。
這個想法很美：只要我們還記得一個人，他們就從來沒有真正離開。

b.title: Death as a Celebration
text: Each year on 1 and 2 November, Mexico fills with marigolds, music, and candlelight for the Day of the Dead — a holiday that treats death not with fear, but with warmth.
Its roots reach back thousands of years, to Aztec traditions that were later woven together with Catholic festivals. The result is uniquely Mexican.

At its heart is the ofrenda, a home altar decorated with photographs, candles, marigold flowers, and the departed's favourite food and drink. The living prepare it to welcome their relatives' spirits back for one night.
The imagery is famous worldwide: sugar skulls, elegant skeleton figures, and faces painted as beautiful calaveras. These are not meant to frighten, but to mock death gently and rob it of its terror.
Families gather in cemeteries too, cleaning graves and sharing stories late into the night, so that sorrow and laughter sit side by side.
The message is tender and bold at once: those we love are not lost while we still speak their names.

tr.en: Its roots reach back thousands of years, to Aztec traditions that were later woven together with Catholic festivals.
tr.zh: 它的起源可以追溯到幾千年前的阿茲特克傳統，後來又和天主教的節日交織在一起。

tr.en: At its heart is the ofrenda, a home altar decorated with photographs, candles, marigold flowers, and the departed's favourite food and drink.
tr.zh: 它的核心是「奧芙蘭達」，一個家中的祭壇，上面擺著照片、蠟燭、萬壽菊，還有逝者最愛的食物和飲料。

tr.en: The imagery is famous worldwide: sugar skulls, elegant skeleton figures, and faces painted as beautiful calaveras.
tr.zh: 它的圖像舉世聞名：糖做的骷髏頭、優雅的骷髏人像，還有畫成美麗骷髏的臉。

tz: 每年 11 月 1 日和 2 日，墨西哥到處是萬壽菊、音樂和燭光，迎接亡靈節——一個不是用恐懼、而是用溫暖來對待死亡的節日。
它的根源可以追溯到幾千年前的阿茲特克傳統，後來又和天主教的節日交織在一起，結果成了獨一無二的墨西哥節日。
它的核心是「奧芙蘭達（ofrenda）」，一個家中的祭壇，裝飾著照片、蠟燭、萬壽菊，以及逝者最愛的食物和飲料。活著的人準備它，迎接親人的靈魂回來過一夜。
它的圖像舉世聞名：糖骷髏、優雅的骷髏人偶，還有被畫成美麗「骷髏頭（calavera）」的臉。這些不是為了嚇人，而是要溫和地嘲弄死亡，奪走它的可怕。
家人們也會聚在墓地，清掃墳墓、分享故事直到深夜，讓悲傷和笑聲並肩同在。
它傳達的訊息既溫柔又大膽：只要我們還說著他們的名字，我們所愛的人就沒有失去。

ph.ex: The custom reaches back hundreds of years.
ph.exzh: 這個習俗可以追溯到好幾百年前。

ph.ex: Old and new ideas are woven together in her art.
ph.exzh: 她的藝術把新舊想法交織在一起。

ph.ex: At its heart, the story is about friendship.
ph.exzh: 這個故事的核心是友誼。

ph.ex: We talked late into the night.
ph.exzh: 我們聊到深夜。

ph.ex: Old houses and new towers stand side by side.
ph.exzh: 老房子和新大樓並肩而立。

c.title: On Speaking Terms with Death
text: Most modern cultures keep death at arm's length, tidied into hospitals and hushed voices. Mexico's Day of the Dead takes the opposite path: for two days each November, it invites death to the party.

The festival is a graft of two traditions — ancient Mesoamerican beliefs about the cyclical nature of life and death, layered with the Catholic calendar brought by Spain. From this union grew something neither parent alone could have produced.

Its genius lies in tone. The ofrenda laden with marigolds and favourite foods, the grinning sugar skulls, the elegant skeleton known as Catrina in her fine hat — all treat the dead not as ghosts to be feared, but as guests to be welcomed, teased, and fed.

This is not a denial of grief; cemeteries on those nights are full of real tears. It is, rather, a refusal to let grief have the last word — a cultural insistence that love and memory outlast the body.
In a world that so often hides from mortality, the festival offers a quietly radical lesson: that we might live more freely, and love more fully, if we were a little less afraid of the end.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: The festival hides grief by turning death into a colourful party.
The festival is, at its heart, mainly a Catholic religious tradition.
Modern Western cultures handle death far better than Mexico does.
Welcoming death with warmth teaches that love outlasts the body.
q.why: 主旨：愛與記憶勝過死亡。

q.q: In paragraph 2, the festival is called “a graft of two traditions,” meaning it ___.
opts: joins two traditions into one new thing
copies one older tradition exactly
rejects both of the older traditions
replaced an older Aztec festival
q.why: graft = 嫁接。

q.q: Why does the writer insist this is “not a denial of grief”?
opts: Nobody feels sad at all during the festival
Real tears are shed; it faces grief, not hides it
Showing grief is forbidden during these days
People hide their tears so that the dead feel happy
q.why: 線索：“This is not a denial of grief; cemeteries on those nights are full of real tears.”

q.q: What does the writer mean by a “quietly radical lesson”?
opts: A loud protest against fast modern life
A religious rule that everyone must follow
Facing death calmly can help us live more fully
Death should be feared, so we should avoid thinking of it
q.why: 末段。

q.q: How is the essay developed?
opts: Aztec history → its appearance in modern films
A list of the foods placed on the ofrenda
A deeper lesson first → then the festival's Aztec roots
Hiding death → mixed roots and tone → a deeper lesson
q.why: 結構如選項。

q.q: Which action best reflects the festival's lesson in everyday life?
opts: Never mentioning people in the family who have died
Sharing happy stories about a grandparent who died
Avoiding cemeteries so that you don't feel sad
Throwing away old family photos to move on
q.why: 以溫暖記憶紀念逝者，正是節慶的啟示。

tz: 大多數現代文化都把死亡推得遠遠的，收拾在醫院和壓低的聲音裡。墨西哥的亡靈節走的是相反的路：每年十一月有兩天，它邀請死亡來參加派對。
這個節日是兩種傳統的嫁接——古代中美洲關於生死循環的信仰，再疊上西班牙帶來的天主教曆法。從這個結合中長出的東西，是任何一方單獨都無法產生的。
它的天才之處在於它的語氣。堆滿萬壽菊和愛吃食物的祭壇、咧嘴笑的糖骷髏、戴著華麗帽子、被稱為「卡特麗娜（Catrina）」的優雅骷髏——全都不把逝者當成可怕的鬼魂，而是當成要歡迎、調侃、招待吃喝的客人。
這並不是否認悲傷；那幾個晚上，墓地裡滿是真實的眼淚。它其實是拒絕讓悲傷說最後一句話——一種文化上的堅持：愛與記憶比身體更長久。
在一個常常逃避死亡的世界裡，這個節日提供了一堂安靜而激進的課：如果我們對終點少一點害怕，也許就能活得更自在、愛得更完整。

ph.ex: She keeps strangers at arm's length.
ph.exzh: 她和陌生人保持距離。

ph.ex: Instead of hiding, he took the opposite path and spoke up.
ph.exzh: 他沒有躲起來，而是走相反的路，勇敢發聲。

ph.zh: 說最後一句話、做最終定論
ph.ex: Don't let fear have the last word.
ph.exzh: 別讓恐懼替你做最後的決定。

ph.ex: It's not a problem but a chance.
ph.exzh: 這不是問題，而是機會。
ph.m: not as ghosts to be feared, but as guests

ph.ex: You can't hide from your problems forever.
ph.exzh: 你不能永遠逃避問題。

ph.ex: Try to worry a little less.
ph.exzh: 試著少擔心一點。

discuss: How do people in Taiwan remember those who have died? How is it similar to or different from the Day of the Dead?
The festival treats death with warmth, not fear. Do you think that is healthy? Why?
What is one way you would want to be remembered by the people you love?

topic: The Day Television Began
zh: 電視誕生的那一天：世界第一個電視台開播
src: BBC · Science Museum · TIME

a.title: The First TV Station
text: Today, we can watch shows on TVs, phones and computers. But TV was once brand new.
On November 2, 1936, the BBC in London started the world's first regular TV service.
The pictures were black and white, and the screens were very small. Only a few hundred families in London had a TV set.
TV sets were very expensive, so many people watched in shops or at a friend's house.
In 1939, a big war started, and the BBC turned off its TV service. It came back in 1946.
From that small start, TV grew into something almost every home has today.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The start of the first regular TV service
Why TV sets were so expensive in 1936
How the BBC turned TV off during a war
Why many people watched TV in shops
q.why: 全文講第一個定期電視服務的開始；其他都是文中細節。

q.q: When did the BBC start its TV service?
opts: November 2, 1939
November 2, 1936
In 1946, after the war
September 1, 1939
q.why: 第二段：On November 2, 1936。1939 是停播、1946 是復播。

q.q: Why did many people watch TV in shops?
opts: Shops had bigger screens
TV was only shown in shops at first
The pictures were clearer in shops
TV sets were very expensive
q.why: 第四段：TV sets were very expensive。

q.q: In the text, “expensive” means ___.
opts: very large and heavy
new and very modern
costing a lot of money
hard to use or fix
q.why: expensive = 昂貴的。

q.q: Why did the TV service stop in 1939?
opts: Because a big war started
Because too few people watched
Because the pictures were only black and white
Because TV sets became too cheap
q.why: 第五段：a big war started。

q.q: In 1936 a family wanted to watch TV but could not buy a set. Based on the text, what could they most likely do?
opts: Rent a TV set from the BBC each week
Watch at a shop or at a friend's house
Watch the programmes on a phone
Wait a few years for colour TV
q.why: 第四段：many people watched in shops or at a friend's house。

gt.en: On November 2, 1936, the BBC in London started the world's first regular TV service.
gt.zh: 1936 年 11 月 2 日，倫敦的 BBC 開播了世界上第一個定期的電視服務。

gt.en: The pictures were black and white, and the screens were very small.
gt.zh: 畫面是黑白的，螢幕也非常小。

gt.en: TV sets were very expensive, so many people watched in shops or at a friend's house.
gt.zh: 電視機非常昂貴，所以很多人都在商店裡或朋友家看電視。

gt.en: In 1939, a big war started, and the BBC turned off its TV service.
gt.zh: 1939 年，一場大戰爆發了，BBC 關掉了它的電視服務。

tz: 今天，我們可以在電視、手機和電腦上看節目。但電視曾經是全新的東西。
1936 年 11 月 2 日，倫敦的英國廣播公司（BBC）開辦了世界上第一個定期的電視服務。
畫面是黑白的，螢幕非常小。在倫敦只有幾百個家庭有電視機。
電視機非常昂貴，所以很多人是在商店裡或朋友家看電視。
1939 年，一場大戰開始了，BBC 關掉了它的電視服務，直到 1946 年才恢復。
從那個小小的開始，電視成長為今天幾乎每個家庭都有的東西。

ph.ex: I watched the game at a friend's house.
ph.exzh: 我在朋友家看比賽。

ph.ex: Please turn off the lights when you leave.
ph.exzh: 離開時請把燈關掉。

ph.ex: The singer came back after a long break.
ph.exzh: 那位歌手休息很久後復出了。

ph.ex: The small shop grew into a big company.
ph.exzh: 那家小店成長為一家大公司。

b.title: Switching On the World's First TV Service
text: On November 2, 1936, the BBC began broadcasting from Alexandra Palace, a hilltop building in north London. It was the world's first regular, high-definition public television service.
'High-definition' meant something very different then. Pictures were black and white, with a few hundred lines on screens no bigger than a book.

At first the BBC used two rival systems on alternate weeks: one designed by the Scottish inventor John Logie Baird and another by the company Marconi-EMI. The electronic Marconi-EMI system produced clearer pictures, and Baird's was dropped in 1937.

Television sets cost about as much as a small car, so only a few thousand households in the London area owned one. Viewers watched news, variety shows and coverage of events such as a royal coronation.
On September 1, 1939, as the Second World War approached, the service was switched off without warning. It returned in June 1946.
Within a few decades, television had become the centre of family life around the world.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The Marconi-EMI system gave clearer pictures than Baird's system.
The television service was switched off during the Second World War.
The BBC's 1936 TV service grew from a costly novelty into daily life.
Early television sets cost about as much as a small family car.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: Why was Baird's system dropped?
opts: The Marconi-EMI system gave clearer pictures
Baird's system was too expensive to build
Viewers preferred Baird's but the BBC chose Marconi-EMI
It broke down during the war
q.why: 第三段：The electronic Marconi-EMI system produced clearer pictures。

q.q: What happened on September 1, 1939?
opts: It started showing the news every night
Baird's system was dropped by the BBC
It came back on air after a long break
It was switched off as war approached
q.why: 第五段：the service was switched off without warning。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “alternate” weeks means ___.
opts: two weeks in a row, then a break
every other week, taking turns
different weeks in each year
the same week in every month
q.why: alternate = 輪流、交替。

q.q: What does the writer suggest by comparing a TV set to a small car?
opts: They were so costly that few could own one
Early TV sets were as large as cars
TV sets were as cheap as buying a small toy car
People watched TV while in their cars
q.why: 價格相當於小汽車，所以只有少數家庭擁有。

q.q: Which modern technology is in a situation MOST like TV in 1936?
opts: A smartphone that almost everyone already owns
A radio design that has existed for a century
A rare, costly new device that may become common
A book printed hundreds of years ago
q.why: 1936 的電視是昂貴稀有、後來普及的新科技。

tr.en: On November 2, 1936, the BBC began broadcasting from Alexandra Palace, a hilltop building in north London.
tr.zh: 1936 年 11 月 2 日，BBC 從倫敦北部山丘上的一棟建築——亞歷山德拉宮——開始播送節目。

tr.en: Pictures were black and white, with a few hundred lines on screens no bigger than a book.
tr.zh: 畫面是黑白的，只有幾百條掃描線，螢幕比一本書還小。

tr.en: Television sets cost about as much as a small car, so only a few thousand households in the London area owned one.
tr.zh: 一台電視機的價錢跟一輛小汽車差不多，所以倫敦地區只有幾千戶人家擁有電視。

tz: 1936 年 11 月 2 日，BBC 開始從亞歷山德拉宮播出節目——那是倫敦北部山丘上的一棟建築。這是世界上第一個定期的高畫質公共電視服務。
當時的「高畫質」意思跟現在很不一樣。畫面是黑白的，只有幾百條掃描線，螢幕不比一本書大。
一開始，BBC 每隔一週輪流使用兩套互相競爭的系統：一套由蘇格蘭發明家約翰・羅傑・貝爾德設計，另一套由馬可尼－EMI 公司研發。電子式的馬可尼－EMI 系統畫面比較清楚，貝爾德的系統在 1937 年被淘汰。
一台電視機的價格大約等於一輛小汽車，所以倫敦地區只有幾千戶人家擁有電視。觀眾收看新聞、綜藝節目，以及像皇室加冕典禮這類活動的轉播。
1939 年 9 月 1 日，隨著第二次世界大戰逼近，這項服務在沒有預警的情況下被關掉，直到 1946 年 6 月才恢復。
短短幾十年內，電視已經成為全世界家庭生活的中心。

ph.ex: At first, the game seemed easy.
ph.exzh: 一開始，這個遊戲看起來很簡單。

ph.ex: This bag costs as much as a phone.
ph.exzh: 這個包包和一支手機一樣貴。

ph.ex: The lights went out without warning.
ph.exzh: 燈在沒有預警的情況下熄了。

ph.ex: Within a few decades, the village became a city.
ph.exzh: 短短幾十年內，這個村莊就變成了一座城市。

ph.ex: The kitchen is the centre of our home.
ph.exzh: 廚房是我們家的中心。

c.title: Before Television Was Ordinary
text: Every technology that later becomes invisible begins as a spectacle. On November 2, 1936, the BBC opened the world's first regular 'high-definition' television service from Alexandra Palace in north London, and a handful of viewers peered at flickering black-and-white images on screens barely larger than a postcard.

The launch was also a contest. For several months the BBC alternated between John Logie Baird's partly mechanical system and the fully electronic one developed by Marconi-EMI. The electronic approach was sharper and more reliable, and by early 1937 Baird's pioneering equipment had been abandoned — a reminder that being first is no guarantee of winning.

Ownership was a luxury. Sets cost roughly as much as a modest car, and only a few thousand households could receive the signal. Yet those viewers glimpsed what was coming: live coverage that let ordinary people watch distant events as they happened.

The experiment was cut short on September 1, 1939, when the service went dark ahead of war; it resumed in 1946. Afterwards, television spread with astonishing speed, reshaping politics, advertising and family routines.
Looking back at 1936 is useful precisely because it makes television strange again — and invites us to ask which of today's expensive novelties will soon seem too ordinary to notice.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's point?
opts: New technologies start as rare spectacles before becoming ordinary.
Baird deserved to win the competition because he got there first.
The 1936 service largely failed because the war interrupted it.
Television changed politics more than any other modern invention.
q.why: 主旨：新科技先是稀罕奇觀，後來變得平常。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “pioneering” equipment is equipment that ___.
opts: was the most reliable of its kind
was built by many inventors together
was later improved by others
was among the first of its kind
q.why: pioneering = 開創性的。

q.q: What lesson does the writer draw from Baird's system being abandoned?
opts: Mechanical systems are always better in the end
The BBC treated Baird unfairly and unwisely
Being first does not guarantee winning
Electronic systems are far too complicated
q.why: 第二段：being first is no guarantee of winning。

q.q: How would you describe the writer's tone?
opts: Nostalgic and sad
Reflective and curious
Critical of the BBC
Purely factual with no opinion
q.why: 作者回顧歷史並引導思考。

q.q: How does the final paragraph connect back to the first?
opts: It repeats the exact date the service began
It applies the spectacle-to-ordinary idea to today
It argues that today's technologies will never become ordinary
It introduces a new inventor and his system
q.why: 首尾呼應：奇觀 → 平常，並延伸到今天。

q.q: A company was the first to sell a new kind of phone but went out of business. How would the writer most likely explain this?
opts: The company should never have tried to be first at all
New kinds of phones are almost always commercial failures
Customers only ever buy from the oldest, best-known firms
Being first doesn't guarantee winning; rivals can overtake
q.why: 作者以貝爾德為例：搶先不代表勝出。

tz: 每一項後來變得「看不見」的科技，一開始都是一場奇觀。1936 年 11 月 2 日，BBC 從倫敦北部的亞歷山德拉宮開辦了世界上第一個定期的「高畫質」電視服務，少數觀眾湊近盯著閃爍的黑白影像，螢幕幾乎沒比一張明信片大。
這次開播也是一場競賽。好幾個月裡，BBC 輪流使用約翰・羅傑・貝爾德半機械式的系統，以及馬可尼－EMI 開發的全電子式系統。電子式的做法更清晰、更可靠，到了 1937 年初，貝爾德開創性的設備就被淘汰了——這提醒我們，搶先並不保證獲勝。
擁有電視是一種奢侈。一台電視機的價格大約等於一輛普通汽車，只有幾千戶人家能接收到訊號。但這些觀眾已經瞥見了未來：讓普通人能在事件發生的當下，觀看遠方事件的現場轉播。
這場實驗在 1939 年 9 月 1 日被迫中斷，因為戰爭在即，服務停播了；直到 1946 年才恢復。之後，電視以驚人的速度普及，重塑了政治、廣告和家庭的日常作息。
回顧 1936 年之所以有用，正是因為它讓電視重新變得陌生——也邀請我們思考：今天哪些昂貴的新奇玩意兒，很快就會平凡到讓人注意不到？

ph.ex: The children peered at the tiny insect.
ph.exzh: 孩子們湊近盯著那隻小蟲看。

ph.ex: Being popular is no guarantee of being happy.
ph.exzh: 受歡迎不保證就會快樂。

ph.ex: We followed the news as it happened.
ph.exzh: 我們即時關注新聞的發展。

ph.ex: Our trip was cut short by the storm.
ph.exzh: 我們的旅行因為暴風雨而提前結束。

ph.ex: Travel makes everyday things strange again.
ph.exzh: 旅行讓日常的事物重新變得新奇。

ph.ex: Some heroes are too ordinary to notice.
ph.exzh: 有些英雄平凡到讓人注意不到。

discuss: Early TVs were rare and expensive. What technology today is expensive now but might be in every home in the future?
How did people get news and entertainment before television? How is it different now?
Do you think people today spend too much time watching screens? Explain your view.

topic: The Earl Who Gave Us the Sandwich
zh: 三明治伯爵：一道點心的名字從哪來？
src: Smithsonian Magazine · BBC · The New York Times

a.title: Who Named the Sandwich?
text: November 3 is Sandwich Day in some countries. It is the birthday of a man from England called the Earl of Sandwich.
Long ago, people ate bread with meat or cheese. But it did not have a special name.
The story says the Earl was very busy. He did not want to stop and eat at a table.
So he asked for meat between two slices of bread. He could eat with one hand and keep working.
His friends liked the idea. They began to order 'the same as Sandwich'. Soon the food had a name!
Today, people all over the world eat sandwiches. In Taiwan, many students eat one for breakfast.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: Why the Earl of Sandwich was so busy
What people ate with bread long ago
Why students in Taiwan eat sandwiches
How the sandwich got its name
q.why: 全文講三明治名字的由來。

q.q: Why did the Earl want food between bread?
opts: He did not like eating with a fork
He wanted to share food with his friends
He was busy and did not want to stop
He did not have any plates at home
q.why: 第三、四段：He did not want to stop and eat at a table。

q.q: What did his friends begin to order?
opts: Meat with melted cheese
'The same as Sandwich'
A new kind of bread
A breakfast sandwich
q.why: 第五段：'the same as Sandwich'。

q.q: In the text, “slices” are ___.
opts: thin, flat pieces cut from something
whole loaves of bread baked fresh each day
whole loaves of fresh bread
tiny crumbs left on a plate
q.why: slices = 片。

q.q: What does “The story says” suggest?
opts: The Earl wrote the whole story himself
Scientists have checked and proved it
Everyone agrees the story is true
The story may not be completely certain
q.why: The story says 表示這是流傳的說法。

q.q: Which food name comes about in the SAME way as “sandwich”?
opts: A fruit named after its bright colour
A drink named after the country it comes from
A dish named after the person who made it popular
A dish named after the city where it was first made
q.why: 三明治以人名命名；以推廣者命名的食物最相似。

gt.en: It is the birthday of a man from England called the Earl of Sandwich.
gt.zh: 這天是一位英國人的生日，他就是三明治伯爵。

gt.en: Long ago, people ate bread with meat or cheese.
gt.zh: 很久以前，人們就會把麵包配著肉或起司吃。

gt.en: So he asked for meat between two slices of bread.
gt.zh: 所以他要人把肉夾在兩片麵包中間。

gt.en: They began to order 'the same as Sandwich'.
gt.zh: 他們開始點「跟三明治伯爵一樣的」。

tz: 11 月 3 日在一些國家是三明治日。這天是一位英國人的生日，他被稱為三明治伯爵。
很久以前，人們就會吃夾著肉或起司的麵包，但它沒有一個特別的名字。
故事說，這位伯爵非常忙碌，他不想停下來坐在桌邊吃飯。
所以他要了夾在兩片麵包中間的肉。這樣他就能用一隻手吃東西，同時繼續工作。
他的朋友們喜歡這個點子，開始點「跟三明治一樣的」。很快地，這種食物就有了名字！
今天，全世界的人都吃三明治。在台灣，很多學生早餐都吃三明治。

ph.ex: We stopped and ate at a small café.
ph.exzh: 我們在一間小咖啡館停下來吃東西。

ph.ex: He asked for a glass of water.
ph.exzh: 他要了一杯水。

ph.ex: She kept working until midnight.
ph.exzh: 她一直工作到半夜。

ph.ex: People all over the world drink tea.
ph.exzh: 全世界的人都喝茶。

b.title: A Snack Named After an Earl
text: Americans celebrate National Sandwich Day on November 3, the birthday of John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich, who was born in England in 1718.
People had, of course, been eating bread with fillings for thousands of years. What Montagu gave the world was not the food itself but its name.

According to a popular story, first written down by a French visitor in the 1760s, the Earl was so absorbed in a long card game that he refused to leave the table and asked for beef between two slices of toast.
One of his biographers offers a less colourful explanation: Montagu, a hard-working politician who ran the navy, often ate at his desk while he worked.
Either way, the convenient snack became fashionable among his friends, who asked for 'the same as Sandwich', and the name stuck.
Today the idea has travelled everywhere, from Vietnamese bánh mì to Taiwan's gua bao — proof that a good idea can outlive the person it is named after.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The Earl of Sandwich invented the idea of eating bread with fillings.
The sandwich is named after an earl, though why he ate it is uncertain.
The Earl of Sandwich was said to love playing cards for long hours.
Sandwiches are now eaten in many different forms all over the world.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；第二項與文意相反。

q.q: What did Montagu give the world, according to the text?
opts: The idea of putting meat in bread
A famous card game
The name 'sandwich'
A recipe for toast
q.why: 第二段：not the food itself but its name。

q.q: What is the 'less colourful' explanation?
opts: He was playing cards all night
He was too busy travelling
He did not like the food at dinner parties
He ate at his desk while working
q.why: 第四段：often ate at his desk while he worked。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “absorbed” means ___.
opts: completely focused on something
completely bored and unable to focus
quickly bored by a game
slightly confused by a task
q.why: absorbed (in) = 全神貫注。

q.q: Why does the writer mention bánh mì and gua bao?
opts: To say they are older than the English sandwich
To compare their prices with British sandwiches
To explain where the Earl first got his idea
To show the sandwich idea has spread worldwide
q.why: 最後一段：the idea has travelled everywhere。

q.q: A website says: “The Earl of Sandwich invented bread with meat inside.” Based on the text, what is wrong with this?
opts: People ate filled bread for ages; he only gave it a name
Nothing — it is exactly what the text says happened
He invented toast, not bread with meat inside
Nothing — the Earl was the first person ever to put meat in bread
q.why: 第二段：People had … been eating bread with fillings for thousands of years。

tr.en: People had, of course, been eating bread with fillings for thousands of years.
tr.zh: 當然，人們吃夾著餡料的麵包已經有好幾千年了。

tr.en: What Montagu gave the world was not the food itself but its name.
tr.zh: 蒙塔古帶給世界的不是這種食物本身，而是它的名字。

tr.en: Either way, the convenient snack became fashionable among his friends, who asked for 'the same as Sandwich', and the name stuck.
tr.zh: 不管是哪一種說法，這種方便的點心在他的朋友之間流行起來，他們會點「跟三明治伯爵一樣的」，於是這個名字就傳了下來。

tz: 美國人在 11 月 3 日慶祝全國三明治日，這天是第四代三明治伯爵約翰・蒙塔古的生日，他 1718 年出生於英國。
當然，人們吃夾著餡料的麵包已經有好幾千年了。蒙塔古帶給世界的不是這種食物本身，而是它的名字。
根據一個流行的故事——最早是一位法國訪客在 1760 年代寫下的——伯爵沉迷於一場漫長的牌局，不肯離開牌桌，於是要人把牛肉夾在兩片吐司之間送來。
他的一位傳記作者則提出一個比較不那麼精彩的解釋：蒙塔古是一位勤奮的政治人物，掌管海軍，常常一邊工作一邊在書桌前吃飯。
不管是哪一種，這種方便的點心在他的朋友圈中流行起來，他們會點「跟三明治一樣的」，這個名字就這樣固定了下來。
今天這個點子已經傳遍各地，從越南的法國麵包（bánh mì）到台灣的刈包——證明一個好點子可以比以它命名的人活得更久。

ph.ex: Of course you can join us!
ph.exzh: 你當然可以加入我們！

ph.ex: Write down the new words in your notebook.
ph.exzh: 把新單字寫在你的筆記本上。

ph.ex: He was so absorbed in his book that he missed the bus.
ph.exzh: 他太專心看書，錯過了公車。

ph.ex: We can walk or take the bus — either way, we'll be on time.
ph.exzh: 我們可以走路或搭公車，不管哪一種都會準時到。

ph.zh: 這個名字就這樣固定下來了
ph.ex: His friends called him 'Rocket', and the name stuck.
ph.exzh: 朋友們叫他「火箭」，這個綽號就這樣叫開了。

c.title: How a Name Outlived a Man
text: Few aristocrats are remembered for their lunch. John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich, born on November 3, 1718, held senior political posts and oversaw Britain's navy, yet his lasting fame rests on a convenient arrangement of bread and meat.

It is worth stressing that he invented nothing edible. Bread wrapped around fillings is ancient; what changed in eighteenth-century London was that a fashionable circle gave the habit a fashionable label.

The traditional explanation, recorded by a French travel writer in the 1760s, casts the Earl as a gambler too engrossed in cards to sit down for a meal. His modern biographer, however, finds the story implausible for a man of his workload and suggests a more mundane origin: meals snatched at his desk.
The disagreement is instructive. Colourful anecdotes travel faster than dull truths, especially when they flatter our assumptions about idle aristocrats.

Meanwhile the word escaped its origins entirely. Today 'sandwich' names countless variations, from Vietnamese bánh mì to Taiwanese gua bao, and has even become a verb. A forgotten politician survives as an everyday noun — a reminder that language, not achievement, often decides who is remembered.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: The Earl invented the sandwich during a long all-night card game.
He is remembered through a word, and its origin story may be a myth.
The Earl's naval work was far more important than the sandwich.
Language always remembers the most important people in history.
q.why: 主旨：伯爵靠一個字被記住，起源故事可能只是迎合偏見的傳說。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “implausible” means ___.
opts: well proven
widely known
recently discovered
hard to believe
q.why: implausible = 難以置信。

q.q: Why does the writer call the disagreement “instructive”?
opts: Entertaining stories spread more easily than truths
It proves that the card-game story is true after all
It shows that biographers are always right in the end
It teaches readers the long history of bread
q.why: 第四段：Colourful anecdotes travel faster than dull truths。

q.q: What is the writer's tone?
opts: Angry and critical
Admiring and celebratory
Wry and thoughtful
Neutral and dry
q.why: 略帶冷嘲並引導思考。

q.q: What does the final sentence conclude?
opts: The Earl deserves much more credit for his naval work
Sandwiches will probably be given a new name soon
Achievement, more than language, decides who is remembered
Language, more than achievement, decides who is remembered
q.why: 結尾：language, not achievement, often decides who is remembered。

q.q: Which example best supports the writer's idea that “colourful anecdotes travel faster than dull truths”?
opts: A funny rumour spreads faster than the boring correction
A science report is read only by a handful of experts
A school textbook is updated every few years
A museum labels each of its objects carefully
q.why: 有趣的謠言比無聊的更正傳得快，正是作者的論點。

tz: 很少有貴族是因為他們的午餐而被記住的。1718 年 11 月 3 日出生的第四代三明治伯爵約翰・蒙塔古，曾擔任重要的政治職位、主管英國海軍，但他長久的名聲，卻建立在一種把麵包和肉組合起來的方便吃法上。
值得強調的是，他並沒有發明任何可以吃的東西。用麵包包住餡料的吃法很古老；十八世紀倫敦改變的，只是一群時髦的人替這個習慣貼上了一個時髦的標籤。
傳統的解釋由一位法國遊記作家在 1760 年代記錄下來，把伯爵描寫成一個太沉迷於牌局、不肯坐下來吃飯的賭徒。然而，他的現代傳記作者認為，以他的工作量來看，這個故事不太可信，並提出一個更平凡的起源：在書桌前匆匆解決的餐點。
這個分歧很有啟發性。多采多姿的軼事比平淡的事實傳得更快，特別是當它們符合我們對「遊手好閒的貴族」的既定印象時。
與此同時，這個字完全脫離了它的起源。今天，「三明治」這個名稱涵蓋了無數變化，從越南的法國麵包到台灣的刈包，甚至還變成了一個動詞。一位被遺忘的政治人物，以一個日常名詞的身分存活下來——提醒我們，決定誰被記住的，往往是語言，而不是成就。

ph.ex: Our plan rests on good weather.
ph.exzh: 我們的計畫取決於好天氣。

ph.ex: It is worth stressing that everyone can join.
ph.exzh: 值得強調的是，每個人都可以參加。

ph.ex: She was too tired to finish her homework.
ph.exzh: 她太累了，沒辦法寫完作業。
ph.m: too engrossed in cards to sit down

ph.ex: Rumours travel faster than the truth.
ph.exzh: 謠言傳得比真相還快。

ph.ex: The word has escaped its origins and is used everywhere.
ph.exzh: 這個字早已脫離它的起源，到處都在用。

ph.ex: The rain was a reminder that summer was over.
ph.exzh: 這場雨提醒我們夏天結束了。

discuss: Why do you think the more exciting story about the card game became more popular than the 'eating at his desk' story?
Describe your favourite kind of sandwich or 'bread with fillings' food in Taiwan.
If a food were named after you, what would it be and why?

topic: The Boy King's Tomb
zh: 少年法老圖坦卡門的寶藏
src: National Geographic · Smithsonian · The Guardian

a.title: Treasure Under the Sand
text: More than 3,000 years ago, a young king ruled Egypt. His name was Tutankhamun. He became king when he was only about nine years old.
He died young, at about 19. People put him in a tomb with many treasures.
Over time, sand covered the tomb, and people forgot about it.
On November 4, 1922, a British man named Howard Carter found a stone step in the sand. It led down to the tomb!
Inside, there were gold, jewels, chariots and a famous gold mask. There were more than 5,000 objects.
Many old tombs were robbed long ago. This one was almost full, so it taught us a lot about ancient Egypt.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The famous gold mask of a young king
Finding the tomb of a young Egyptian king
How a powerful Egyptian king ruled for many years
Why so many old tombs were robbed
q.why: 全文講圖坦卡門陵墓的發現；其他是細節。

q.q: How old was Tutankhamun when he became king?
opts: About nineteen
About three
About nine
About thirty
q.why: 第一段：about nine years old。十九歲是他過世的年紀。

q.q: What did Howard Carter find first?
opts: A stone step in the sand
The famous gold mask
A door full of treasure
The young king's chariot
q.why: 第四段：found a stone step in the sand。

q.q: In the text, a “tomb” is ___.
opts: a palace where the king lived with his family
a palace where a king lives
a deep hole dug in the sand
a place where a dead person is buried
q.why: tomb = 陵墓。

q.q: Why was this tomb so important?
opts: It was almost full, so it taught us a lot
It was the biggest tomb in all of Egypt
It belonged to Egypt's most powerful king
It was the oldest tomb ever found in Egypt
q.why: 最後一段：This one was almost full。

q.q: Imagine a museum wants to show how ancient Egyptians lived. Why would this tomb be especially useful?
opts: It is the largest building in all of Egypt
It has the newest objects from ancient times
It was very easy to find in the desert
It kept over 5,000 real objects together
q.why: 5,000 多件完整的文物能呈現古埃及生活。

gt.en: More than 3,000 years ago, a young king ruled Egypt.
gt.zh: 三千多年前，一位年輕的國王統治著埃及。

gt.en: People put him in a tomb with many treasures.
gt.zh: 人們把他和許多寶物一起放進一座陵墓裡。

gt.en: Over time, sand covered the tomb, and people forgot about it.
gt.zh: 隨著時間過去，沙子蓋住了陵墓，人們也忘了它。

gt.en: It led down to the tomb!
gt.zh: 它一路通往陵墓！

tz: 三千多年前，一位年輕的國王統治著埃及，他的名字叫圖坦卡門。他成為國王時只有大約九歲。
他很年輕就死了，大約 19 歲。人們把他和許多寶物一起放進一座墳墓裡。
隨著時間過去，沙子蓋住了這座墳墓，人們也就忘了它。
1922 年 11 月 4 日，一位名叫霍華德・卡特的英國人在沙子裡發現了一級石階。它一路往下通到墳墓！
墳墓裡有黃金、珠寶、戰車，還有一副有名的黃金面具，一共有五千多件物品。
很多古老的墳墓很久以前就被盜了。這一座幾乎是完整的，所以它讓我們學到很多關於古埃及的事。

ph.ex: More than 100 people came to the show.
ph.exzh: 有超過一百人來看表演。

ph.ex: Don't forget about the test tomorrow.
ph.exzh: 別忘了明天的考試。

ph.ex: The stairs lead down to the basement.
ph.exzh: 這段樓梯往下通到地下室。

b.title: Wonderful Things in the Valley of the Kings
text: On November 4, 1922, workers led by the British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered a stone step in Egypt's Valley of the Kings, the desert burial ground of ancient pharaohs near the Nile.
Carter had searched the valley for years, funded by the wealthy Lord Carnarvon, and the money was running out. The step led to a sealed doorway — and to the tomb of Tutankhamun.
Tutankhamun became pharaoh as a child, around 1332 BC, and died at about 19. He was not an especially important ruler, which may explain why his small tomb was soon forgotten and buried under rubble.

That obscurity protected it. While most royal tombs had been looted in ancient times, Tutankhamun's still held more than 5,000 objects, including furniture, chariots, weapons and a solid gold mask weighing about ten kilograms.
Carter's team spent around ten years carefully recording and removing everything.
When Lord Carnarvon died a few months after the opening, newspapers spread rumours of a 'pharaoh's curse'. Scientists point out that most people who entered the tomb lived long, ordinary lives.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Tutankhamun was a powerful king, so his tomb was naturally full of treasure.
Forgotten, the tomb survived almost untouched, revealing thousands of treasures.
Lord Carnarvon died a few months later because of a pharaoh's curse.
Forgotten for centuries, the tomb was robbed of almost all of its treasure long ago.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；第二項因果錯誤（他並不重要）；第三項是謠言。

q.q: Who paid for Carter's search?
opts: The Egyptian government
A British museum
Lord Carnarvon
Carter himself
q.why: 第二段：funded by the wealthy Lord Carnarvon。

q.q: About how much does the gold mask weigh?
opts: About ten kilograms
About one kilogram
About fifty kilograms
About one hundred kilograms
q.why: 第四段：about ten kilograms。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “looted” means ___.
opts: carefully studied by experts
covered over with sand
moved into a museum
robbed of valuable things
q.why: looted = 被洗劫。

q.q: What does the writer think about the 'pharaoh's curse'?
opts: It was a newspaper rumour not backed by facts
It is partly true, because Carnarvon died
Scientists are still unsure whether it is real
It is the reason the tomb was forgotten
q.why: 最後一段：most people who entered the tomb lived long, ordinary lives。

q.q: A video claims: “Everyone who entered the tomb died young because of the curse.” Which fact from the text best challenges this claim?
opts: Carnarvon died just a few months after the opening
The tomb was full of gold and precious objects
Carter searched for the tomb for about ten years
Most who entered the tomb lived long, ordinary lives
q.why: 大多數進入陵墓的人都活得很長，直接反駁這個說法。

tr.en: Carter had searched the valley for years, funded by the wealthy Lord Carnarvon, and the money was running out.
tr.zh: 卡特在富有的卡那封勳爵資助下，已經在山谷裡找了好幾年，而經費快要用完了。

tr.en: Tutankhamun became pharaoh as a child, around 1332 BC, and died at about 19.
tr.zh: 圖坦卡門在大約西元前 1332 年還是個孩子時就成了法老，大約十九歲就過世了。

tr.en: When Lord Carnarvon died a few months after the opening, newspapers spread rumours of a 'pharaoh's curse'.
tr.zh: 陵墓開啟幾個月後卡那封勳爵過世，報紙就散播起「法老的詛咒」的謠言。

tz: 1922 年 11 月 4 日，由英國考古學家霍華德・卡特帶領的工人，在埃及的帝王谷——尼羅河附近古代法老的沙漠墓地——挖出了一級石階。
卡特在山谷裡尋找了好幾年，經費由富有的卡納馮勳爵資助，而錢快要用完了。這級石階通往一道封住的門口——也就是圖坦卡門的墳墓。
圖坦卡門大約在西元前 1332 年還是個孩子時就成為法老，大約 19 歲就過世了。他並不是特別重要的統治者，這或許說明了為什麼他的小墳墓很快就被遺忘，埋在瓦礫底下。
正是這份默默無聞保護了它。大多數王室墳墓在古代就已遭到洗劫，但圖坦卡門的墳墓裡仍有五千多件物品，包括家具、戰車、武器，還有一副重約十公斤的純金面具。
卡特的團隊花了大約十年，仔細地記錄並搬出所有的東西。
卡納馮勳爵在開墓後幾個月過世時，報紙散播了「法老的詛咒」的謠言。科學家指出，大多數進過墳墓的人，都過著長壽而平凡的生活。

ph.ex: We ran out of milk this morning.
ph.exzh: 我們今天早上牛奶喝完了。

ph.ex: He slept late, which may explain why he was tired.
ph.exzh: 他很晚才睡，這或許說明了他為什麼很累。

ph.ex: In ancient times, people used shells as money.
ph.exzh: 在古代，人們用貝殼當錢。

ph.ex: The baby weighs about four kilos.
ph.exzh: 這個嬰兒重約四公斤。

ph.ex: My teacher pointed out my spelling mistakes.
ph.exzh: 老師指出了我的拼字錯誤。

c.title: The Advantage of Being Forgotten
text: History usually rewards the powerful with remembrance. Tutankhamun's posthumous fame is a rare exception: he became the most famous pharaoh of all precisely because his own civilisation forgot him.

Crowned as a child around 1332 BC and dead by about nineteen, he ruled during an unsettled period and left little political mark. His modest tomb in the Valley of the Kings was soon buried under debris from later construction, slipping from memory while grander tombs nearby were systematically plundered.

On November 4, 1922, after years of fruitless digging financed by Lord Carnarvon, Howard Carter's workmen exposed a step cut into the rock. Behind the sealed doors lay a near-intact royal burial: more than 5,000 objects, from gilded shrines and chariots to the gold mask that has become a global emblem of ancient Egypt.

The discovery also produced a modern myth. Carnarvon's death months later, from an infected mosquito bite, fed press stories of a vengeful curse — a tale that sold newspapers far better than painstaking archaeology ever could.
Perhaps the deeper lesson concerns what survives. The objects that tell us most about the past are often those that escaped attention, not those that commanded it.
gloss: 費盡心力的；一絲不苟的

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: He became famous because his tomb was forgotten and survived.
Tutankhamun is famous today because he was a truly great ruler.
The newspaper story of the curse is what made him famous.
Carter was simply the most important archaeologist in history.
q.why: 主旨：被遺忘反而讓陵墓完整保存，他也因此成名。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “posthumous” fame is fame that comes ___.
opts: during a person's childhood
after a person's death
because of great wealth
from political power
q.why: posthumous = 死後的。

q.q: Why does the writer say the curse story “sold newspapers far better than painstaking archaeology”?
opts: Archaeologists refused to speak to newspapers
The curse had been proven true by scientists
Readers prefer drama to slow, careful science
Newspapers had paid for the whole excavation
q.why: 聳動的詛咒故事比嚴謹考古更吸引讀者。

q.q: What is the writer's attitude to the 'curse'?
opts: Fearful
Neutral and undecided
Amused but convinced
Sceptical
q.why: 稱其為 modern myth 並指出真正死因。

q.q: How does the essay's ending relate to its opening?
opts: It directly contradicts the argument of the opening
It repeats the full list of treasures from the tomb
It shows that the curse was the real reason for his fame
It widens the paradox into a lesson about what survives
q.why: 開頭的悖論在結尾延伸為普遍啟示。

q.q: According to the writer's final idea, which kind of object is MOST likely to teach future historians about everyday life today?
opts: Famous paintings hanging in the biggest museums
Statues of presidents standing in city squares
Ordinary things kept without thought, like old receipts
Gold treasures made specially to be buried with leaders
q.why: 結尾：最能告訴我們過去的，常是沒被注意的東西。

tz: 歷史通常會用「被記住」來獎賞有權勢的人。圖坦卡門死後的名聲卻是一個罕見的例外：他之所以成為最有名的法老，正是因為他自己的文明遺忘了他。
他大約在西元前 1332 年還是個孩子時加冕，大約十九歲就過世；他統治的時期動盪不安，在政治上沒留下什麼痕跡。他位於帝王谷的樸素墳墓，很快就被後來工程的廢土掩埋，從人們的記憶中消失，而附近更宏偉的墳墓則被有系統地洗劫一空。
1922 年 11 月 4 日，在卡納馮勳爵資助、多年一無所獲的挖掘之後，霍華德・卡特的工人挖出了一級鑿在岩石裡的台階。封住的門後是一座幾乎完整的王室墓葬：五千多件物品，從鍍金的神龕和戰車，到那副已成為古埃及全球象徵的黃金面具。
這項發現也製造了一個現代神話。卡納馮幾個月後因蚊子叮咬感染而死，助長了報紙上關於「復仇詛咒」的報導——這種故事比費心費力的考古工作好賣得多。
也許更深一層的啟示，與「什麼會留存下來」有關。最能告訴我們過去的物品，往往是那些逃過注意的東西，而不是那些吸引了所有目光的東西。

ph.ex: Sunny days in winter here are a rare exception.
ph.exzh: 這裡冬天的晴天是罕見的例外。

ph.ex: She succeeded precisely because she never gave up.
ph.exzh: 她成功，正是因為她從不放棄。

ph.ex: His name has slipped from my memory.
ph.exzh: 我想不起他的名字了。

ph.ex: Her absence fed stories that she had left the team.
ph.exzh: 她的缺席助長了她已經離隊的說法。

ph.ex: The new phone works far better than the old one.
ph.exzh: 新手機比舊的好用得多。

ph.ex: Small acts of kindness often escape attention.
ph.exzh: 小小的善舉常常沒有被注意到。

discuss: Tutankhamun became famous because his tomb was forgotten. Why do you think forgotten things can sometimes survive better?
Should treasures from ancient tombs stay in their home country or be shown in museums around the world? Why?
Why do stories like the 'pharaoh's curse' spread so easily?

topic: World Tsunami Awareness Day
zh: 世界海嘯意識日：大浪來之前要知道的事
src: UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction · Taipei Times · NBC

a.title: Run to High Ground!
text: November 5 is World Tsunami Awareness Day. A tsunami is a group of very big, strong waves.
Most tsunamis happen after a big earthquake under the sea. The water moves, and huge waves rush to the coast.
There are warning signs. The ground may shake hard. Sometimes the sea goes far away from the beach very quickly.
If you see these signs near the sea, do not stay to look. Run to high ground right away!
The day comes from an old story in Japan. A man burned his rice to call villagers up a hill, and they were saved from a tsunami.
Taiwan is next to the sea, so it is important for everyone to know what to do.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: What a tsunami is and how to stay safe
An old Japanese story about burning rice
Why Taiwan is next to the sea
How earthquakes happen under the sea
q.why: 全文介紹海嘯與自保方法。

q.q: What usually causes a tsunami?
opts: Very strong winds during a storm
Heavy rain falling for many days
The pull of a bright full moon
A big earthquake under the sea
q.why: 第二段：after a big earthquake under the sea。

q.q: What should you do if you see the warning signs?
opts: Go to the beach to look at the sea
Run to high ground right away
Wait for an official alarm first
Stay inside a house near the beach
q.why: 第四段：Run to high ground right away!

q.q: In the text, the “coast” is ___.
opts: the bottom of the deep sea
a high hill far from the sea
the land next to the sea
a very big wave in the ocean
q.why: coast = 海岸。

q.q: Why did the man in Japan burn his rice?
opts: To stop the fire from spreading to the other houses
To get villagers up the hill, away from the wave
Because the rice was wet from the waves
To cook a big meal for all the villagers
q.why: 第五段：燒稻引村民上山。

q.q: You are at the beach and suddenly the sea goes far away from the sand. What should you do?
opts: Run to high ground immediately
Walk out to collect the shells
Take a video of the empty sea
Wait to see what happens next
q.why: 海水急退是警訊，應立刻往高處跑。

gt.en: November 5 is World Tsunami Awareness Day.
gt.zh: 十一月五日是世界海嘯意識日。

gt.en: Most tsunamis happen after a big earthquake under the sea.
gt.zh: 大部分的海嘯都發生在海底大地震之後。

gt.en: If you see these signs near the sea, do not stay to look.
gt.zh: 如果你在海邊看到這些徵兆，不要留下來看。

gt.en: A man burned his rice to call villagers up a hill, and they were saved from a tsunami.
gt.zh: 一個男人燒掉自己的稻子，把村民召到山丘上，他們因此逃過了海嘯。

tz: 11 月 5 日是世界海嘯意識日。海嘯是一群非常巨大、強力的海浪。
大部分的海嘯發生在海底大地震之後。海水被推動，巨浪就衝向海岸。
海嘯有警訊。地面可能會劇烈搖晃，有時候海水會很快地從海灘退得很遠。
如果你在海邊看到這些警訊，不要留下來看。立刻跑到高的地方去！
這個日子來自日本一個古老的故事。一個男人燒掉了自己的稻子，把村民叫到山丘上，他們因此逃過了海嘯。
台灣四面環海，所以每個人都知道該怎麼做是很重要的。

ph.ex: The children rushed to the door when the bell rang.
ph.exzh: 鐘一響，孩子們就衝向門口。

ph.ex: Don't go far away from the group on the trip.
ph.exzh: 校外教學時不要離隊伍太遠。

ph.ex: Call me right away if you need help.
ph.exzh: 需要幫忙的話立刻打給我。

ph.ex: My school is next to a park.
ph.exzh: 我的學校在一座公園旁邊。

b.title: Knowing the Signs Saves Lives
text: Every November 5, the United Nations marks World Tsunami Awareness Day. It was created in 2015 to help people around the world understand one of nature's most destructive hazards.

Tsunamis are usually triggered by powerful undersea earthquakes, which suddenly lift or drop huge areas of the sea floor. The waves can cross an ocean at the speed of a jet plane and grow much taller as they reach shallow water.
History shows how deadly they can be. The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami killed around 230,000 people in more than a dozen countries, and in 2011 a tsunami devastated Japan's northeast coast.

Yet many deaths can be prevented. Natural warnings include strong or long shaking, a loud roar from the ocean, and the sea suddenly pulling back from the shore. Anyone who notices them should head inland or uphill immediately, without waiting for an official alarm.
The date honours a Japanese story from 1854, in which a villager set fire to his harvested rice to lead people to safety.
Taiwan, surrounded by sea and sitting on active fault lines, runs warning systems and drills — but personal knowledge is still the fastest alarm.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Tsunamis are deadly, but knowing the signs and acting fast saves lives.
The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami killed around 230,000 people in total.
Tsunami waves can cross an ocean almost as fast as a jet plane.
Official warning systems now make personal knowledge unnecessary.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；第四項與文意相反。

q.q: How fast can tsunami waves cross an ocean?
opts: As fast as a car on a highway
As fast as a jet plane
As slowly as a ship
As fast as sound
q.why: 第二段：at the speed of a jet plane。

q.q: Which is NOT listed as a natural warning sign?
opts: Strong or long shaking
A loud roar from the ocean
Dark clouds and heavy rain
The sea suddenly pulling back
q.why: 第四段列出搖晃、轟鳴、海水急退；沒有提到烏雲大雨。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “inland” means ___.
opts: along the beach, close to the water
into the water, away from the dry land
into a tall building by the sea
away from the coast, towards the middle
q.why: inland = 往內陸。

q.q: Why does the writer say personal knowledge is “the fastest alarm”?
opts: People can act on the signs before official warnings
Official alarms do not exist in most coastal places
Phones always stop working during big earthquakes
Personal knowledge is more accurate than science
q.why: 看到徵兆就能立刻行動，不必等官方警報。

q.q: Your school is planning a tsunami drill. Which plan matches the text's advice best?
opts: Practise waiting in class for an official message
Practise walking to the beach to check the water
Practise moving uphill or inland once shaking stops
Practise only on paper, without moving at all
q.why: 文章強調強烈搖晃後立刻往高處或內陸。

tr.en: It was created in 2015 to help people around the world understand one of nature's most destructive hazards.
tr.zh: 它在 2015 年設立，目的是幫助世界各地的人了解大自然最具破壞力的災害之一。

tr.en: Tsunamis are usually triggered by powerful undersea earthquakes, which suddenly lift or drop huge areas of the sea floor.
tr.zh: 海嘯通常是由強烈的海底地震引發的，這種地震會突然抬升或下沉大片的海床。

tr.en: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami killed around 230,000 people in more than a dozen countries, and in 2011 a tsunami devastated Japan's northeast coast.
tr.zh: 2004 年的印度洋海嘯在十幾個國家奪走了大約二十三萬人的性命，而 2011 年的一場海嘯則重創了日本的東北海岸。

tz: 每年 11 月 5 日，聯合國都會舉行世界海嘯意識日。它在 2015 年設立，目的是幫助全世界的人了解這種大自然最具破壞力的災害之一。
海嘯通常是由強烈的海底地震引起，地震會讓大片海床突然上升或下降。海浪可以用噴射機的速度橫越大洋，到了淺水區又會變得高得多。
歷史顯示海嘯可以多麼致命。2004 年的印度洋海嘯在十多個國家造成約二十三萬人死亡；2011 年，海嘯重創了日本東北海岸。
然而，許多死亡是可以避免的。大自然的警訊包括強烈或長時間的搖晃、海洋傳來的巨大轟隆聲，以及海水突然從岸邊退去。任何人發現這些警訊，都應該立刻往內陸或高處移動，不要等官方的警報。
這個日期是為了紀念日本一個 1854 年的故事：一位村民放火燒了自己收割好的稻子，帶領人們前往安全的地方。
台灣四面環海，又位在活躍的斷層帶上，設有警報系統，也會舉行演練——但個人的知識仍然是最快的警報。

ph.ex: The fire was triggered by a small spark.
ph.exzh: 這場火是由一個小火花引起的。

ph.ex: The crowd pulled back from the fire.
ph.exzh: 人群從火邊退開。

ph.ex: He left without waiting for an answer.
ph.exzh: 他沒等回答就離開了。

ph.ex: The teacher led the students to safety.
ph.exzh: 老師帶領學生到安全的地方。

ph.ex: Taiwan is surrounded by the sea.
ph.exzh: 台灣四面環海。

c.title: The Ten Minutes That Matter
text: Tsunamis compress catastrophe into a cruelly short window. When a large undersea earthquake abruptly displaces the sea floor, waves can race across an ocean at jet-like speeds, then rear up as they meet shallow coastal water. Communities nearest the epicentre may have only minutes.

World Tsunami Awareness Day, adopted by the United Nations in 2015 and marked on November 5, exists because those minutes are where lives are won or lost. The 2004 Indian Ocean disaster, which killed roughly 230,000 people, exposed how few coastal residents recognised the danger signs or had anywhere planned to go.

The date commemorates the Japanese legend of 'Inamura-no-hi', in which, after an 1854 earthquake, a villager set his own harvested rice sheaves alight to draw neighbours uphill before the sea struck. The story endures because its logic is timeless: act decisively on the evidence in front of you, even at personal cost.

Modern warning networks, Taiwan's included, have improved dramatically, yet they cannot entirely replace instinct. Strong shaking, a sudden retreat of the sea or an unfamiliar roar should trigger evacuation on their own.
Preparedness, in the end, is less a technology than a habit — one that must be learned long before the water arrives.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Modern warning networks have now largely solved the tsunami problem.
Tsunamis are so rare that serious preparation is not really necessary.
Survival depends on recognising signs and acting at once — a learned habit.
Survival depends mainly on modern warning sirens, which make drills unnecessary now.
q.why: 主旨：預警時間極短，存活靠事先養成的習慣。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “evacuation” means ___.
opts: moving people away from danger
warning people over the radio
measuring the size of the waves
rebuilding after a disaster
q.why: evacuation = 撤離。

q.q: Why does the writer say the Inamura-no-hi story's logic is “timeless”?
opts: Rice has always been very valuable in Japan
Burning a rice field is the best way to warn people of anything
Japan still burns rice fields as a warning
Acting fast on evidence, even at a cost, is always right
q.why: 第三段：act decisively on the evidence … even at personal cost。

q.q: What is the writer's tone?
opts: Calm and relaxed
Urgent but practical
Hopeless and gloomy
Angry at governments
q.why: 強調分秒必爭，又給具體做法。

q.q: What is the function of the last sentence?
opts: To introduce a different kind of natural disaster
To sum up that preparedness is a learned habit
To praise modern warning networks and sirens
To describe the risks along Taiwan's coast
q.why: 結尾收束：防災是習慣。

q.q: A town says: “We bought an excellent warning siren, so we don't need drills.” How would the writer respond?
opts: Sirens help, but people must practise acting at once
Agree — an excellent siren is all a town really needs
Agree — drills only frighten people unnecessarily
Disagree — warning sirens never work in a real disaster
q.why: 作者認為警報網路無法完全取代直覺與習慣。

tz: 海嘯把災難壓縮在一段殘酷的短暫時間裡。當一場大型海底地震突然讓海床位移，海浪能以近乎噴射機的速度橫越大洋，碰到淺淺的沿岸海水時再高高掀起。離震央最近的社區，可能只有幾分鐘的時間。
聯合國在 2015 年通過、於 11 月 5 日舉行的世界海嘯意識日，之所以存在，就是因為生命正是在那幾分鐘之內被保住或失去的。造成約二十三萬人死亡的 2004 年印度洋災難，暴露出有多少沿海居民認不出危險的警訊，或根本沒有計畫好要往哪裡逃。
這個日期紀念日本「稻むらの火」的傳說：1854 年一場地震後，一位村民點燃了自己收割好的稻束，把鄰居們引上山丘，趕在海水來襲之前。這個故事流傳至今，因為它的道理永不過時：根據眼前的證據果斷行動，即使要付出個人的代價。
現代的警報網——包括台灣的——已經大幅進步，但它們無法完全取代直覺。強烈的搖晃、海水突然退去，或一陣陌生的轟隆聲，本身就應該讓人立刻撤離。
說到底，防災準備與其說是一項技術，不如說是一種習慣——一種必須在海水到來之前很久就學會的習慣。

ph.ex: The horse reared up when it heard the noise.
ph.exzh: 馬聽到聲音就高高揚起前腳。

ph.ex: The game was won or lost in the last minute.
ph.exzh: 比賽的勝負就在最後一分鐘。

ph.ex: Judge people on the evidence, not on rumours.
ph.exzh: 要根據證據判斷別人，而不是謠言。

ph.ex: She told the truth, even at personal cost.
ph.exzh: 即使要付出個人代價，她還是說了實話。

ph.ex: These signs should be enough on their own.
ph.exzh: 這些跡象本身就應該足夠了。

ph.ex: In the end, practice matters most.
ph.exzh: 說到底，練習最重要。

ph.ex: Start packing long before the trip.
ph.exzh: 早在旅行前很久就開始打包。

discuss: What would you do if you were at the beach and felt a strong earthquake?
The man in the story burned his own rice to save others. What does this tell us about him?
How does your school or town prepare for earthquakes or other disasters? What could be better?

topic: The Monkey King
zh: 齊天大聖孫悟空
src: Journey to the West · BBC · The Guardian

a.title: The Monkey Born from a Stone
text: A long time ago, in a Chinese story, a monkey was born from a magic stone. His name was Sun Wukong, the Monkey King.
He was very clever and very strong. He learned 72 ways to change his shape, and he could jump onto a cloud and fly far away.
He had a magic stick. It could become as small as a needle or as big as a tree.
But the Monkey King was proud and naughty. He made a lot of trouble in Heaven, so the Buddha trapped him under a mountain.
Five hundred years later, a kind monk freed him. The Monkey King promised to protect the monk on a long trip to the West.
Today, children all over the world know the Monkey King from books, cartoons and games.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The Monkey King from a Chinese story
How the Buddha trapped a clever monkey
A monk's long and difficult trip to the West
Monkeys that can fly on clouds in the sky
q.why: 全文介紹孫悟空；其他是故事片段。

q.q: Where was the Monkey King born?
opts: On a white cloud
From a magic stone
Under a mountain
High in Heaven
q.why: 第一段：born from a magic stone。

q.q: Why was he trapped under a mountain?
opts: He refused to protect the travelling monk
He lost the magic stick he always carried
He grew too strong for anyone to control
He made a lot of trouble in Heaven
q.why: 第四段：He made a lot of trouble in Heaven。

q.q: In the text, “proud” means ___.
opts: feeling sad and lonely after a mistake
being very clever with tricks
thinking you are better than others
feeling sorry for what you did
q.why: proud 在此帶有自大的意思。

q.q: How did the Monkey King change after he was freed?
opts: He became much weaker than he was before
He promised to protect the monk instead
He stopped using his magic completely
He went straight back up to Heaven
q.why: 第五段：promised to protect the monk。

q.q: A very talented classmate often causes trouble. What does the Monkey King's story suggest could help?
opts: Telling him to stop using his talent completely
Ignoring him and his trouble for the whole year
Making him leave the class and study alone
Giving him an important job where his talent helps
q.why: 悟空的才能被引導去保護唐僧——讓才能用在幫助別人。

gt.en: A long time ago, in a Chinese story, a monkey was born from a magic stone.
gt.zh: 很久以前，在一個中國故事裡，一隻猴子從一顆神奇的石頭裡誕生了。

gt.en: He was very clever and very strong.
gt.zh: 他非常聰明，也非常強壯。

gt.en: He had a magic stick.
gt.zh: 他有一根神奇的棍子。

gt.en: But the Monkey King was proud and naughty.
gt.zh: 但是美猴王既驕傲又頑皮。

tz: 很久以前，在一個中國故事裡，一隻猴子從一顆神奇的石頭裡蹦了出來。牠的名字叫孫悟空，也就是美猴王。
牠非常聰明，也非常強壯。牠學會了七十二種變化，還能跳上一朵雲飛到很遠的地方。
牠有一根神奇的棒子，能變得像針一樣小，也能變得像樹一樣大。
但是美猴王很驕傲，又很調皮。牠在天宮大鬧一場，所以佛祖把牠壓在一座山下。
五百年後，一位善良的和尚把牠救了出來。美猴王答應在前往西方的漫長旅程中保護這位和尚。
今天，全世界的孩子都從書本、卡通和遊戲裡認識了美猴王。

ph.ex: In the story, the girl was born from a peach.
ph.exzh: 故事裡，那個女孩是從桃子裡誕生的。

ph.ex: The cat jumped onto the table.
ph.exzh: 貓跳上了桌子。

ph.ex: Don't make trouble in class.
ph.exzh: 上課不要惹麻煩。

ph.ex: We sang songs on a long trip to Kaohsiung.
ph.exzh: 我們去高雄的長途旅行中一路唱歌。

b.title: From Troublemaker to Protector
text: Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, is the star of Journey to the West, a sixteenth-century Chinese novel usually credited to Wu Cheng'en. It remains one of the most beloved stories in Asia.

Born from a stone on a mountaintop, Wukong becomes king of the monkeys and then sets out to find the secret of eternal life. He masters 72 transformations, can travel 108,000 li in a single somersault, and wields a staff that can shrink to the size of a needle.
Power goes to his head. He declares himself 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven', steals heavenly peaches and fights off entire armies of gods, until the Buddha traps him under a mountain.

Five centuries later, the monk Tang Sanzang releases him on condition that he guards the monk on a dangerous pilgrimage to India to collect Buddhist scriptures. A golden band around Wukong's head tightens whenever he disobeys.
Along with Pigsy and Sandy, he battles demons through eighty-one trials.
The story still inspires films, comics and video games, including the hit game Black Myth: Wukong.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The Monkey King can change himself into 72 different shapes and forms.
Journey to the West was written by Wu Cheng'en in the sixteenth century.
The video game Black Myth: Wukong has brought him to new audiences.
The rebellious Monkey King is punished, then becomes a pilgrim's protector.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: What title did Wukong give himself?
opts: Great Sage Equal to Heaven
King of the Monkeys
Protector of the Monk
Master of 72 Transformations
q.why: 第三段：'Great Sage Equal to Heaven'。

q.q: What happens when Wukong disobeys?
opts: His staff shrinks to the size of a needle
He is sent back under the mountain
The golden band around his head tightens
He loses one of his transformations
q.why: 第四段：A golden band … tightens whenever he disobeys。

q.q: In paragraph 4, a “pilgrimage” is ___.
opts: a battle against demons
a journey to a holy place
a punishment from the gods
a royal ceremony
q.why: pilgrimage = 朝聖之旅。

q.q: What does “Power goes to his head” mean?
opts: Great power makes him proud and reckless
He grows wiser as he grows stronger
His head is where all his power comes from
He uses his power only to protect others
q.why: 有了權力就驕傲自大。

q.q: Which modern situation is most like the golden band on Wukong's head?
opts: A prize given to the best student at the end of the year
A long holiday given after a difficult journey
A rule with a clear consequence that keeps someone on track
A special gift from a close friend on your birthday
q.why: 金箍是有後果的約束，幫助有能力但衝動的人守規矩。

tr.en: Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, is the star of Journey to the West, a sixteenth-century Chinese novel usually credited to Wu Cheng'en.
tr.zh: 美猴王孫悟空是《西遊記》的主角，這是一部十六世紀的中國小說，一般認為作者是吳承恩。

tr.en: Born from a stone on a mountaintop, Wukong becomes king of the monkeys and then sets out to find the secret of eternal life.
tr.zh: 悟空從山頂上的一塊石頭裡誕生，成為猴王，接著出發去尋找長生不老的秘密。

tr.en: A golden band around Wukong's head tightens whenever he disobeys.
tr.zh: 每當悟空不聽話，他頭上的金箍就會收緊。

tz: 美猴王孫悟空是《西遊記》的主角；這部十六世紀的中國小說通常被認為是吳承恩所寫，至今仍是亞洲最受喜愛的故事之一。
悟空從山頂的一塊石頭中誕生，成為猴王後，出發去尋找長生不老的祕密。他學會了七十二變，一個筋斗就能翻十萬八千里，手上還有一根可以縮到針那麼小的棒子。
權力沖昏了他的頭。他自封「齊天大聖」，偷吃天上的蟠桃，打退一整支天兵天將，直到佛祖把他壓在一座山下。
五百年後，唐三藏把他放了出來，條件是他要保護這位和尚，踏上前往印度取佛經的危險旅程。悟空頭上的金箍，每當他不聽話時就會收緊。
他和豬八戒、沙悟淨一起，經歷九九八十一難，和妖魔作戰。
這個故事至今仍啟發著電影、漫畫和電玩，包括熱門遊戲《黑神話：悟空》。

ph.ex: The song is credited to a famous singer.
ph.exzh: 這首歌被認為是一位知名歌手的作品。

ph.ex: He set out to find his lost dog.
ph.exzh: 他出發去找走失的狗。

ph.ex: Don't let your success go to your head.
ph.exzh: 別讓成功沖昏了你的頭。

ph.ex: You can borrow it on condition that you return it tomorrow.
ph.exzh: 你可以借，條件是明天還回來。

ph.ex: Along with my sister, I cleaned the house.
ph.exzh: 我和姐姐一起打掃了房子。

c.title: Why We Love a Rebel Who Learns
text: Few literary characters have proved as durable as Sun Wukong. The Monkey King of Journey to the West, the sixteenth-century Ming novel traditionally attributed to Wu Cheng'en, has leapt from woodblock prints to opera stages, cartoons and blockbuster video games.

His appeal begins with his outrageous abilities: born from stone, he commands 72 transformations, crosses impossible distances in a single cloud somersault and wields a staff that expands or shrinks at will. Yet the novel is less interested in power than in what power does to character.

Intoxicated by his talents, Wukong proclaims himself 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven' and turns the celestial court upside down, until the Buddha pins him beneath a mountain for five hundred years. Freed to escort the monk Tang Sanzang to India in search of scriptures, he is fitted with a golden headband that tightens when he strays — a vivid image of discipline imposed from outside.
Over eighty-one ordeals, the trickster gradually becomes a loyal guardian, his brilliance redirected rather than extinguished.
That arc may explain his staying power. Wukong flatters our rebellious instincts while reassuring us that cleverness, properly harnessed, can serve something larger than oneself.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Wukong is popular today mainly because of his spectacular magic powers.
Wukong endures as a brilliant rebel who learns to serve a larger purpose.
Wukong's story shows that rebels must give up their talents to be good.
Journey to the West is mainly a story about the monk, not the monkey.
q.why: 主旨：天才叛逆者學會把才能用在更大的目標。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “ordeals” are ___.
opts: happy celebrations after a long trip
long speeches to the gods
religious books and scrolls
difficult and painful experiences
q.why: ordeals = 磨難。

q.q: What does the writer mean by brilliance “redirected rather than extinguished”?
opts: He keeps his cleverness but uses it for good
He loses his cleverness once he becomes a guardian
His brilliance is controlled only by the golden band
He becomes more mischievous as the journey goes on
q.why: 聰明沒有被消滅，而是被導向正途。

q.q: How does the writer regard Wukong?
opts: With amusement, but no real interest in him
With amusement, and nothing more
With admiration and thoughtful analysis
With complete neutrality throughout
q.why: 作者欣賞角色並深入分析。

q.q: How is the essay organised?
opts: His abilities → his many battles → the ending
Popularity → powers → fall → change → why it appeals
A comparison of the novel and the video game
A plot summary of the whole novel, and nothing more
q.why: 結構如選項所示。

q.q: Which statement would the writer MOST likely agree with?
opts: Clever people should never break any rules at all
Discipline always destroys a person's creativity
Clever rebels should lose their talents before they can be good
Cleverness is valuable when guided toward a larger goal
q.why: 結尾：cleverness, properly harnessed, can serve something larger than oneself。

tz: 很少有文學角色像孫悟空一樣經久不衰。這位出自《西遊記》——一部傳統上認為由吳承恩所寫的十六世紀明代小說——的美猴王，從木刻版畫一路跳上戲曲舞台、卡通和賣座電玩。
他的魅力始於他那些誇張的本領：從石頭中誕生，掌握七十二變，一個騰雲的筋斗就能跨越不可思議的距離，還揮舞著一根能隨意變大縮小的棒子。然而，這部小說感興趣的與其說是力量本身，不如說是力量對一個人品格的影響。
陶醉於自己才能的悟空，自封「齊天大聖」，把天庭攪得天翻地覆，直到佛祖把他壓在山下五百年。他被放出來護送唐三藏前往印度取經時，頭上被戴上一個金箍，只要他偏離正道就會收緊——這是一個「由外而來的紀律」的生動意象。
經過八十一次磨難，這個搗蛋鬼漸漸成為一名忠誠的守護者；他的聰明才智被重新導向，而不是被撲滅。
這段轉變也許正是他歷久不衰的原因。悟空滿足了我們內心叛逆的本能，同時也讓我們安心：只要好好駕馭，聰明才智能為比自己更遠大的目標服務。

ph.ex: These old shoes have proved durable.
ph.exzh: 這雙舊鞋證明很耐穿。

ph.ex: The cat comes and goes at will.
ph.exzh: 這隻貓隨意進出。

ph.ex: The test is less about memory than about thinking.
ph.exzh: 這個考試與其說是考記憶，不如說是考思考。
ph.m: less interested in power than in

ph.ex: The puppy turned the living room upside down.
ph.exzh: 小狗把客廳弄得天翻地覆。
ph.m: turns the celestial court upside down

ph.ex: They travelled north in search of work.
ph.exzh: 他們往北走去找工作。

ph.ex: He chose to help rather than complain.
ph.exzh: 他選擇幫忙，而不是抱怨。

discuss: The Monkey King is very powerful but also proud. Is it good or bad to be very confident? Explain.
The golden headband tightens when Wukong disobeys. What 'headbands' (rules or limits) help people behave well in real life?
Why do you think the Monkey King is still popular in games and films today?

topic: Marie Curie: A Life in the Glow
zh: 居禮夫人：兩度諾貝爾獎的科學家
src: Nobel Prize Outreach · Science · The New York Times

a.title: The Scientist Who Won Two Nobel Prizes
text: Marie Curie was born on November 7, 1867, in Warsaw, Poland. She loved to read and study.
At that time, many universities did not let women study. So Marie moved to Paris, France, to go to university.
There she met Pierre Curie, another scientist. They worked together and found two new elements, polonium and radium.
In 1903, she won a Nobel Prize. She was the first woman to win one. In 1911, she won a second Nobel Prize.
During a war, she helped doctors use X-ray machines to find broken bones and save soldiers.
Marie Curie showed the world that girls and women can be great scientists.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How X-ray machines helped soldiers
Why women could not study in Poland
How polonium and radium were found
The life and work of Marie Curie
q.why: 全文介紹居禮夫人的一生；其他是細節。

q.q: Why did Marie move to Paris?
opts: Many universities did not let women study
She wanted to work alongside Pierre Curie
She was looking for a job as a teacher
Her whole family moved there from Poland
q.why: 第二段：many universities did not let women study。

q.q: What did Marie and Pierre find?
opts: The first X-ray machine for hospitals
A new cure for broken bones and cuts
Two new elements, polonium and radium
A new kind of university for women
q.why: 第三段：two new elements, polonium and radium。

q.q: In the text, a “scientist” is a person who ___.
opts: teaches students at a university
studies how the natural world works
helps doctors care for people in hospitals
writes books about history and the past
q.why: scientist = 科學家。

q.q: What does the last sentence want readers to understand?
opts: Only women can win two Nobel Prizes
Women can be great scientists too
Science is easier for women
Marie Curie was the only female scientist
q.why: 最後一段：girls and women can be great scientists。

q.q: A girl says, “Science isn't for girls.” Which fact from the text would best change her mind?
opts: Pierre Curie was also a scientist
Paris has many universities
Marie Curie won two Nobel Prizes
X-ray machines help find broken bones
q.why: 居禮夫人兩度獲得諾貝爾獎，最能證明女性也能成為傑出科學家。

gt.en: At that time, many universities did not let women study.
gt.zh: 在那個時候，許多大學不讓女性就讀。

gt.en: There she met Pierre Curie, another scientist.
gt.zh: 她在那裡遇見了另一位科學家皮耶・居禮。

gt.en: In 1903, she won a Nobel Prize.
gt.zh: 1903 年，她獲得了諾貝爾獎。

gt.en: During a war, she helped doctors use X-ray machines to find broken bones and save soldiers.
gt.zh: 在一場戰爭期間，她幫助醫生使用 X 光機找出骨折的地方，拯救士兵。

tz: 瑪麗・居禮 1867 年 11 月 7 日出生於波蘭的華沙。她很喜歡閱讀和讀書。
在那個時候，許多大學不讓女性就讀。所以瑪麗搬到法國巴黎去上大學。
她在那裡認識了另一位科學家皮耶・居禮。他們一起研究，發現了兩種新元素：釙和鐳。
1903 年，她得到了諾貝爾獎，是第一位得到諾貝爾獎的女性。1911 年，她又得到第二座諾貝爾獎。
在一場戰爭期間，她幫助醫生使用 X 光機找出骨折的地方，救了許多士兵。
瑪麗・居禮讓全世界看到，女孩和女性也能成為偉大的科學家。

ph.ex: She loves to dance.
ph.exzh: 她喜歡跳舞。

ph.ex: My cousin moved to Canada last year.
ph.exzh: 我表哥去年搬到加拿大。

ph.ex: Let's work together on this project.
ph.exzh: 我們一起合作完成這個專題吧。

ph.ex: Many families lost their homes during a war.
ph.exzh: 許多家庭在戰爭期間失去了家園。

b.title: Two Nobel Prizes and a Notebook That Still Glows
text: Maria Skłodowska was born in Warsaw on November 7, 1867. Because women could not attend university in Russian-ruled Poland, she studied in secret before moving to Paris in 1891, where she enrolled at the Sorbonne.
There she met the physicist Pierre Curie, and the couple began investigating the mysterious rays given off by uranium. Marie coined the word 'radioactivity' to describe them.
In 1898 they announced two new elements: polonium, named after her homeland, and radium. Isolating them meant processing tonnes of mineral waste in a leaky shed.

In 1903 Marie became the first woman to receive a Nobel Prize, shared with Pierre and Henri Becquerel. After Pierre died in a street accident in 1906, she took over his professorship and won a second Nobel, in chemistry, in 1911 — still the only person honoured in two different sciences.
During the First World War she equipped vehicles with X-ray machines to help army surgeons.
She died in 1934 from illness linked to years of radiation exposure. Her notebooks remain so radioactive that they are kept in lead-lined boxes.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Marie Curie named polonium after her occupied homeland, Poland.
Despite great obstacles, Curie made key discoveries and won two Nobels.
Despite great obstacles, Curie won the very first Nobel Prize ever given.
Marie and Pierre Curie did their research in a cold, leaky shed.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: Where did the name 'polonium' come from?
opts: Pierre's family name
The city of Paris
A Greek word for 'light'
Marie's homeland, Poland
q.why: 第三段：named after her homeland。

q.q: What makes Marie Curie unique among Nobel winners?
opts: The only person to win the Chemistry prize two times
The only person to win the Physics prize twice
The only person honoured in two different sciences
The only winner to share it with her daughter
q.why: 第四段：the only person honoured in two different sciences。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “coined” the word means she ___.
opts: invented the word
measured the rays
discovered the element
published a book
q.why: coin a word = 創造新詞。

q.q: Why are her notebooks kept in lead-lined boxes?
opts: They are still radioactive
They are extremely valuable
They are written in a secret code
They are very old and fragile
q.why: 最後一段：remain so radioactive。

q.q: Which lesson from Curie's life is MOST useful for scientists working with new materials today?
opts: Avoid all new materials because they might be dangerous
Work alone so that nobody else is ever harmed
Keep new discoveries secret until they are proven safe
Study the dangers and use protection, even when excited
q.why: 她因長期接觸輻射而病逝——研究新物質要重視風險與防護。

tr.en: There she met the physicist Pierre Curie, and the couple began investigating the mysterious rays given off by uranium.
tr.zh: 她在那裡遇見了物理學家皮耶・居禮，這對夫妻開始研究鈾所放出的神秘射線。

tr.en: Isolating them meant processing tonnes of mineral waste in a leaky shed.
tr.zh: 要把它們分離出來，就得在一間會漏水的棚子裡處理好幾噸的礦物廢料。

tr.en: During the First World War she equipped vehicles with X-ray machines to help army surgeons.
tr.zh: 第一次世界大戰期間，她在車輛上裝設 X 光機，協助軍醫。

tz: 瑪麗亞・斯克沃多夫斯卡 1867 年 11 月 7 日生於華沙。因為在俄國統治下的波蘭，女性不能上大學，她只好偷偷地讀書，直到 1891 年搬到巴黎，進入索邦大學就讀。
她在那裡認識了物理學家皮耶・居禮，兩人開始研究鈾所發出的神秘射線。瑪麗創造了「放射性」這個詞來描述它們。
1898 年，他們宣布發現兩種新元素：以她的祖國命名的釙，以及鐳。要把它們分離出來，必須在一間會漏水的棚子裡處理好幾噸的礦物廢料。
1903 年，瑪麗成為第一位獲得諾貝爾獎的女性，與皮耶和亨利・貝克勒共享這個獎。皮耶在 1906 年死於一場街頭意外後，她接下了他的教授職位，並在 1911 年獲得第二座諾貝爾獎（化學獎）——至今仍是唯一在兩個不同科學領域獲獎的人。
第一次世界大戰期間，她把 X 光機裝到車輛上，協助軍醫治療傷兵。
她在 1934 年死於與多年暴露在輻射下有關的疾病。她的筆記本至今仍帶有很強的放射性，被保存在內襯鉛板的盒子裡。

ph.ex: They planned the party in secret.
ph.exzh: 他們偷偷地籌備派對。

ph.ex: The flowers give off a sweet smell.
ph.exzh: 這些花散發出甜甜的香味。

ph.ex: The ship was named after the queen.
ph.exzh: 這艘船以女王命名。

ph.ex: She took over the shop from her father.
ph.exzh: 她從父親手中接管了這家店。

ph.ex: Many illnesses are linked to stress.
ph.exzh: 許多疾病和壓力有關。

c.title: The Price of Discovery
text: Marie Curie's biography reads like a sequence of barriers overcome. Born Maria Skłodowska in Warsaw on November 7, 1867, she grew up under Russian rule in a society that excluded women from higher education, and studied clandestinely before reaching Paris and the Sorbonne in 1891.

With her husband Pierre, she pursued the strange emissions of uranium, coining the term 'radioactivity' and, in 1898, announcing two new elements: polonium, a pointed tribute to her occupied homeland, and radium. Extracting even tiny quantities required years of gruelling labour in a draughty shed.

Recognition came, though not without resistance. She became the first woman Nobel laureate in 1903, and after Pierre's sudden death she won a second prize, in chemistry, in 1911 — a distinction no one has matched across two sciences. Yet the French press also hounded her over her private life, and a scientific academy rejected her membership.

Her legacy is double-edged. Radioactivity transformed medicine and physics, and during the First World War her mobile X-ray units aided countless wounded soldiers. But the hazards were poorly understood: she died in 1934 of a condition linked to prolonged exposure, and her papers still require protective handling.
Curie's life thus embodies both the brilliance of science and the cost of discovering something before we know how dangerous it is.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Curie overcame huge barriers to transform science, at a real personal cost.
Curie's life shows that radioactivity is far too dangerous to study.
Curie overcame huge barriers mainly because Pierre did most of the work for her.
Curie's discoveries were less important than the fame they brought.
q.why: 主旨：突破障礙的成就與未知危險的代價。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “clandestinely” means ___.
opts: proudly
slowly
secretly
carelessly
q.why: clandestinely = 秘密地。

q.q: Why does the writer call naming polonium “a pointed tribute”?
opts: It honoured Pierre, who helped her discover it
It was named after the sharp shape of its crystals
It began as a private joke between the two scientists
It honoured Poland, then occupied and not independent
q.why: 以被佔領的祖國命名——刻意的致敬。

q.q: How does the writer present Curie's legacy?
opts: As entirely positive in every way
As 'double-edged' — beneficial, yet dangerous
As a warning against doing science
As 'double-edged' — famous, but not very useful
q.why: 第四段：Her legacy is double-edged。

q.q: What does the final sentence do?
opts: Introduces her daughter's scientific career
Lists her most important scientific papers
Argues that she deserved a third Nobel Prize
Sums up both sides: brilliance and cost
q.why: 結尾總結光輝與代價。

q.q: A new technology could help many patients but its long-term risks are unknown. Which approach best reflects the lesson of Curie's life?
opts: Stop all research on it immediately and for good
Continue the research, but study and limit the risks
Use it widely at once, because the benefits are clear
Ignore the risks, as Curie herself once did
q.why: 居禮的一生顯示：發現的價值與未知危險並存，需謹慎研究。

tz: 瑪麗・居禮的傳記讀起來就像一連串被克服的障礙。她本名瑪麗亞・斯克沃多夫斯卡，1867 年 11 月 7 日生於華沙，在俄國統治下、一個把女性排除在高等教育之外的社會中長大；她偷偷地求學，直到 1891 年才來到巴黎、進入索邦大學。
她和丈夫皮耶一起研究鈾發出的奇特輻射，創造了「放射性」這個詞，並在 1898 年宣布發現兩種新元素：釙——一個刻意向她被占領的祖國致敬的名字——以及鐳。即使只是提煉出極少的量，也需要在一間透風的棚子裡進行多年艱苦的勞動。
肯定終究到來，但並非沒有阻力。她在 1903 年成為第一位女性諾貝爾獎得主；皮耶驟逝後，她在 1911 年又獲得第二座獎（化學獎）——至今沒有人能在兩個科學領域達到這樣的成就。然而，法國媒體也因她的私生活窮追猛打，一個科學院還拒絕了她的入會申請。
她的遺產是兩面刃。放射性徹底改變了醫學和物理學，第一次世界大戰期間，她的行動 X 光車也幫助了無數受傷的士兵。但當時人們對其危險了解得很少：她在 1934 年死於一種與長期暴露有關的疾病，她的文件至今仍需要防護措施才能處理。
因此，居禮的一生同時體現了科學的光輝，以及在我們還不知道某樣東西有多危險之前就發現它所要付出的代價。

ph.ex: Her diary reads like a novel.
ph.exzh: 她的日記讀起來像一本小說。

ph.ex: The plan worked, though not without problems.
ph.exzh: 這個計畫成功了，但並非沒有問題。

ph.ex: His record is one that no one has matched.
ph.exzh: 他的紀錄至今沒有人比得上。

ph.ex: Reporters hounded the actor over his private life.
ph.exzh: 記者們因為那位演員的私生活不斷騷擾他。

ph.ex: Fame can be a double-edged sword.
ph.exzh: 名氣可能是一把兩面刃。

ph.ex: He trained every day and thus became the fastest runner.
ph.exzh: 他每天訓練，因此成為跑得最快的人。

discuss: Marie Curie had to study in secret because she was a woman. What barriers do some students still face today?
Her discoveries helped people but also harmed her health. Should scientists keep researching something if they don't yet know whether it is dangerous?
If you could ask Marie Curie one question, what would it be?

topic: Diwali: The Festival of Lights
zh: 排燈節：點亮黑夜的光明節
src: BBC · National Geographic · VOA

a.title: A Festival Full of Lights
text: This year, Diwali is on November 8. Diwali is a big festival in India. People also call it the Festival of Lights.
During Diwali, families light many small oil lamps called diyas. They put them in windows and doorways.
People clean their homes and wear new clothes. They draw colourful patterns on the floor with coloured powder.
Families visit each other and share sweets. In the evening, many people watch fireworks.
Diwali celebrates light winning over darkness and good winning over evil.
Many people in other countries celebrate Diwali too, so it is a festival for the whole world.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to make small oil lamps
Why people watch fireworks
Diwali, the Festival of Lights
Coloured powder patterns on the floor
q.why: 全文介紹排燈節；其他是細節。

q.q: What are diyas?
opts: Small oil lamps
Colourful floor patterns
Sweets shared by families
Electric lights in the city
q.why: 第二段：small oil lamps called diyas。

q.q: What do people use to draw patterns on the floor?
opts: Oil from the lamps
Coloured powder
Paint brushes
Flowers and leaves only
q.why: 第三段：with coloured powder。

q.q: In the text, “evil” means ___.
opts: something dark
something old
something scary but fun
something very bad
q.why: evil = 邪惡。

q.q: Why do people light lamps during Diwali?
opts: To help people see the fireworks
Because it is very dark in winter
To show light winning over darkness
To decorate their windows for visitors
q.why: 第五段：light winning over darkness。
