q.q: Which Taiwanese festival is MOST similar to Diwali in its use of light?
opts: The Dragon Boat Festival
Teachers' Day
Children's Day
The Lantern Festival
q.why: 元宵節也以燈火為核心，與排燈節最相似。

gt.en: Diwali is a big festival in India.
gt.zh: 排燈節是印度的一個大節日。

gt.en: During Diwali, families light many small oil lamps called diyas.
gt.zh: 排燈節期間，家家戶戶都會點亮許多叫做「迪亞」的小油燈。

gt.en: They draw colourful patterns on the floor with coloured powder.
gt.zh: 他們用彩色的粉末在地上畫出繽紛的圖案。

gt.en: In the evening, many people watch fireworks.
gt.zh: 到了晚上，許多人會看煙火。

tz: 今年的排燈節在 11 月 8 日。排燈節是印度的一個重要節日，人們也叫它「光明節」。
在排燈節期間，家家戶戶會點起許多叫做「迪亞（diya）」的小油燈，把它們放在窗邊和門口。
人們會打掃家裡、穿上新衣服，還會用彩色粉末在地上畫出繽紛的圖案。
家人會互相拜訪、分享甜點。到了晚上，很多人會觀賞煙火。
排燈節慶祝的是光明戰勝黑暗、善良戰勝邪惡。
其他國家也有很多人慶祝排燈節，所以它是一個屬於全世界的節日。

ph.ex: We call it the 'cat café'.
ph.exzh: 我們把它叫做「貓咪咖啡館」。

ph.ex: Our families visit each other at New Year.
ph.exzh: 我們兩家過年時會互相拜訪。

ph.ex: Good wins over evil in most fairy tales.
ph.exzh: 在大部分童話裡，善良都會戰勝邪惡。

ph.ex: Children wear new clothes at Lunar New Year.
ph.exzh: 過年時孩子們會穿新衣服。

b.title: Lamps Against the Dark
text: Diwali, which falls on November 8 this year, is one of the most important festivals in India, celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains as well as by communities from Singapore to Britain.

Its name comes from a Sanskrit word meaning 'row of lights'. Families place rows of small clay oil lamps, called diyas, along windows, roofs and doorways, and many cities glow with electric decorations.

Different traditions explain the festival in different ways. In much of northern India, Diwali marks the return of the prince Rama to his kingdom of Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravana; people lit lamps to guide him home.

Many families also pray to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and good fortune, after cleaning and decorating their homes. Rangoli — bright patterns made from coloured powder, rice or flowers — welcome guests at the door.
The celebrations usually last five days and are filled with family visits, gifts and sweets.
In recent years, some cities, including Delhi, have limited fireworks because of serious air pollution, encouraging quieter, greener ways to celebrate.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: In northern India, Diwali marks Rama's return to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana.
Families light lamps and pray to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and good fortune.
Diwali is a single-night festival in Delhi that is mainly about lighting fireworks.
Diwali, the Festival of Lights, has many meanings and is adapting to modern concerns.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: What does the name 'Diwali' mean?
opts: Festival of wealth
Return of the prince
Row of lights
New year
q.why: 第二段：'row of lights'。

q.q: In northern India, what does Diwali mark?
opts: Rama's return to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana
The birthday of Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth
The start of the rice harvest in the north
The founding of the city of Delhi long ago
q.why: 原文：“In much of northern India, Diwali marks the return of the prince Rama to his kingdom of Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravana; people lit lamps to guide him home.”

q.q: In paragraph 6, “pollution” means ___.
opts: loud noise made only by fireworks
harmful things in the air, water or land
too many people crowded into one place
smoke that comes only from oil lamps
q.why: pollution = 汙染。

q.q: Why have some cities limited fireworks?
opts: Because fireworks are too expensive
Because people no longer celebrate Diwali
Because fireworks scare animals
Because of serious air pollution
q.why: 最後一段：because of serious air pollution。

q.q: A city wants to keep Diwali joyful but cut pollution. Which idea fits the text best?
opts: Cancel all Diwali celebrations in the city completely
Allow unlimited fireworks, but for one night only
More lamps and electric lights, and fewer fireworks
Ban every kind of light during the festival days
q.why: 文章提到城市鼓勵更安靜、更環保的慶祝方式。

tr.en: Families place rows of small clay oil lamps, called diyas, along windows, roofs and doorways, and many cities glow with electric decorations.
tr.zh: 家家戶戶在窗邊、屋頂和門口擺上一排排叫做「迪亞」的小陶土油燈，許多城市也因電燈裝飾而閃閃發亮。

tr.en: Many families also pray to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and good fortune, after cleaning and decorating their homes.
tr.zh: 許多家庭在打掃和布置好家裡之後，也會向財富與好運的女神吉祥天女祈禱。

tr.en: In recent years, some cities, including Delhi, have limited fireworks because of serious air pollution, encouraging quieter, greener ways to celebrate.
tr.zh: 近年來，包括德里在內的一些城市因為嚴重的空氣汙染而限制施放煙火，鼓勵大家用更安靜、更環保的方式慶祝。

tz: 今年落在 11 月 8 日的排燈節，是印度最重要的節日之一，印度教徒、錫克教徒和耆那教徒都會慶祝，從新加坡到英國的各地社群也會一起過節。
它的名字來自一個意思是「一排燈火」的梵文字。家家戶戶把一排排叫做「迪亞」的小陶製油燈，擺在窗邊、屋頂和門口，許多城市也被電燈裝飾照得發亮。
不同的傳統用不同的方式解釋這個節日。在印度北部的大部分地區，排燈節紀念王子羅摩打敗魔王羅波那後，回到他的王國阿約提亞；人們點燈指引他回家。
許多家庭在打掃和布置好家裡後，也會向財富與好運女神拉克什米祈禱。門口用彩色粉末、米或花朵排成的鮮豔圖案「蘭果麗（rangoli）」，則用來迎接客人。
慶祝活動通常持續五天，充滿了家人間的拜訪、禮物和甜點。
近年來，包括德里在內的一些城市因為嚴重的空氣污染而限制燃放煙火，鼓勵人們用更安靜、更環保的方式慶祝。

ph.ex: She speaks English as well as Japanese.
ph.exzh: 她會說英文，也會說日文。

ph.ex: The word 'pajamas' comes from Hindi.
ph.exzh: 「pajamas」這個字來自印地語。

ph.ex: People learn in different ways.
ph.exzh: 人們用不同的方式學習。

ph.ex: The room was filled with laughter.
ph.exzh: 房間裡充滿了笑聲。

ph.ex: The game was stopped because of the rain.
ph.exzh: 比賽因為下雨而中止。

c.title: A Festival of Many Meanings
text: Diwali, which in 2026 falls on November 8, is often summarised as India's 'festival of lights', a phrase that captures its spectacle but understates its variety. Celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains, and by diaspora communities across the globe, it carries different stories for different people.

In northern India it commemorates the homecoming of Rama to Ayodhya after his victory over the demon king Ravana; elsewhere it honours Lakshmi, goddess of prosperity, or marks other religious milestones. What unites these traditions is a shared symbolism: light dispelling darkness, knowledge overcoming ignorance.

The rituals are tangible and communal. Homes are scrubbed and adorned, rows of clay diyas flicker on balconies, and intricate rangoli patterns welcome visitors. Over five days, families exchange sweets and gifts, settle accounts and renew relationships.

Modernity has complicated the picture. Fireworks, long central to the celebrations, now contribute to hazardous smog in cities such as Delhi, prompting bans and debates about whether tradition must bend to public health.
Diwali thus offers a vivid example of how a living festival evolves: its core meaning endures while its practices are continually renegotiated by each generation.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Diwali has only one true meaning: the return of Rama to his kingdom.
Diwali is, at heart, mainly a festival of fireworks and celebration.
Diwali's many meanings are slowly being replaced by one modern meaning: shopping.
Diwali's many meanings are united by light; its practices evolve, its core endures.
q.why: 主旨：多元意義以光明象徵相連，做法演變、核心不變。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “diaspora” communities are ___.
opts: religious leaders who guide the celebrations
families who live in northern India
people living outside their ancestral homeland
groups that campaign against fireworks
q.why: diaspora = 海外僑民。

q.q: Why does the writer say the phrase 'festival of lights' “understates its variety”?
opts: The lights used are not actually very bright
It has many different stories and meanings
The festival lasts for only a single night
The festival is mainly about food and sweets
q.why: 第一段：carries different stories for different people。

q.q: How does the writer discuss the fireworks debate?
opts: In a balanced way, as tradition meeting health
As a clear and complete victory for tradition
As proof that big festivals are harmful
Without showing any real interest in it
q.why: 第四段把放煙火的爭議呈現為「傳統」與「公共健康」之間的取捨，語氣平衡。

q.q: What does the final paragraph conclude?
opts: Diwali should stop changing and return to its old form
Fireworks will soon be banned in every Indian city
Only diaspora communities still keep the old traditions
A living festival keeps its core while practices change
q.why: 結尾：core meaning endures while its practices are renegotiated。

q.q: Which change to a Taiwanese festival best fits the writer's idea of a “living festival”?
opts: Stopping the festival completely to protect the air
Keeping every single custom exactly the same forever
Burning less paper money while still honouring ancestors
Using more fireworks than ever while forgetting the ancestors
q.why: 保留核心意義、調整做法，正是作者說的活的節日。

tz: 2026 年落在 11 月 8 日的排燈節，常被概括為印度的「光明節」——這個說法抓住了它的壯觀，卻低估了它的多樣性。印度教徒、錫克教徒、耆那教徒，以及遍布全球的海外僑民社群都會慶祝它，而它對不同的人承載著不同的故事。
在印度北部，它紀念羅摩戰勝魔王羅波那後回到阿約提亞；在其他地方，它敬拜繁榮女神拉克什米，或標記其他宗教上的里程碑。把這些傳統連結在一起的，是共同的象徵：光明驅散黑暗，知識戰勝無知。
這些儀式具體而且充滿群體感。家裡被刷洗、裝飾一新，一排排陶製油燈在陽台上搖曳，精緻的蘭果麗圖案迎接訪客。在五天之中，家人互贈甜點和禮物、結清帳目、重新聯絡感情。
現代生活讓情況變得複雜。長久以來是慶典核心的煙火，如今在德里等城市造成危險的霧霾，引來禁令，也引發一場辯論：傳統是否必須為公共健康讓步？
因此，排燈節生動地說明了一個仍然活著的節日如何演變：它的核心意義持續不變，而它的習俗則不斷被每一個世代重新協商。

ph.ex: The movie can be summarised as a story about hope.
ph.exzh: 這部電影可以概括為一個關於希望的故事。

ph.ex: The new rule complicates the picture for small shops.
ph.exzh: 新規定讓小店家的情況變得更複雜。

ph.ex: What unites us is our love of music.
ph.exzh: 把我們連在一起的是對音樂的熱愛。

ph.ex: Holidays are a time to renew relationships.
ph.exzh: 假期是重新聯絡感情的時候。

ph.ex: The school would not bend to the pressure.
ph.exzh: 學校不願向壓力讓步。

ph.ex: Each generation has its own music.
ph.exzh: 每一個世代都有自己的音樂。

discuss: Diwali celebrates light winning over darkness. Which festivals in Taiwan use lights or lanterns, and what do they mean?
Should festivals change their traditions (like fireworks) to protect the environment? Why or why not?
If you could invite a friend from India to a Taiwanese festival, which one would you choose and why?

topic: What Are the US Midterm Elections?
zh: 美國期中選舉是什麼？
src: AP · NBC · VOA · The Washington Post

a.title: Americans Vote in the Middle
text: On November 3, 2026, people in the United States will vote. These elections are called the midterm elections.
They are called 'midterm' because they happen in the middle of the President's four years.
People do not choose a new President this time. They choose people for Congress. Congress makes the country's laws.
Congress has two parts: the House of Representatives and the Senate. Every seat in the House is part of this election, and about one third of the Senate is too.
Many states also choose new governors. Each state has its own leader.
After the votes are counted, Congress may change. This can make it easier or harder for the President to make new laws.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How Americans choose a new President every four years
The US midterm elections and what they decide
Why the US Congress has two different parts
How each state chooses its own governor
q.why: 全文講期中選舉；其他是細節或錯誤。

q.q: Why are they called 'midterm' elections?
opts: They happen in the middle of the President's term
They happen in the middle of each calendar year
They choose people for the middle part of Congress
They take about half a year to finish counting
q.why: 原文：“They are called 'midterm' because they happen in the middle of the President's four years.”

q.q: What do people choose in these elections?
opts: A new President for the next four years
A new President and a new Vice President
People for Congress and many governors
Only the governors of the fifty states
q.why: 原文：“Many states also choose new governors.”

q.q: In the text, “laws” are ___.
opts: the votes that people make in elections
the seats that members have in Congress
the leaders who run each of the states
rules everyone in a country must follow
q.why: laws = 法律。

q.q: Why do the midterm results matter for the President?
opts: They decide whether the President stays in office
They choose the members of the President's team
They change the President's term to two years
They make it easier or harder to pass new laws
q.why: 線索：“This can make it easier or harder for the President to make new laws.”

q.q: If most new members of Congress disagree with the President after the midterms, what is the MOST likely result?
opts: It becomes harder for the President to pass laws
The President must leave office straight away
The President is given even more power than before
Nothing changes at all in how the country is run
q.why: 國會改變會讓總統推動新法更容易或更困難。

gt.en: On November 3, 2026, people in the United States will vote.
gt.zh: 2026 年 11 月 3 日，美國人將會投票。

gt.en: Congress makes the country's laws.
gt.zh: 國會負責制定國家的法律。

gt.en: Many states also choose new governors.
gt.zh: 許多州也會選出新的州長。

gt.en: After the votes are counted, Congress may change.
gt.zh: 選票統計完之後，國會可能會改變。

tz: 2026 年 11 月 3 日，美國人民將要投票。這些選舉叫做「期中選舉」。
它們之所以叫做「期中」，是因為它們在總統四年任期的中間舉行。
這次人們不是選新的總統，而是選國會的成員。國會負責制定國家的法律。
國會有兩個部分：眾議院和參議院。眾議院的每一個席次都在這次改選，參議院則大約有三分之一要改選。
許多州也會選出新的州長。每個州都有自己的領導人。
選票計算完後，國會可能會改變。這可能讓總統更容易、或更難制定新的法律。

ph.ex: The phone rang in the middle of dinner.
ph.exzh: 晚餐吃到一半時電話響了。

ph.ex: Music is part of my daily life.
ph.exzh: 音樂是我日常生活的一部分。

ph.ex: A map makes it easier to find the museum.
ph.exzh: 有地圖會更容易找到博物館。

b.title: Halfway Through, Voters Have Their Say
text: On Tuesday, November 3, Americans head to the polls for the 2026 midterm elections. By law, federal elections are held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

Midterms take place halfway through a president's four-year term. The presidency itself is not on the ballot, but voters decide who will sit in Congress, the branch of government that writes laws and controls federal spending.

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are up for election, because House members serve two-year terms. Senators serve six-year terms, so only about a third of the 100 Senate seats are contested this year. Most states are also electing governors, along with thousands of local officials.

Going into the vote, Republicans held narrow majorities in both chambers. Historically, the president's party has usually lost seats in midterm elections, partly because voters often use them to express how they feel about the government's performance.
Results can take days in close races, as mail-in ballots are counted.
Whichever party controls each chamber next year will shape which laws can pass during the president's final two years.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Every one of the hundred seats in the Senate is up for election in 2026.
Held at the end of a term, midterms choose the next president and Vice President.
The president's party usually wins more seats in the midterm elections.
Held halfway through a term, midterms decide Congress and shape the next two years.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；第二、四項錯誤。

q.q: Why is every House seat up for election?
opts: House members serve six-year terms
House members serve two-year terms
The House was dissolved by the president
There are only a few House seats
q.why: 原文：“All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are up for election, because House members serve two-year terms.”

q.q: What has usually happened to the president's party in midterms?
opts: It has usually lost seats
It has usually won more seats
It has usually kept exactly the same seats
It has usually lost the presidency
q.why: 原文：“Historically, the president's party has usually lost seats in midterm elections, partly because voters often use them to express how they feel about the …”

q.q: In paragraph 2, a “ballot” is ___.
opts: a building where people vote
a group in a political party
the paper or form used to vote
the result of an election
q.why: ballot = 選票。

q.q: Why might results take days in close races?
opts: Voting lasts for several days
The Senate must approve the results first
Mail-in ballots take time to count
Computers are not used in US elections
q.why: 線索：“Results can take days in close races, as mail-in ballots are counted.”

q.q: A news headline the day after the vote says: “Final results in!” for a very close race. Based on the text, why should readers be careful?
opts: Close races are usually decided by the president on the same night
Close races can take days while mail-in ballots are counted
Newspaper headlines about elections are never correct
Only the president is allowed to announce the results
q.why: 第五段：接近的選情因郵寄選票可能要幾天才有結果。

tr.en: On Tuesday, November 3, Americans head to the polls for the 2026 midterm elections.
tr.zh: 11 月 3 日星期二，美國人前往投票所，參加 2026 年的期中選舉。

tr.en: Senators serve six-year terms, so only about a third of the 100 Senate seats are contested this year.
tr.zh: 參議員的任期是六年，所以今年 100 個參議院席次中只有大約三分之一要改選。

tr.en: Going into the vote, Republicans held narrow majorities in both chambers.
tr.zh: 在投票之前，共和黨在參眾兩院都只握有些微的多數。

tz: 11 月 3 日星期二，美國人將前往投票所，參加 2026 年的期中選舉。依照法律，聯邦選舉在十一月第一個星期一之後的第一個星期二舉行。
期中選舉在總統四年任期的一半時舉行。總統本身不在選票上，但選民會決定誰坐進國會——也就是負責寫法律、掌控聯邦支出的政府部門。
眾議院全部 435 個席次都要改選，因為眾議員的任期是兩年。參議員的任期是六年，所以今年 100 個參議院席次中只有大約三分之一要競爭。大多數的州也在選州長，還有數千名地方官員。
選前，共和黨在兩院都只掌握些微的多數。從歷史上看，總統所屬的政黨通常會在期中選舉中失去席次，部分原因是選民常用這個機會表達他們對政府表現的感受。
在選情接近的選區，因為郵寄選票還在計算，結果可能要好幾天才會出來。
明年由哪一個政黨掌控兩院，將決定在總統最後兩年任期內，哪些法律能夠通過。

ph.ex: After school, we headed to the library.
ph.exzh: 放學後，我們前往圖書館。

ph.ex: Half of the seats are up for election this year.
ph.exzh: 今年有一半的席次要改選。

ph.ex: Going into the final, our team felt confident.
ph.exzh: 進入決賽前，我們隊伍很有信心。

ph.ex: I like this city, partly because of the food.
ph.exzh: 我喜歡這座城市，部分是因為這裡的食物。

ph.ex: Three people are on the ballot for class president.
ph.exzh: 有三個人參選班長。

c.title: A National Report Card
text: Every two years, American politics pauses for a verdict, and the 2026 midterm elections on November 3 are the latest. Falling midway through a presidential term, they leave the White House untouched but decide who controls Congress — and therefore how much of a president's agenda can survive the remaining two years.

The mechanics explain the stakes. All 435 members of the House of Representatives face voters, since they serve two-year terms, while roughly a third of the Senate's 100 seats rotate on six-year cycles. Dozens of governorships and thousands of state and local offices are decided on the same ballot.

Political scientists often describe midterms as a referendum on the incumbent. The president's party has lost ground in most midterms of the modern era, a pattern attributed to voters' tendency to check whoever holds power and to the lower turnout of more satisfied supporters.

Going into the vote, Republicans held slim majorities in both chambers, so even a modest shift could transfer control and usher in a period of divided government — gridlock to some, healthy restraint to others.
Whatever the outcome, the midterms illustrate a defining feature of the American system: power is deliberately fragmented, and voters are given frequent chances to rebalance it.
gloss: 公投；（對施政的）信任投票

q.q: Which best captures the writer's point?
opts: Midterms decide which party will be able to choose the next president.
Midterms are a frequent check on power, deciding Congress and the agenda.
Midterms matter much less than the presidential elections do.
Divided government always leads to complete political gridlock.
q.why: 主旨：期中選舉是對權力的定期檢驗。

q.q: In paragraph 3, the “incumbent” is ___.
opts: the person or party now in power
the party that lost the last election
a brand-new candidate for office
a voter who supports the president
q.why: incumbent = 現任者。

q.q: Why might the president's party tend to lose seats in midterms, according to the text?
opts: The president's supporters vote more in midterms
The law limits how many seats the party can win
Midterm ballots are harder to understand
Voters often check whoever holds power
q.why: 線索：“The president's party has lost ground in most midterms of the modern era, a pattern attributed to voters' tendency to check whoever holds power and to the lower …”

q.q: How does the writer describe divided government?
opts: As always harmful to the American people
As always healthy for American democracy
Balanced — 'gridlock to some, restraint to others'
As a system the writer wants to replace with one party
q.why: 第四段。

q.q: What idea does the final paragraph highlight?
opts: The president should be given more power to act
Midterm elections should be cancelled in future
The system gives all of the power to the president alone
The system spreads power and lets voters rebalance it
q.why: 結尾。

q.q: Taiwan also holds elections at different times for different offices. Which statement best applies the writer's idea to Taiwan?
opts: Frequent elections let voters regularly check power
Elections should be held only once every ten years
Only one office in the country should be elected
Elections never really change anything at all
q.why: 作者強調頻繁選舉讓選民有機會再平衡權力。

tz: 每隔兩年，美國政治就會暫停一下，等待一次評判；11 月 3 日的 2026 年期中選舉就是最新的一次。它落在總統任期的中間，不會動到白宮，卻決定了誰掌控國會——也因此決定總統的施政議程在剩下的兩年中能保住多少。
選舉的運作方式說明了其中的利害關係。眾議院全部 435 名議員都要面對選民，因為他們的任期是兩年；而參議院的 100 個席次以六年為一輪，大約三分之一會輪替。數十個州長職位，以及數千個州和地方的公職，也都在同一張選票上決定。
政治學家常把期中選舉形容為對執政者的一場公投。在近代大多數的期中選舉中，總統所屬政黨都會失去席次——這個模式被歸因於選民傾向於制衡掌權者，以及比較滿意的支持者投票率較低。
選前，共和黨在兩院都只掌握微弱多數，所以即使是小幅的變動，也可能讓控制權易手，迎來一段「分立政府」時期——對某些人來說是僵局，對另一些人來說則是健康的制衡。
不論結果如何，期中選舉都說明了美國制度的一個關鍵特色：權力被刻意地分散，而選民被賦予頻繁的機會去重新平衡它。

ph.ex: Let's pause for a short break.
ph.exzh: 我們停下來休息一下吧。

ph.ex: The storm left the old temple untouched.
ph.exzh: 這場暴風雨沒有讓這座老廟受到任何損壞。

ph.ex: Several questions were on the same ballot.
ph.exzh: 好幾個議題都在同一張選票上。

ph.ex: Our team lost ground in the second half.
ph.exzh: 我們隊在下半場失去了優勢。

ph.ex: The new law ushered in a period of change.
ph.exzh: 這條新法律開啟了一段變革時期。

ph.ex: Whatever the outcome, I'm proud of you.
ph.exzh: 不論結果如何，我都以你為榮。

discuss: Why do you think the US holds elections for Congress every two years instead of only when choosing a president?
Compare elections in the US and in Taiwan. What is similar and what is different?
Some people think 'divided government' slows things down; others think it stops one side from having too much power. Which view do you agree with, and why?

topic: Carl Sagan and the Pale Blue Dot
zh: 卡爾・薩根與「暗淡藍點」
src: NASA · Science · The New York Times

a.title: A Tiny Blue Dot in Space
text: Carl Sagan was born on November 9, 1934, in New York. He loved the stars when he was a child.
He grew up to be a scientist who studied planets.
He also made a famous TV show called Cosmos. It helped millions of people learn about space.
In 1990, a spacecraft called Voyager 1 was very far from home. Sagan asked NASA to turn its camera and take a photo of Earth.
In the photo, Earth looks like a very small blue dot. People call it the Pale Blue Dot.
Sagan said the photo shows that our planet is small and special, so we must take care of it and of each other.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How Carl Sagan made the TV show Cosmos in 1980
Carl Sagan and a photo showing how small Earth is
How Voyager 1 travelled so far away from Earth
Why NASA took so many photos of other planets
q.why: 全文以薩根為主，重點是他請 NASA 拍的地球照片與其意義；其他選項只是文中細節。

q.q: What was Cosmos?
opts: A spacecraft that took a famous photo of Earth
The name given to the famous photo of Earth
A TV show that helped people learn about space
A faraway planet that Sagan studied for years
q.why: 第三段：a famous TV show called Cosmos。

q.q: Who asked NASA to take the photo of Earth?
opts: Carl Sagan
Voyager 1's team, to test the camera
Millions of TV viewers
NASA's leaders, for a TV show
q.why: 第四段：Sagan asked NASA to turn its camera。

q.q: In the text, a “spacecraft” is ___.
opts: a scientist who studies the stars
a photo that was taken in space
a TV show that is about space
a machine that travels in space
q.why: spacecraft = 太空船；Voyager 1 是一艘太空船。

q.q: Why did Sagan think the photo was important?
opts: It proved that Earth is the brightest of the planets
It was the very first photo NASA had ever taken
It showed our small planet, so we should care for it
It helped NASA find new planets around other stars
q.why: 最後一段：our planet is small and special, so we must take care of it and of each other。

q.q: Your class is making a poster about the Pale Blue Dot. Which title fits Sagan's message best?
opts: “One Small Home — Let's Take Care of It”
“Earth: The Biggest Planet of Them All”
“How to Build Your Own Spacecraft”
“Space Is Much Too Far Away to Matter”
q.why: 薩根想傳達地球渺小而珍貴，要彼此照顧；第二個標題最符合。

gt.en: He grew up to be a scientist who studied planets.
gt.zh: 他長大後成為一位研究行星的科學家。

gt.en: He also made a famous TV show called Cosmos.
gt.zh: 他也製作了一個有名的電視節目，叫做《宇宙》。

gt.en: In 1990, a spacecraft called Voyager 1 was very far from home.
gt.zh: 1990 年，一艘叫做航海家一號的太空船離家非常遙遠。

gt.en: Sagan asked NASA to turn its camera and take a photo of Earth.
gt.zh: 薩根請 NASA 把它的相機轉過來，拍一張地球的照片。

tz: 卡爾・薩根 1934 年 11 月 9 日出生於紐約。他小時候就很喜歡星星。
他長大後成為一位研究行星的科學家。
他也製作了一個很有名的電視節目，叫做《宇宙》（Cosmos）。這個節目幫助數百萬人認識太空。
1990 年，一艘名叫航海家 1 號的太空船已經離家非常遙遠。薩根請美國太空總署（NASA）把它的相機轉過來，拍一張地球的照片。
在照片裡，地球看起來像一個非常小的藍色小點。大家把它叫做「暗淡藍點」。
薩根說，這張照片告訴我們：我們的星球又小又特別，所以我們必須好好照顧它，也要好好照顧彼此。

ph.ex: I want to be a teacher when I grow up.
ph.exzh: 我長大後想當老師。

ph.ex: Can you take a photo of us in front of the tree?
ph.exzh: 你可以幫我們在樹前拍張照嗎？

ph.ex: My sister takes care of our cat when I am at school.
ph.exzh: 我上學時，姐姐會照顧我們的貓。

ph.ex: Good friends help each other.
ph.exzh: 好朋友會互相幫忙。

b.title: Seeing Ourselves from Six Billion Kilometres Away
text: Carl Sagan, born in New York on November 9, 1934, became one of the best-known scientists of the twentieth century — not only for his research on planets but for his gift for explaining science to ordinary people.
His 1980 television series Cosmos took viewers on a journey from atoms to galaxies and was watched by hundreds of millions of people around the world.

Sagan also helped plan NASA's missions to other planets. For the two Voyager spacecraft launched in 1977, he led the team that chose sounds, music and pictures for a golden record meant for any aliens who might find it.
In 1990, Voyager 1 was about six billion kilometres from Earth. At Sagan's urging, NASA turned the spacecraft around to photograph its home planet one last time.
In the image, Earth appears as a tiny, pale blue speck, smaller than a single pixel, floating in a beam of scattered sunlight.

Sagan argued that the photo should make us humble: every war, every empire and every person who ever lived existed on that tiny dot, which is all the more reason to treat it, and one another, with care.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Voyager 1 carried a golden record with sounds and music from Earth.
Sagan made science popular and used a photo of Earth to show its fragility.
Cosmos was watched by hundreds of millions of people around the world.
Sagan proved that Earth is the smallest and least important planet in our solar system.
q.why: 其他三項都是文中的真實細節，但只有第二項涵蓋全文重點。

q.q: How far from Earth was Voyager 1 when it took the photo?
opts: About six million kilometres
About sixty billion kilometres
As far as the edge of our galaxy
About six billion kilometres
q.why: 第四段：about six billion kilometres from Earth。

q.q: What was the golden record for?
opts: To play music for astronauts during the long trip
To store all of the photos that Voyager took
To carry sounds and pictures of Earth for any finders
To record Cosmos so that future viewers could see it
q.why: 第三段：for a golden record meant for any aliens who might find it。

q.q: In paragraph 6, “humble” means ___.
opts: aware that you are less important than you think
proud of everything that humans have built
afraid of what might be out there in space
proud that humans are the centre of the universe
q.why: humble = 謙卑的；照片讓人明白自己的渺小。

q.q: Why does the writer say Earth was “smaller than a single pixel”?
opts: To show how tiny Earth looks from so far away
To suggest the camera was not working properly
To explain why scientists could not use the photo
To prove that Earth is smaller than the other planets
q.why: 強調從那麼遠的地方看，地球小得連一個像素都不到。

q.q: Two countries are arguing about a small piece of land. Which sentence would Sagan most likely say to them?
opts: “The stronger country should simply take the land.”
“Space travel is far more important than land.”
“Each country should build its own spacecraft.”
“We all share one tiny planet — solve this with care.”
q.why: 第六段：每場戰爭、每個帝國都發生在那個小點上，所以要彼此善待——第二句最符合他的觀點。

tr.en: Sagan also helped plan NASA's missions to other planets.
tr.zh: 薩根也協助規劃 NASA 前往其他行星的任務。

tr.en: At Sagan's urging, NASA turned the spacecraft around to photograph its home planet one last time.
tr.zh: 在薩根的力勸下，NASA 把太空船轉過來，最後一次拍攝它的家鄉星球。

tr.en: In the image, Earth appears as a tiny, pale blue speck, smaller than a single pixel, floating in a beam of scattered sunlight.
tr.zh: 在影像中，地球看起來像一個微小的淡藍色小點，比一個像素還小，飄浮在一道散射的陽光裡。

tz: 卡爾・薩根 1934 年 11 月 9 日生於紐約，成為二十世紀最知名的科學家之一——不只因為他對行星的研究，也因為他擅長把科學講給一般人聽。
他 1980 年的電視節目《宇宙》帶領觀眾從原子一路旅行到星系，全世界有好幾億人看過。
薩根也協助規劃美國太空總署前往其他行星的任務。1977 年發射的兩艘航海家太空船上，各帶著一張金唱片，是由他領導的團隊挑選聲音、音樂和圖片，要送給任何可能發現它的外星生物。
1990 年，航海家 1 號距離地球大約六十億公里。在薩根的力勸下，美國太空總署把太空船轉過頭，最後一次拍攝它的家鄉星球。
在影像中，地球只是一個微小、淡藍色的光點，比一個像素還小，飄浮在一道散射的陽光裡。
薩根認為這張照片應該讓我們謙卑：每一場戰爭、每一個帝國、每一個曾經活過的人，都存在於那個小點上——這更是我們應該用心對待它、也用心對待彼此的理由。

ph.ex: She is not only smart but also very kind.
ph.exzh: 她不只聰明，而且非常善良。

ph.ex: At my teacher's urging, I joined the speech contest.
ph.exzh: 在老師的力勸下，我參加了演講比賽。

ph.ex: Please turn your chair around and face the board.
ph.exzh: 請把椅子轉過來，面向黑板。

ph.ex: Let's practise the song one last time before the show.
ph.exzh: 表演前我們再練最後一次。

ph.ex: The test is next week — all the more reason to start studying now.
ph.exzh: 下週就要考試了——更有理由現在開始讀書。

c.title: The Smallest Photograph Ever Taken of Everything
text: Few scientists have been as comfortable in front of a camera as Carl Sagan. Born in Brooklyn on November 9, 1934, he combined serious planetary research with an almost evangelical conviction that science belonged to everyone, a belief he carried into the 1980 series Cosmos, which reached audiences of hundreds of millions.

His most enduring idea, however, came from a photograph that was nearly never taken. By 1990 Voyager 1 had completed its scientific tour of the outer planets and was heading out of the solar system. Pointing its camera back toward the Sun risked damaging the instruments, and some engineers saw little scientific value in the attempt.
Sagan persisted. The resulting image showed Earth from roughly six billion kilometres away as a fraction of a pixel, a pale blue mote caught in a streak of scattered light.

In his writing he turned that speck into a meditation on perspective: every quarrel and conquest in human history had played out on that minuscule stage, and no help, he observed, was likely to come from elsewhere to save us from ourselves.

The photograph is scientifically trivial and philosophically enormous — a reminder that sometimes the most important thing an instrument can show us is not something new, but ourselves, seen clearly for the first time.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's point?
opts: The Pale Blue Dot photo added important new scientific data on Earth.
A photo of little scientific value became a lesson about our place.
Sagan was more interested in television fame than in real research.
Voyager 1's mission ended because taking the photo damaged its camera.
q.why: 主旨：科學價值不大的照片，卻成為關於人類處境的強大啟示。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “persisted” means Sagan ___.
opts: kept pushing for the photo despite objections
quietly accepted the engineers' final decision
changed the plan to photograph Mars instead
persuaded all of the engineers immediately
q.why: persisted = 堅持；即使有人反對仍堅持拍照。

q.q: Why did some engineers resist taking the photo?
opts: Earth would look far too small, so the photo had no beauty
Voyager 1 had already run completely out of power
They wanted to save the camera for one more planet
Facing the Sun risked damage for little scientific gain
q.why: 第二段：risked damaging the instruments … little scientific value。

q.q: How would you describe the writer's attitude toward the photo?
opts: Neutral and purely technical
Sceptical about its importance
Admiring and reflective
Nostalgic but disappointed
q.why: 作者稱它 philosophically enormous，語氣欽佩且深思。

q.q: What contrast does the final paragraph draw?
opts: Large scientific value versus small philosophical meaning
Small scientific value versus large philosophical meaning
The engineers' fears versus the photo's great success
Earth versus the other planets that Voyager visited
q.why: 結尾：scientifically trivial and philosophically enormous。

q.q: A student says: “A photo with no new scientific data is a waste of money.” Which response best reflects the writer's view?
opts: Agree — science should spend its money only on collecting new data.
Agree — the engineers were right to resist taking the photo at all.
Disagree — the photo actually contained a lot of new scientific data.
Disagree — some images matter because they change how we see ourselves.
q.why: 作者認為照片的價值在於讓我們重新看見自己（結尾句），而非新數據。

tz: 很少有科學家像卡爾・薩根那樣在鏡頭前自在。他 1934 年 11 月 9 日生於布魯克林，把嚴謹的行星研究，和一種近乎傳教般的信念結合在一起：科學屬於每一個人。他把這份信念帶進 1980 年的影集《宇宙》，觸及了好幾億名觀眾。
然而，他最歷久不衰的想法，卻來自一張差點沒拍成的照片。到了 1990 年，航海家 1 號已完成對外行星的科學巡禮，正飛出太陽系。把相機轉回太陽的方向，有損壞儀器的風險，而且有些工程師認為這麼做沒什麼科學價值。
薩根堅持不放棄。拍出來的影像從大約六十億公里外看地球，它只佔一個像素的一小部分，是一粒被困在散射光線中的淡藍色微塵。
他在著作中把那個小點化為一段關於視角的沉思：人類歷史上的每一次爭吵與征服，都在那個極小的舞台上演；而且他指出，不太可能有任何來自別處的救援，能把我們從自己手中拯救出來。
這張照片在科學上微不足道，在哲學上卻意義重大——它提醒我們，有時候一件儀器能讓我們看到最重要的東西，不是什麼新事物，而是我們自己，第一次被看得如此清楚。

ph.ex: I get nervous when I speak in front of the class.
ph.exzh: 在全班面前說話時，我會緊張。

ph.ex: This notebook belongs to my brother.
ph.exzh: 這本筆記本是我哥哥的。

ph.ex: The bus was heading out of the city when it started to rain.
ph.exzh: 公車正要開出城時，開始下雨了。

ph.ex: If you skip breakfast, you risk feeling tired all morning.
ph.exzh: 不吃早餐的話，你可能整個早上都很累。

ph.ex: She turned her old T-shirt into a shopping bag.
ph.exzh: 她把舊 T 恤改成了一個購物袋。

ph.ex: Nobody knows how the story will play out.
ph.exzh: 沒有人知道事情會怎麼發展。

ph.ex: Last summer I saw the sea for the first time.
ph.exzh: 去年夏天我第一次看到海。

discuss: If you could send one sound or picture from Earth to aliens, what would you choose and why?
Sagan believed science belongs to everyone. How can scientists make their work easier for ordinary people to understand?
Does seeing Earth as a tiny dot change how you think about arguments between people or countries? Explain.

topic: Sesame Street: How a TV Street Taught the World
zh: 芝麻街：一條教會全世界的電視街道
src: PBS · The New York Times · NBC

a.title: Can You Tell Me How to Get to Sesame Street?
text: On November 10, 1969, a new TV show started in the United States. It was called Sesame Street.
The show was made for young children. It taught letters, numbers, and how to be kind.
The show had funny puppets called Muppets, like Big Bird, Elmo, and Cookie Monster.
Children learned while they laughed. The songs were short and easy to remember.
Today, Sesame Street is shown in more than 150 countries. Some countries make their own version with new characters.
Many adults around the world first learned to count with Sesame Street.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The puppets on Sesame Street, like Big Bird and Elmo
How the show is made in more than 150 countries
A children's TV show that helped kids learn
Songs that help young children remember numbers
q.why: 全文介紹《芝麻街》如何幫助孩子學習；布偶、各國版本、歌曲都是細節。

q.q: What did the show teach?
opts: Only songs and dances for fun
How to make your own puppets
Letters and numbers, but not manners
Letters, numbers, and how to be kind
q.why: 第二段：letters, numbers, and how to be kind。

q.q: In how many countries is Sesame Street shown today?
opts: In more than 150 countries
Only in the United States
In about 15 countries
In every country in the world
q.why: 第五段：more than 150 countries。

q.q: In the text, “puppets” are ___.
opts: actors who wear big animal costumes
toy figures that people move to act
cartoon drawings shown on television
children who sing songs on the show
q.why: puppets = 布偶。

q.q: Why do some countries make their own version of the show?
opts: So the show fits their children and culture
Because the American version cost too much
Because their children did not like Big Bird
So they can stop showing the American version
q.why: 各國用自己的角色和語言，讓節目更貼近當地孩子。

q.q: A little cousin finds counting boring. Based on the text, which idea would most likely help?
opts: Give the cousin a long list of numbers to copy
Use a short, funny song about counting
Tell the cousin to wait until school starts
Show a long lesson with no pictures
q.why: 第四段：孩子在歡笑中學習，短歌好記——用好玩的短歌最符合文章的方法。

gt.en: It taught letters, numbers, and how to be kind.
gt.zh: 它教字母、數字，還有如何待人親切。

gt.en: The show had funny puppets called Muppets, like Big Bird, Elmo, and Cookie Monster.
gt.zh: 這個節目有一些好笑的布偶，叫做布偶家族，像是大鳥、艾蒙和餅乾怪獸。

gt.en: The songs were short and easy to remember.
gt.zh: 這些歌又短又好記。

gt.en: Some countries make their own version with new characters.
gt.zh: 有些國家用新的角色製作自己的版本。

tz: 1969 年 11 月 10 日，美國開播了一個新的電視節目，叫做《芝麻街》。
這個節目是為幼兒製作的。它教字母、數字，還有怎麼做一個善良的人。
節目裡有好笑的布偶，叫做「布偶秀（Muppets）」，像是大鳥、艾蒙和餅乾怪獸。
孩子們一邊笑一邊學習。歌曲又短又好記。
今天，《芝麻街》在超過 150 個國家播出。有些國家還做了自己的版本，加入新的角色。
世界上很多大人，第一次學數數就是跟著《芝麻街》學的。

ph.ex: This game was made for young children.
ph.exzh: 這個遊戲是為幼兒設計的。

ph.ex: My dad taught me how to ride a bike.
ph.exzh: 爸爸教我怎麼騎腳踏車。

ph.ex: The museum has more than 500 paintings.
ph.exzh: 這間博物館有超過 500 幅畫。

ph.ex: Many children learn to swim in summer.
ph.exzh: 很多孩子在夏天學會游泳。

b.title: The Experiment That Became a Neighbourhood
text: When Sesame Street first aired on November 10, 1969, it was a bold experiment: could television, which many parents saw as a waste of time, actually help young children learn?
The idea came from television producer Joan Ganz Cooney and psychologist Lloyd Morrisett, who noticed that children from poorer families often started school behind their classmates.
Their team worked closely with educational researchers, testing each segment to see whether children paid attention and remembered what they had seen.
Jim Henson's Muppets made the lessons lively. Big Bird, Elmo and Cookie Monster became stars, and short, catchy songs turned the alphabet into something to sing.
The show also set its stories on a diverse city street where people of different backgrounds lived together, which was unusual for television at the time.
Over the decades, local versions have been produced around the world, each adapting the lessons to its own culture — proof that a good idea about learning can travel far.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Sesame Street was a tested experiment proving TV could teach, and it spread.
Jim Henson's Muppets made Sesame Street popular all around the world.
Sesame Street was created because parents in 1969 loved television.
The show's street showed people of different backgrounds living together.
q.why: 其他選項是細節或與文意相反；第二項涵蓋全文。

q.q: Why did Cooney and Morrisett start the show?
opts: To give Jim Henson's Muppets their own TV show
Parents wanted many more cartoons on television
Schools asked for a show that could replace teachers
Poorer children often started school behind others
q.why: 第二段：children from poorer families often started school behind。

q.q: What was unusual about the show's street?
opts: It was filmed on a real street in New York City
Only puppets lived there, with no humans at all
People of different backgrounds lived together there
Everyone on the street came from exactly the same background
q.why: 第五段：a diverse city street where people of different backgrounds lived together。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “bold” means ___.
opts: carefully planned and safe
willing to take risks
very popular
expensive to make
q.why: bold = 大膽的。

q.q: Why did the team test each segment with children?
opts: To check whether children paid attention and learned
To choose which children could appear on television
To find out which puppet children liked the most
To make sure each episode was long enough
q.why: 第三段：testing each segment to see whether children paid attention and remembered。

q.q: Your school wants to make a short learning video for first graders. Which step follows the Sesame Street method most closely?
opts: Make the video as long as possible to cover everything
Ask only the teachers which songs they like best
Copy a Sesame Street episode exactly as it is
Show a draft to first graders and fix what they forget
q.why: 《芝麻街》的關鍵是「先給孩子看、測試、再修改」（第三段）。

tr.en: Their team worked closely with educational researchers, testing each segment to see whether children paid attention and remembered what they had seen.
tr.zh: 他們的團隊和教育研究人員密切合作，測試每一個片段，看看孩子們是否專心看，並記得看過的內容。

tr.en: Big Bird, Elmo and Cookie Monster became stars, and short, catchy songs turned the alphabet into something to sing.
tr.zh: 大鳥、艾蒙和餅乾怪獸都成了明星，簡短好記的歌曲讓字母變成可以唱的東西。

tz: 《芝麻街》在 1969 年 11 月 10 日首播時，是一場大膽的實驗：許多家長認為看電視是浪費時間，但電視真的能幫助幼兒學習嗎？
這個構想來自電視製作人瓊・甘茲・庫尼和心理學家勞埃德・莫里塞特，他們注意到，來自較貧窮家庭的孩子，常常一入學就落後同學。
他們的團隊和教育研究人員密切合作，測試每一個片段，看孩子們有沒有專心、記不記得自己看過的內容。
吉姆・漢森的布偶讓課程變得生動。大鳥、艾蒙和餅乾怪獸成了明星，簡短又好記的歌曲，把字母變成了可以唱的東西。
節目也把故事設定在一條多元的城市街道上，不同背景的人在那裡一起生活，這在當時的電視上很少見。
幾十年來，世界各地都製作了在地版本，每一個都把課程調整成適合自己的文化——證明一個關於學習的好點子可以傳得很遠。

ph.ex: Some people think video games are a waste of time.
ph.exzh: 有些人認為電玩是在浪費時間。

ph.ex: The idea for the club came from a student.
ph.exzh: 成立這個社團的點子來自一位學生。

ph.ex: Our teacher works closely with parents.
ph.exzh: 我們的老師和家長密切合作。

ph.ex: Please pay attention to the instructions.
ph.exzh: 請注意聽說明。

ph.ex: Over the decades, the town has changed a lot.
ph.exzh: 數十年來，這個小鎮改變了很多。

c.title: Teaching by Television
text: In 1969 the idea that television could educate small children struck many critics as faintly absurd. The medium was widely regarded as a 'vast wasteland', and few believed that a programme sandwiched between advertisements could teach anything worth knowing.

Sesame Street, which premiered on November 10 of that year, set out to prove them wrong — and, unusually, to measure whether it had. Producer Joan Ganz Cooney and psychologist Lloyd Morrisett built research into the production process itself, revising segments that failed to hold children's attention or to leave a trace in their memory.
The aim was explicitly social. Children from low-income homes were arriving at school already behind, and television reached them where books often did not.
Jim Henson's Muppets supplied the charm that made the method palatable, while the show's integrated street quietly modelled a society in which difference was ordinary.

Decades of studies have since associated the programme with gains in early literacy and numeracy, and its international co-productions have adapted its format to contexts from South Africa to the Middle East. Its legacy is less a set of characters than an argument: that entertainment and education need not be enemies if learning is designed, tested and taken seriously.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Sesame Street succeeded mainly because of its famous puppets.
Most American television in 1969 was already educational.
International versions became more successful than the original.
Entertainment can educate when learning is designed and tested.
q.why: 主旨：只要學習經過設計與測試，娛樂也能教育。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “palatable” means ___.
opts: boring and hard to accept
pleasant or easy to accept
old-fashioned and dull
expensive to produce
q.why: palatable = 容易接受的。

q.q: What made Sesame Street unusual compared with most TV shows of its time?
opts: It was paid for entirely by advertisements
It was the very first show made for children
It used research to test and revise its content
It was filmed in many countries at the same time
q.why: 第二段：built research into the production process itself。

q.q: How does the writer present the 1969 critics?
opts: As doubters the show set out to disprove
As experts who were later proven right
As the people who first suggested the show
As unfair enemies of children's education
q.why: set out to prove them wrong——作者把批評者當作被節目推翻的觀點。

q.q: What does the final sentence do?
opts: Summarises the most popular characters
Introduces criticism of the programme
Describes the show's plans for the future
States the broader lesson of its legacy
q.why: 結尾總結：entertainment and education need not be enemies。

q.q: A parent says: “Any cartoon my child enjoys must be educational.” Based on the text, what is the best reply?
opts: “Not necessarily — learning must be designed and tested.”
“True — if children enjoy it, they must be learning from it.”
“True — that is exactly what the 1969 critics believed.”
“Not at all — entertainment can never teach children anything.”
q.why: 作者主張娛樂與教育可以結合，但前提是學習經過設計與測試。

tz: 在 1969 年，「電視能教育幼兒」這個想法，在許多評論家看來有點荒謬。電視被普遍看作一片「廣大的荒原」，很少人相信一個夾在廣告之間的節目，能教出什麼值得知道的東西。
那年 11 月 10 日首播的《芝麻街》，就是要證明他們錯了——而且很不尋常地，還要去測量自己是否真的做到了。製作人瓊・甘茲・庫尼和心理學家勞埃德・莫里塞特把研究直接納入製作流程，凡是抓不住孩子注意力、或沒在孩子記憶中留下痕跡的片段，都會被修改。
它的目標明確帶有社會意義。來自低收入家庭的孩子，進學校時就已經落後，而電視能觸及他們，書本卻常常做不到。
吉姆・漢森的布偶提供了魅力，讓這套方法變得容易被接受；節目裡那條多元融合的街道，則默默示範了一個「差異是很平常的事」的社會。
此後數十年的研究顯示，這個節目與幼兒讀寫和數學能力的提升有關；它的國際合製版本，也把節目形式調整到從南非到中東的各種環境。它留下的，與其說是一群角色，不如說是一個論點：只要學習經過設計、測試並被認真對待，娛樂和教育並不一定是敵人。

ph.ex: She set out to read 50 books this year.
ph.exzh: 她今年打算讀 50 本書。

ph.ex: He trained hard to prove his coach wrong.
ph.exzh: 他努力訓練，要證明教練看錯了。

ph.ex: The plan failed to solve the problem.
ph.exzh: 這個計畫沒能解決問題。

ph.ex: We arrived at school just before the bell.
ph.exzh: 我們在鐘響前一刻到達學校。

ph.ex: Too much screen time is associated with poor sleep.
ph.exzh: 花太多時間看螢幕和睡不好有關。

ph.ex: Learning English need not be boring.
ph.exzh: 學英文不必是無聊的。

discuss: Did you learn anything from a TV show or video when you were small? What was it?
Can entertainment and learning go together? Give an example from your own life.
If you created a TV show to teach children in Taiwan, what would it teach and who would the characters be?

topic: Singles' Day: From a Joke to the World's Biggest Sale
zh: 雙十一：從玩笑變成全球最大購物節
src: The Economist · NBC · Taipei Times

a.title: Why 11/11 Is a Shopping Day
text: The date November 11 looks like four ones: 11/11. In China, some students called it Singles' Day, a day for people without a boyfriend or girlfriend.
At first, it was just a joke. Students had parties and bought small gifts for themselves.
In 2009, a big online shopping company started selling things at low prices on that day.
Soon, millions of people were shopping online on November 11. Now it is one of the biggest shopping days in the world.
In Taiwan, many online shops also have 11/11 sales.
But shopping too much is not always good. Some people buy things they do not need, and the boxes make a lot of waste.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: Why the date 11/11 looks like four number ones
How online shops in Taiwan hold 11/11 sales
How Singles' Day became a huge shopping day
Why online shopping boxes make so much waste
q.why: 全文講雙十一的轉變；其他是細節。

q.q: Why was the day first called Singles' Day?
opts: It was the day a big shopping company started
It is an official holiday for students in China
Shops sold only one item each on that day
The date looks like four ones, like single people
q.why: 第一段：looks like four ones … a day for people without a boyfriend or girlfriend。

q.q: What happened in 2009?
opts: A big online shop started low-price sales that day
Students held the very first Singles' Day party
Taiwan's online shops held their first 11/11 sale
Singles' Day became an official national holiday
q.why: 第三段：In 2009, a big online shopping company started selling things at low prices。

q.q: In the text, “waste” means ___.
opts: money that people save up
things that are thrown away
things that are on sale
boxes that are used again
q.why: waste = 廢棄物。

q.q: What does the writer think about shopping on 11/11?
opts: Everyone should wait until 11/11 to buy things
It can be fun, but buying too much is not good
The sales are really only meant for students
It is bad, so nobody should shop on that day
q.why: 最後一段：shopping too much is not always good。

q.q: On 11/11 you see a sale on a game you don't really need. What would the writer most likely advise?
opts: Buy it quickly before the sale price ends
Buy two so that you can give one away
Think about whether you really need it first
Buy it, because everyone else is buying too
q.why: 文章提醒有人買了不需要的東西——先想清楚是否需要。

gt.en: Students had parties and bought small gifts for themselves.
gt.zh: 學生們開派對，還買小禮物送給自己。

gt.en: In 2009, a big online shopping company started selling things at low prices on that day.
gt.zh: 2009 年，一家大型網路購物公司開始在那天低價賣東西。

gt.en: Soon, millions of people were shopping online on November 11.
gt.zh: 很快地，數百萬人在十一月十一日上網購物。

gt.en: In Taiwan, many online shops also have 11/11 sales.
gt.zh: 在台灣，許多網路商店也有雙十一特價。

tz: 11 月 11 日這個日期看起來像四個 1：11/11。在中國，有些學生把它叫做「光棍節」，是給沒有男朋友或女朋友的人過的節日。
一開始，這只是一個玩笑。學生們開派對，買小禮物送給自己。
2009 年，一家大型網路購物公司在這一天開始低價拍賣商品。
很快地，數百萬人在 11 月 11 日上網購物。現在它是全世界最大的購物日之一。
在台灣，很多網路商店也有 11/11 的特價活動。
但是買太多不一定是好事。有些人會買下自己不需要的東西，而且那些紙箱會製造很多垃圾。

ph.ex: The cloud looks like a rabbit.
ph.exzh: 那朵雲看起來像一隻兔子。

ph.ex: At first I was shy, but now I love the class.
ph.exzh: 一開始我很害羞，但現在我很喜歡這堂課。

ph.ex: The shop sells fruit at low prices on Sundays.
ph.exzh: 這家店星期天低價賣水果。

b.title: How a Student Joke Became a Shopping Giant
text: Singles' Day began in the 1990s as a joke among university students in Nanjing, China. Because the date 11/11 is made up of four ones, they adopted it as a day to celebrate being single.
In 2009 the e-commerce company Alibaba saw a business opportunity and held a one-day online sale. Only a few dozen brands took part, but the idea caught on fast.

Within a decade, Singles' Day had grown into the world's largest shopping event, far bigger than America's Black Friday. Sales were counted live on giant screens, and in 2021 Alibaba reported orders worth over 80 billion US dollars during the festival period.
The event spread across Asia, including Taiwan, where online platforms now offer 11/11 discounts.
Its critics point to the costs. Mountains of packaging create waste, delivery vehicles add pollution, and clever marketing encourages impulse buying — purchases people later regret.
In recent years the festival has become quieter, as companies stopped announcing record totals and shoppers became more careful with money.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: A student joke grew into a giant shopping event, with benefits and costs.
In 2021, Alibaba reported orders worth over 80 billion US dollars.
A shopping company invented the day in 2009 and asked students to celebrate it.
Students in Nanjing chose 11/11 because the date has four ones.
q.why: 只有第二項涵蓋起源、成長與代價。

q.q: How many brands took part in the first sale in 2009?
opts: A few hundred
Several thousand
Every brand in China
Only a few dozen
q.why: 第二段：Only a few dozen brands took part。

q.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a cost of the festival?
opts: Waste from all the packaging
Shops closing because of low prices
Pollution from delivery vehicles
Impulse buying by shoppers
q.why: 第五段列出包裝、汙染、衝動購物；沒有提到商店倒閉。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “impulse buying” means buying things ___.
opts: only after comparing many prices
in large amounts to save money
suddenly, without careful thought
for other people as presents
q.why: impulse buying = 衝動購物。

q.q: What does the last paragraph suggest about the festival today?
opts: It is growing faster than it ever has before
It has now been replaced by Black Friday
It is now really only for single people
It has become less showy as habits changed
q.why: 最後一段：the festival has become quieter。

q.q: An online shop shows a countdown: “Only 5 minutes left! Buy now!” Based on the text, why might this be a problem?
opts: The pressure can lead to impulse buying
It means the products are of low quality
It makes delivery much slower than usual
It is against the law in Taiwan
q.why: 倒數製造急迫感，促成文章提到的衝動購物。

tr.en: Because the date 11/11 is made up of four ones, they adopted it as a day to celebrate being single.
tr.zh: 因為 11/11 這個日期是由四個一組成的，他們就把它當作慶祝單身的日子。

tr.en: In 2009 the e-commerce company Alibaba saw a business opportunity and held a one-day online sale.
tr.zh: 2009 年，電子商務公司阿里巴巴看到了商機，舉辦了一場為期一天的網路特賣。

tr.en: Mountains of packaging create waste, delivery vehicles add pollution, and clever marketing encourages impulse buying — purchases people later regret.
tr.zh: 堆積如山的包裝製造了垃圾，送貨車輛增加了汙染，而聰明的行銷手法則鼓勵衝動購物——也就是人們事後會後悔的購買。

tz: 光棍節起源於 1990 年代，是中國南京大學生之間的一個玩笑。因為 11/11 這個日期由四個 1 組成，他們就把這天當成慶祝單身的日子。
2009 年，電子商務公司阿里巴巴看見了商機，舉辦了一場為期一天的線上特賣。當時只有幾十個品牌參加，但這個點子很快就流行起來。
不到十年，光棍節就成長為全世界最大的購物活動，遠遠超過美國的黑色星期五。銷售額在巨大的螢幕上即時計算，2021 年阿里巴巴公布，購物節期間的訂單金額超過 800 億美元。
這個活動擴散到整個亞洲，包括台灣，現在台灣的網路平台也會推出 11/11 折扣。
批評者指出它的代價：堆積如山的包裝造成垃圾，送貨車輛增加污染，而巧妙的行銷手法會鼓勵衝動購物——也就是人們事後會後悔的消費。
近年來，這個購物節變得比較低調，因為企業不再公布破紀錄的總額，消費者花錢也變得更謹慎。

ph.ex: The new dance quickly caught on at our school.
ph.exzh: 這支新舞很快就在我們學校流行起來。

ph.ex: Only ten students took part in the race.
ph.exzh: 只有十名學生參加了賽跑。

ph.ex: Teachers point to sleep as a key to good grades.
ph.exzh: 老師們指出，睡眠是好成績的關鍵。

ph.ex: In recent years, more people have started cycling to work.
ph.exzh: 近年來，越來越多人開始騎腳踏車上班。

ph.ex: Be careful with your money on holiday.
ph.exzh: 放假時花錢要小心。

c.title: The Business of Being Alone
text: Few commercial phenomena illustrate the inventiveness of modern marketing as neatly as Singles' Day. What began in the 1990s as a self-mocking ritual among Nanjing university students, who chose 11/11 for its four solitary ones, has been transformed into the largest retail event on the planet.

The pivotal moment came in 2009, when Alibaba repackaged the date as an online sale. The company understood that a festival without traditions could be filled with whatever meaning sold best, and it supplied gala shows, countdowns and real-time sales tallies that turned shopping into a spectator sport.
By 2021 the reported value of orders exceeded 80 billion US dollars, dwarfing America's Black Friday.

Success, however, attracted scrutiny. Environmental groups highlighted the packaging generated by billions of parcels, economists noted how artificial urgency fuels impulsive spending, and regulators grew wary of the platforms' power.

Since then the event has grown more subdued; companies stopped trumpeting record totals and consumers have become more frugal. Singles' Day thus offers a compact lesson in how a date can be manufactured into a festival — and how the meaning a market creates can also, gradually, be questioned.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Singles' Day is an ancient Chinese tradition that Alibaba brought back.
Marketing can turn a date into a festival whose meaning is later questioned.
Marketing can turn any date into a festival that nobody ever questions afterwards.
Singles' Day became popular because single people tend to feel lonely.
q.why: 主旨：行銷能把日期打造成節慶，這種意義也可能被質疑。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “frugal” means ___.
opts: careful not to spend much money
eager to buy new things often
suspicious of big companies
loyal to one favourite brand
q.why: frugal = 節儉的。

q.q: Why does the writer say a festival “without traditions could be filled with whatever meaning sold best”?
opts: Traditional festivals are not allowed to hold any sales
The students had already planned what it would mean
The government decided what the festival would mean
A new festival had no fixed meaning for a company to shape
q.why: 第二段：沒有傳統包袱的節日，可以被填入最好賣的意義。

q.q: How does the writer view Singles' Day?
opts: Enthusiastic — a model for every country
Hostile — the festival is purely harmful
Analytical — impressed, yet aware of costs
Neutral — the writer gives no opinion
q.why: 既讚嘆行銷創意，也指出環境與消費問題。

q.q: How is the essay organised?
opts: Problem → proposed solution → final result
A comparison of Singles' Day and Black Friday throughout
Origin → commercial change → scale → criticism → lesson
Criticism first, then the history of the festival
q.why: 結構：起源 → 商業化 → 規模 → 批評 → 近年變化與啟示。

q.q: Which modern example is MOST similar to how Singles' Day was created?
opts: A traditional festival that families have celebrated for centuries
A company inventing “Pet Love Day” with discounts on pet products
A national holiday chosen to remember a war
A school sports day planned by students
q.why: 雙十一是企業把一個日期包裝成購物節；公司自創節日促銷最相似。

tz: 很少有商業現象能像光棍節一樣，簡潔地展現現代行銷的創造力。它在 1990 年代原本是南京大學生自我調侃的儀式，他們選中 11/11，是因為這四個孤單的 1；如今它卻被轉變成地球上規模最大的零售活動。
關鍵時刻出現在 2009 年，阿里巴巴把這個日期重新包裝成一場線上特賣。這家公司明白，一個沒有傳統的節日，可以被填進任何最好賣的意義；於是它推出晚會、倒數計時和即時銷售數字，把購物變成一項觀眾運動。
到了 2021 年，公布的訂單金額超過 800 億美元，讓美國的黑色星期五相形見絀。
然而，成功也招來檢視。環保團體指出數十億個包裹所產生的包裝廢棄物，經濟學家指出人為製造的緊迫感會助長衝動消費，監管機關也開始警惕這些平台的權力。
從那之後，這個活動變得比較收斂；企業不再大肆宣傳破紀錄的總額，消費者也變得更節儉。因此，光棍節提供了一堂精簡的課：一個日期如何被製造成一個節日——而市場所創造出來的意義，也可能逐漸受到質疑。

ph.ex: They turned the empty lot into a garden.
ph.exzh: 他們把那塊空地變成了花園。

ph.ex: Her diary is filled with drawings.
ph.exzh: 她的日記裡滿是圖畫。

ph.ex: The star's comments attracted scrutiny online.
ph.exzh: 這位明星的言論在網路上引來檢視。

ph.ex: Parents have grown wary of free apps that collect data.
ph.exzh: 家長開始對蒐集資料的免費應用程式有戒心。

ph.ex: He missed the bus and thus arrived late.
ph.exzh: 他錯過了公車，因此遲到了。

ph.ex: The app shows real-time information about the next bus.
ph.exzh: 這個應用程式會顯示下一班公車的即時資訊。

discuss: Have you or your family ever bought something on 11/11? Was it something you really needed?
How can shoppers avoid impulse buying when there are big sales?
Do you think online shopping festivals are good or bad for the environment? What could companies do better?

topic: Petra: The Rose-Red City
zh: 佩特拉：玫瑰色的古城
src: UNESCO · National Geographic · The New York Times

a.title: A City Cut into the Rocks
text: Petra is an old city in the desert of Jordan. Its buildings are not built with bricks. They are cut into the pink and red rocks!
People called the Nabataeans made the city more than 2,000 years ago.
To enter Petra, you walk through a long, narrow path between high rocks. It is called the Siq.
At the end of the path, you see a beautiful building called the Treasury. It is very tall.
The Nabataeans were clever with water. They made channels to catch rain in the dry desert.
Today, many tourists visit Petra. Some ride camels or donkeys to see more of the old city.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The long, narrow path known as the Siq
An ancient city carved into rocks in Jordan
How the Nabataeans collected rainwater
Tourists riding camels across the desert
q.why: 全文介紹佩特拉古城；其他都是細節。

q.q: What is the Siq?
opts: A tall building at the end of the path
A channel that carries the rainwater
The people who built the city of Petra
A long, narrow path between high rocks
q.why: 第三段：a long, narrow path between high rocks. It is called the Siq。

q.q: How did the Nabataeans get water in the dry desert?
opts: They carried it from the sea on camels
They dug deep wells under the Treasury
They made channels to catch rain
They bought water from other cities
q.why: 第五段：They made channels to catch rain。

q.q: In the text, “narrow” means ___.
opts: not wide
very long
very high
dark and cold
q.why: narrow = 狹窄的。

q.q: Why is Petra different from most cities?
opts: It was built only for tourists to visit and enjoy
It has no water at all, even in the rainy season
Its buildings are cut into rock, not built of bricks
It was built long ago by people from Europe
q.why: 第一段：cut into the pink and red rocks!

q.q: You are making a travel plan for Petra. Based on the text, what should you plan to do FIRST when you arrive?
opts: Walk through the Siq to reach the Treasury
Visit the water channels on the top of the Treasury
Ride a camel into the Treasury
Take a boat along the river
q.why: 第三、四段：要進入佩特拉先走過蛇道，盡頭才看到寶庫。

gt.en: Petra is an old city in the desert of Jordan.
gt.zh: 佩特拉是約旦沙漠裡的一座古城。

gt.en: To enter Petra, you walk through a long, narrow path between high rocks.
gt.zh: 要進入佩特拉，你得走過一條夾在高聳岩石之間、又長又窄的小路。

gt.en: The Nabataeans were clever with water.
gt.zh: 納巴泰人很懂得運用水。

gt.en: Today, many tourists visit Petra.
gt.zh: 今天，許多觀光客來參觀佩特拉。

tz: 佩特拉是約旦沙漠裡的一座古城。它的建築不是用磚頭蓋的，而是從粉紅色和紅色的岩石裡切鑿出來的！
一群叫做納巴泰人的人，在兩千多年前建造了這座城市。
要進入佩特拉，你得走過一條在高聳岩石之間、又長又窄的小路，它叫做「蛇道（Siq）」。
在小路的盡頭，你會看到一棟美麗的建築，叫做「寶庫」。它非常高。
納巴泰人很懂得利用水。他們在乾燥的沙漠裡挖了水道來收集雨水。
今天，有許多遊客來參觀佩特拉。有些人騎駱駝或驢子，去看古城的更多地方。

ph.ex: The steps are cut into the side of the hill.
ph.exzh: 台階是鑿在山坡上的。

ph.ex: There is a park at the end of my street.
ph.exzh: 我家那條街的盡頭有一座公園。

ph.ex: My grandpa is clever with tools.
ph.exzh: 我爺爺很會用工具。

ph.ex: I want to see more of Taiwan this summer.
ph.exzh: 這個夏天我想多看看台灣。

b.title: Hidden City of the Desert
text: Hidden among the mountains of southern Jordan, Petra is one of the most astonishing archaeological sites on Earth. Its temples and tombs were carved directly into rose-coloured sandstone cliffs.
The city was the capital of the Nabataeans, Arab traders who grew wealthy by controlling caravan routes that carried incense and spices across the desert more than two thousand years ago.

Visitors enter through the Siq, a winding canyon about a kilometre long whose walls rise as high as 80 metres. At its end, the facade of Al-Khazneh, known as the Treasury, suddenly appears in the sunlight.
Despite the dry climate, the Nabataeans supported a large population by building dams, cisterns and channels to collect and store rainwater.

After trade routes shifted and earthquakes struck, Petra slowly declined. For centuries it was known mainly to local Bedouin, until a Swiss traveller, Johann Ludwig Burckhardt, described it to Europeans in 1812.
Today Petra is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Jordan works to balance tourism with the need to protect the fragile stone.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The Treasury is a famous building carved into the rose-coloured cliffs.
Petra, a city built with bricks by Romans, was destroyed in one great earthquake.
The Nabataeans grew rich by trading valuable incense and spices.
Petra, a trading capital carved in stone, is now a protected world treasure.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是部分細節或錯誤說法。

q.q: How did the Nabataeans become wealthy?
opts: By controlling caravan routes for incense and spices
By selling the rose-coloured stone to other cities
By charging travellers to walk through the Siq
By farming the desert with the rain they collected
q.why: 第二段：controlling caravan routes that carried incense and spices。

q.q: Why did Petra decline?
opts: Its water channels dried up very suddenly
Burckhardt took its treasures to Europe
Trade routes shifted and earthquakes struck
Too many tourists damaged its buildings
q.why: 第五段：After trade routes shifted and earthquakes struck。

q.q: In paragraph 3, a “canyon” is ___.
opts: a wide, flat area of open desert
a deep, narrow valley with steep sides
a large building carved in stone
a tall tower carved high into the rock face
q.why: canyon = 峽谷。

q.q: What does the writer suggest by saying Petra was known mainly to local Bedouin?
opts: The local Bedouin were the ones who built Petra
It wasn't truly lost; Burckhardt told Europeans
No one at all lived near Petra for centuries
The Bedouin kept it a secret from Burckhardt
q.why: 當地人一直知道它，布克哈特是讓歐洲人知道。

q.q: Which plan best matches the text's idea of balancing tourism and protection at Petra?
opts: Limit visitor numbers and keep people on set paths
Allow unlimited visitors because tourism brings money
Close Petra to everyone forever
Rebuild the old buildings with new stone
q.why: 最後一段：balance tourism with the need to protect the fragile stone——限制人數、固定路線最平衡。

tr.en: Hidden among the mountains of southern Jordan, Petra is one of the most astonishing archaeological sites on Earth.
tr.zh: 隱藏在約旦南部群山之間的佩特拉，是地球上最令人驚嘆的考古遺址之一。

tr.en: Visitors enter through the Siq, a winding canyon about a kilometre long whose walls rise as high as 80 metres.
tr.zh: 遊客從「蛇道」進入，這是一條大約一公里長的蜿蜒峽谷，兩側的岩壁高達八十公尺。

tr.en: After trade routes shifted and earthquakes struck, Petra slowly declined.
tr.zh: 在貿易路線改變、又遭遇地震之後，佩特拉慢慢地衰落了。

tz: 佩特拉隱藏在約旦南部的群山之間，是地球上最令人驚嘆的考古遺址之一。它的神殿和墳墓直接雕鑿在玫瑰色的砂岩峭壁上。
這座城市是納巴泰人的首都。納巴泰人是阿拉伯商人，兩千多年前靠著掌控穿越沙漠、運送乳香和香料的商隊路線而致富。
遊客從「蛇道」進入，那是一條大約一公里長、蜿蜒的峽谷，兩側岩壁高達 80 公尺。走到盡頭，被稱為「寶庫」的卡茲尼神殿正面，會突然出現在陽光下。
儘管氣候乾燥，納巴泰人仍靠著修建水壩、蓄水池和水道來收集、儲存雨水，養活了大量人口。
在貿易路線改變、又遭遇地震之後，佩特拉慢慢衰落。好幾個世紀以來，主要只有當地的貝都因人知道它，直到 1812 年，瑞士旅行家約翰・路德維希・布克哈特向歐洲人描述了這個地方。
今天，佩特拉是聯合國教科文組織的世界遺產，約旦努力在觀光和保護脆弱的石頭之間取得平衡。

ph.ex: Their names are carved into the old tree.
ph.exzh: 他們的名字被刻在那棵老樹上。

ph.ex: The town grew wealthy from the tea trade.
ph.exzh: 這個小鎮靠茶葉貿易致富。

ph.ex: Prices can go as high as 500 dollars.
ph.exzh: 價格可能高達 500 元。

ph.ex: Despite the rain, we finished the race.
ph.exzh: 儘管下雨，我們還是跑完了比賽。

ph.ex: It is hard to balance schoolwork with sports.
ph.exzh: 要在課業和運動之間取得平衡很難。

c.title: Wealth Carved in Stone
text: Petra is often described as a lost city, but its real story is one of calculated prosperity. Carved into the rose-red sandstone of southern Jordan, it served as the capital of the Nabataeans, who grew rich by taxing and protecting the caravans that carried incense, myrrh and spices between Arabia and the Mediterranean.

The approach is pure theatre. Visitors thread their way through the Siq, a narrow gorge whose walls tower above them, until the facade of Al-Khazneh, the so-called Treasury, bursts into view, its columns cut, not built, from the living rock.

Less photogenic but more remarkable was the city's hydraulic engineering. In an arid landscape, the Nabataeans built dams, terracotta pipes and cisterns that captured flash floods and sustained a population of perhaps tens of thousands.

Petra's decline was gradual rather than sudden: Roman annexation, shifting trade routes toward the sea and devastating earthquakes eroded its importance until only Bedouin herders remained to know it.

Today, its popularity poses a quieter threat. Salt, wind and millions of footsteps wear at the soft stone, and conservationists argue that preserving Petra requires limiting the very admiration that keeps it famous.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: Petra was suddenly destroyed by a single great earthquake in one day.
Petra's most important feature is the carved facade of the Treasury.
Petra rose cleverly and declined slowly, and now its fame threatens it.
Petra survived mainly because almost no one ever came to visit it.
q.why: 主旨：精明的繁榮與緩慢衰落，如今名氣本身成為威脅。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “arid” means ___.
opts: very dry
very rocky
very hot
very empty
q.why: arid = 乾旱的。

q.q: Why does the writer call Petra's water system “more remarkable” than the Treasury?
opts: The water system is much older than the Treasury
Most tourists prefer to visit the water channels
The Treasury was actually built by the Romans
Supporting a city in a dry land beat a fine facade
q.why: 第三段：在乾旱地區養活大量人口，比華麗外觀更了不起。

q.q: How does the writer describe the entrance through the Siq?
opts: As tiring and dangerous
As dramatic, like theatre
As disappointing compared with photos
As purely practical
q.why: 第二段：The approach is pure theatre。

q.q: What irony does the final paragraph point out?
opts: Petra became famous only after it began to decline
Protecting it may mean limiting the admiration it gets
The ancient water system now damages the soft stone
Tourists prefer modern buildings to ancient ones
q.why: 結尾：preserving Petra requires limiting the very admiration that keeps it famous。

q.q: Which piece of evidence would BEST support the writer's claim that popularity threatens Petra?
opts: A record of how many camels live near Petra
A photo of the Treasury glowing at sunset
A study showing stone wears faster on busy paths
A guidebook that names Petra the best site to visit
q.why: 作者說人潮的腳步磨損軟石；顯示熱門路段磨損較快的研究最能支持。

tz: 佩特拉常被形容為一座失落之城，但它真正的故事，是一段精心經營的繁榮。它雕鑿在約旦南部玫瑰紅色的砂岩中，是納巴泰人的首都；納巴泰人靠著向往來阿拉伯與地中海之間、運送乳香、沒藥和香料的商隊收稅並提供保護而致富。
進城的路就像一場戲。遊客穿過「蛇道」——一條兩側岩壁高聳的狹窄峽谷——直到卡茲尼神殿，也就是所謂的「寶庫」，猛然映入眼簾；它的柱子是從整塊岩石中切鑿出來的，而不是一塊塊蓋起來的。
比較不上相、卻更了不起的，是這座城市的水利工程。在乾旱的土地上，納巴泰人修建水壩、陶製水管和蓄水池，攔住突如其來的洪水，養活了或許數以萬計的人口。
佩特拉的衰落是漸進的，而不是突然的：羅馬的併吞、貿易路線轉向海上，加上毀滅性的地震，一點一點削弱了它的重要性，最後只剩下貝都因牧人還知道它。
今天，它的高人氣構成一種比較不顯眼的威脅。鹽分、風和數以百萬計的腳步，正在磨損柔軟的石頭；保育人士認為，要保護佩特拉，就必須限制那份讓它聲名遠播的讚嘆。

ph.ex: He grew rich by selling bubble tea.
ph.exzh: 他靠賣珍珠奶茶致富。

ph.ex: We threaded our way through the crowded market.
ph.exzh: 我們在擁擠的市場中穿梭前進。

ph.ex: As we turned the corner, the ocean burst into view.
ph.exzh: 我們一轉過街角，大海就映入眼簾。

ph.ex: I prefer walking rather than taking the bus.
ph.exzh: 我比較喜歡走路，而不是搭公車。

ph.ex: Plastic waste poses a threat to sea turtles.
ph.exzh: 塑膠垃圾對海龜構成威脅。

ph.ex: The wind slowly wears at the old stone walls.
ph.exzh: 風慢慢地侵蝕著古老的石牆。

discuss: Why do you think the Nabataeans carved their buildings into rock instead of building with bricks?
Should famous places like Petra limit the number of visitors? What are the good and bad sides?
If you could visit one ancient city in the world, which would you choose and why?

topic: World Kindness Day
zh: 世界善意日：小小善意的大力量
src: VOA · Science · Taiwan News

a.title: Small Acts, Big Smiles
text: November 13 is World Kindness Day. It is a day to be kind to others.
Kindness can be very simple. You can smile at someone, help a classmate, or say thank you.
You can hold the door for someone, or share your snack with a friend.
When you are kind, other people feel happy. Scientists say it can make you feel happy too!
Kindness can also spread. When one person is kind, others often want to be kind too.
What kind thing can you do today?

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How scientists study happiness in their labs
World Kindness Day and simple ways to be kind
How to share your snacks with your friends
Why people should always hold the door open
q.why: 全文介紹世界善意日與簡單的善行；其他是例子。

q.q: Which is given as an example of kindness?
opts: Giving someone money
Doing a classmate's homework
Buying expensive gifts
Saying thank you
q.why: 第二段：say thank you。

q.q: What do scientists say about being kind?
opts: It can make you feel happy too
It only helps the other person
It is really good only for children
It makes people feel very tired
q.why: 第四段：it can make you feel happy too!

q.q: In the text, “spread” means ___.
opts: to stay with just one person
to keep something only for yourself
to move from one person to others
to become smaller and smaller
q.why: spread = 傳播、擴散。

q.q: Why does the text end with a question?
opts: To test whether readers remember the date
To show the writer is not sure what kindness is
To make readers think about being kind
To start a short quiz about World Kindness Day
q.why: 結尾問題邀請讀者行動。

q.q: Which situation best shows kindness “spreading” as the text describes?
opts: Amy helps Ben, and later Ben helps a new student
Amy helps Ben, and Ben says thank you
Amy shares her snack because she is full
Amy holds the door because her teacher asked her to
q.why: 文章說善意會傳開：一人善待後，別人也想善待他人——A 幫 B、B 再幫別人。

gt.en: It is a day to be kind to others.
gt.zh: 這是一個善待別人的日子。

gt.en: Kindness can be very simple.
gt.zh: 善意可以非常簡單。

gt.en: You can hold the door for someone, or share your snack with a friend.
gt.zh: 你可以幫別人扶著門，或是和朋友分享你的點心。

gt.en: When you are kind, other people feel happy.
gt.zh: 當你待人友善，別人就會覺得開心。

tz: 11 月 13 日是世界善良日。這是一個對別人好的日子。
善良可以很簡單。你可以對別人微笑、幫助同學，或說聲謝謝。
你可以幫別人扶著門，或和朋友分享你的點心。
當你善良待人，別人會覺得開心。科學家說，這也能讓你自己開心！
善良也會傳出去。當一個人善待別人，其他人往往也會想善待別人。
你今天可以做一件什麼樣的好事呢？

ph.ex: Always be kind to new students.
ph.exzh: 永遠要對新同學友善。

ph.ex: Don't forget to say thank you to the bus driver.
ph.exzh: 別忘了跟公車司機說謝謝。

ph.ex: He held the door for the woman with a baby.
ph.exzh: 他幫抱著嬰兒的女士扶著門。

ph.ex: I want to learn Japanese.
ph.exzh: 我想學日文。

b.title: Why Kindness Is Contagious
text: World Kindness Day, held every November 13, was introduced in 1998 by the World Kindness Movement, a group that grew out of a conference in Tokyo the year before.
The idea is simple: to encourage people everywhere to notice others and do something good for them, without expecting anything back.

Research suggests that kindness benefits the giver as well as the receiver. Studies have found that people who spend money or time on others often report feeling happier than those who spend it only on themselves.
Kindness also appears to be contagious. In experiments, people who received help were more likely to help someone else later, creating a chain of generosity.
Small acts count. Including a lonely classmate, writing a thank-you note or simply listening carefully can change someone's day.
Of course, kindness is not the same as always saying yes. Being kind sometimes means being honest or standing up for someone who is being treated unfairly.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: World Kindness Day began at a conference held in Tokyo in 1998.
Kind people should always say yes when others ask for help.
Spending money on others is the very best way to be happy.
Kindness helps both giver and receiver and can spread to others.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；第二項是細節；第三、四項與文意不符或太絕對。

q.q: Where did the World Kindness Movement grow out of?
opts: A school project in Taiwan
A science study in America
A conference in Tokyo
A UN meeting in 1998
q.why: 第一段：grew out of a conference in Tokyo。

q.q: What did experiments show about people who received help?
opts: They felt they had to pay the helper back soon
They were more likely to help someone else later
They became less independent and more needy
They quickly forgot the help they were given
q.why: 第四段：more likely to help someone else later。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “contagious” means ___.
opts: able to spread from person to person
harmful to your health over time
easy to forget after a few days
only ever shared with close friends
q.why: contagious = 會傳染的。

q.q: What does the last paragraph suggest?
opts: Kind people should always avoid disagreeing
Real kindness can include honesty and standing up
Kindness means doing whatever others ask you
Real kindness means never saying anything honest
q.why: 最後一段：Being kind sometimes means being honest or standing up for someone。

q.q: A classmate is being laughed at by a group. According to the text, which action is the kindest?
opts: Laugh a little so that the group does not target you
Ignore it completely, because it is not your problem
Tell the classmate later on that you felt sorry for them
Calmly tell them to stop and stand with the classmate
q.why: 最後一段：仁慈有時是挺身為受到不公平對待的人說話。

tr.en: The idea is simple: to encourage people everywhere to notice others and do something good for them, without expecting anything back.
tr.zh: 這個想法很簡單：鼓勵各地的人留意身邊的人，為他們做點好事，而且不求回報。

tr.en: Research suggests that kindness benefits the giver as well as the receiver.
tr.zh: 研究顯示，善意不只對接受的人有好處，對付出的人也有好處。

tr.en: In experiments, people who received help were more likely to help someone else later, creating a chain of generosity.
tr.zh: 在實驗中，得到幫助的人後來比較可能去幫助別人，形成一條慷慨的連鎖。

tz: 世界善良日在每年 11 月 13 日舉行，由「世界善良運動」在 1998 年發起；這個組織源自前一年在東京召開的一場會議。
這個構想很簡單：鼓勵世界各地的人留意身邊的人，為他們做一件好事，而且不期待任何回報。
研究顯示，善良對給予者和接受者都有好處。研究發現，把錢或時間花在別人身上的人，往往比只花在自己身上的人覺得更快樂。
善良似乎也會傳染。在實驗中，曾經受到幫助的人，之後比較可能去幫助別人，形成一條慷慨的連鎖。
小小的舉動也很重要。邀請一位孤單的同學加入、寫一張感謝卡，或只是用心聆聽，都可能改變一個人的一天。
當然，善良不等於永遠說「好」。善良有時代表要說實話，或替受到不公平對待的人挺身而出。

ph.ex: She helps her neighbours without expecting anything back.
ph.exzh: 她幫助鄰居，從不求回報。

ph.ex: She plays the piano as well as the violin.
ph.exzh: 她會彈鋼琴，也會拉小提琴。

ph.ex: You are more likely to remember words you use.
ph.exzh: 你比較可能記住自己用過的單字。

ph.zh: 讓某人的一天變得不一樣
ph.ex: A kind word can change someone's day.
ph.exzh: 一句溫暖的話能讓某人的一天變得不一樣。

ph.ex: It takes courage to stand up for a friend.
ph.exzh: 挺身為朋友說話需要勇氣。

c.title: The Quiet Economics of Kindness
text: Kindness is easy to dismiss as sentimental, a soft virtue for greeting cards. World Kindness Day, observed every November 13 since the World Kindness Movement proposed it in 1998, invites a more serious look.

Behavioural research has repeatedly found that prosocial spending — devoting money or time to others — is associated with greater wellbeing than equivalent spending on oneself. The effect appears across very different cultures, which suggests it is not merely a local custom.

Kindness also seems to propagate. Experiments on 'paying it forward' show that recipients of generosity are more inclined to extend it to strangers, so that a single act can ripple outward through a network of people who never meet.
None of this makes kindness simple. Genuine kindness can demand courage: telling an uncomfortable truth, refusing to join in mockery, or defending someone whom the group has decided to exclude.
Seen this way, kindness is less a mood than a practice — an everyday choice that, multiplied across a community, quietly shapes whether people feel safe enough to trust one another.
gloss: 多愁善感的；感情用事的

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Kindness is, above all, about spending money on other people.
Kindness is a nice but unimportant feeling that fades after a day or two.
Kindness is a pleasant feeling rather than something we do.
Kindness is a serious daily practice that builds trust in communities.
q.why: 主旨：善意是值得認真看待的日常實踐。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “propagate” means ___.
opts: to measure
to spread
to reward
to decrease
q.why: propagate = 傳播。

q.q: Why does the writer mention that the effect appears across different cultures?
opts: The kindness–happiness link is not just a local custom
Every culture practises kindness in the same way
Kindness makes people happy only in the country where it began
It explains where the Kindness Movement began
q.why: 第二段：not merely a local custom。

q.q: How does the writer treat the view that kindness is “sentimental”?
opts: As fully accurate
As a scientific finding
As a view worth challenging
As the writer's own belief
q.why: 作者先提出這種看法，再要求 a more serious look。

q.q: How does the final paragraph redefine kindness?
opts: As a kind of spending on other people
As a reaction to the kindness of others
As a personality trait you are born with
As a practice and choice, not just a mood
q.why: 結尾：kindness is less a mood than a practice。

q.q: A school wants to measure whether a “Kindness Week” worked. Which measure fits the writer's view best?
opts: Surveying whether students feel safer and trust more
Counting how many kindness posters students made
Checking how much money students donated that week
Asking teachers which students are the nicest ones
q.why: 結尾：善意累積起來會影響人們是否覺得安全、能互相信任。

tz: 善良很容易被當成濫情而不當一回事，好像只是賀卡上的一種溫柔美德。世界善良日自 1998 年由「世界善良運動」提出後，每年 11 月 13 日舉行，它邀請我們更認真地看待善良。
行為研究一再發現，「利社會支出」——把金錢或時間投入在別人身上——比同樣花在自己身上，更能帶來幸福感。這個效應出現在差異很大的各種文化中，表示它不只是某個地方的習俗。
善良似乎也會擴散。關於「把善意傳下去」的實驗顯示，受過別人慷慨對待的人，比較願意把這份慷慨延伸到陌生人身上；於是一個舉動，就能在一群彼此從未見過面的人之間，像漣漪般向外擴散。
但這一切並不代表善良很簡單。真正的善良可能需要勇氣：說出令人不自在的實話、拒絕加入嘲笑，或為團體決定排擠的人辯護。
從這個角度看，善良與其說是一種心情，不如說是一種實踐——一個每天的選擇；當它在一個社群裡累積起來，就會默默決定人們是否覺得足夠安全，能夠彼此信任。

ph.ex: This recipe is easy to follow.
ph.exzh: 這個食譜很容易照著做。

ph.ex: Exercise is associated with better sleep.
ph.exzh: 運動和睡得比較好有關。

ph.ex: People are more inclined to help when they feel happy.
ph.exzh: 人們心情好的時候，比較願意幫忙。

ph.ex: She refused to give up.
ph.exzh: 她拒絕放棄。

ph.ex: Everyone joined in the song.
ph.exzh: 大家都跟著一起唱。

ph.ex: Seen this way, mistakes are chances to learn.
ph.exzh: 從這個角度看，錯誤是學習的機會。

discuss: Describe a time when someone was kind to you. How did it make you feel?
The text says kindness can mean standing up for someone. Why can that be difficult?
Plan one small act of kindness you could do at school this week. What will you do?

topic: World Diabetes Day and the Discovery of Insulin
zh: 世界糖尿病日：胰島素的發現
src: WHO · Nature · The Washington Post

a.title: The Medicine That Saved Millions
text: November 14 is World Diabetes Day. Diabetes is an illness where there is too much sugar in the blood.
Our bodies need insulin to use sugar for energy. Some people's bodies cannot make enough insulin.
Long ago, children with this kind of diabetes did not live long.
In 1921, two scientists in Canada, Frederick Banting and Charles Best, found a way to make insulin as a medicine.
In 1922, a sick boy of 14 got the first shots. He got better! Banting was born on November 14, so the day is in his honour.
Today, millions of people use insulin. Healthy food and exercise also help people stay well.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: Diabetes and the discovery of insulin
The life of the doctor Frederick Banting
Why too much sugar is bad for children
How to exercise to stay fit and healthy
q.why: 全文講糖尿病與胰島素；其他是細節。

q.q: What is diabetes?
opts: An illness caused by eating too little sugar
An illness with too much sugar in the blood
An illness that only young children can get
A kind of medicine that is made from sugar
q.why: 第一段：too much sugar in the blood。
