q.q: Why is World Diabetes Day on November 14?
opts: It is the day insulin was discovered
It is the day the first patient got better
It is the day the medicine was sold
It is Banting's birthday
q.why: 第五段：Banting was born on November 14。

q.q: In the text, “illness” means ___.
opts: a kind of medicine
a healthy habit
a sickness
a scientist
q.why: illness = 疾病。

q.q: Why was insulin such an important discovery?
opts: Before it, children with this diabetes died young
It made sugar much cheaper for everyone to buy
It cured diabetes completely and forever
It replaced the need for healthy food and exercise
q.why: 第三段：children … did not live long——胰島素救了他們。

q.q: Your friend says, “If there is insulin, I don't need to care about healthy food.” What does the text suggest?
opts: He is right — insulin solves every problem by itself
Only adults need to think about eating healthy food
Exercise matters more than insulin for everyone
Healthy food and exercise also help people stay well
q.why: 最後一段：Healthy food and exercise also help people stay well。

gt.en: Diabetes is an illness where there is too much sugar in the blood.
gt.zh: 糖尿病是一種血液中糖分太多的疾病。

gt.en: Our bodies need insulin to use sugar for energy.
gt.zh: 我們的身體需要胰島素，才能把糖變成能量來用。

gt.en: Healthy food and exercise also help people stay well.
gt.zh: 健康的飲食和運動也能幫助人們保持健康。

tz: 11 月 14 日是世界糖尿病日。糖尿病是一種血液裡有太多糖分的疾病。
我們的身體需要胰島素，才能把糖分用來產生能量。有些人的身體沒辦法製造足夠的胰島素。
很久以前，得到這種糖尿病的孩子活不了多久。
1921 年，加拿大的兩位科學家——弗雷德里克・班廷和查爾斯・貝斯特——找到了把胰島素做成藥物的方法。
1922 年，一個 14 歲生病的男孩打了第一批針，他好轉了！班廷是在 11 月 14 日出生的，所以這一天是為了紀念他。
今天有數百萬人使用胰島素。健康的飲食和運動也能幫助人們保持健康。

ph.ex: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
ph.exzh: 太多糖對牙齒不好。

ph.ex: We must find a way to save water.
ph.exzh: 我們必須找到節約用水的方法。

ph.ex: I had a cold, but I'm getting better.
ph.exzh: 我感冒了，但正在好轉。

ph.ex: The library was named in his honour.
ph.exzh: 這座圖書館是為了紀念他而命名的。

b.title: A Discovery That Changed a Death Sentence
text: World Diabetes Day is held each year on November 14, the birthday of Frederick Banting, the Canadian doctor who helped discover insulin.

Diabetes affects how the body controls blood sugar. In type 1 diabetes, the body cannot produce insulin, the hormone that lets cells absorb sugar. In the more common type 2, the body does not use insulin properly.
Before the 1920s, a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes was essentially a death sentence, especially for children.

In 1921, at the University of Toronto, Banting and his young assistant Charles Best managed to extract insulin. In January 1922, a 14-year-old boy named Leonard Thompson became the first person to receive an injection, and his condition dramatically improved.
Banting shared the 1923 Nobel Prize in Medicine. Remarkably, the discoverers sold the patent to the university for just one dollar each, hoping the medicine would be affordable.
Today more than half a billion adults live with diabetes. Doctors stress that regular exercise and a healthy diet can lower the risk of type 2.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Banting and Best sold the insulin patent for just one dollar each.
Insulin made a deadly illness treatable, and diabetes is still a major issue.
Insulin has now cured diabetes, so it is no longer a serious health issue anywhere.
Leonard Thompson, aged 14, was the first person to receive insulin.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: What is the difference between type 1 and type 2 diabetes?
opts: Type 1 affects only adults; type 2, only children
Type 1 is caused by sugar; type 2 by insulin
Type 1 makes no insulin; type 2 uses it poorly
Type 1 can now be cured, but type 2 cannot
q.why: 第二段說明兩型差異。

q.q: How much did the discoverers sell the patent for?
opts: One dollar each
One thousand dollars each
Nothing; they gave it away
Enough to build a hospital
q.why: 第五段：for just one dollar each。

q.q: In paragraph 3, a “diagnosis” is ___.
opts: a treatment that cures an illness
a medicine that a doctor gives a patient
a patient's recovery after illness
a doctor's identification of an illness
q.why: diagnosis = 診斷。

q.q: Why did the discoverers sell the patent so cheaply?
opts: They wanted the medicine to be affordable
They were not sure the medicine would work
The university paid them in other ways
They wanted to avoid paying high taxes
q.why: 第五段：hoping the medicine would be affordable。

q.q: A medicine company wants to sell a new life-saving drug at a very high price. Which argument from the text could be used AGAINST this?
opts: Insulin was first discovered at a Canadian university
Insulin was first given to a 14-year-old boy in a Toronto hospital
Insulin's discoverers sold the patent cheaply for patients
Exercise lowers the risk of getting type 2 diabetes
q.why: 以一美元出售專利、讓藥物負擔得起的例子，可用來反對高價。

tr.en: In type 1 diabetes, the body cannot produce insulin, the hormone that lets cells absorb sugar.
tr.zh: 在第一型糖尿病中，身體無法製造胰島素——一種讓細胞能吸收糖分的荷爾蒙。

tr.en: Before the 1920s, a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes was essentially a death sentence, especially for children.
tr.zh: 在 1920 年代以前，被診斷出第一型糖尿病幾乎等於被判了死刑，對孩子來說尤其如此。

tr.en: In 1921, at the University of Toronto, Banting and his young assistant Charles Best managed to extract insulin.
tr.zh: 1921 年，在多倫多大學，班廷和他年輕的助手查爾斯・貝斯特成功地提取出胰島素。

tz: 世界糖尿病日訂在每年 11 月 14 日，也就是協助發現胰島素的加拿大醫生弗雷德里克・班廷的生日。
糖尿病會影響身體控制血糖的方式。第一型糖尿病是身體無法製造胰島素——一種讓細胞吸收糖分的荷爾蒙。比較常見的第二型，則是身體無法正常利用胰島素。
在 1920 年代以前，被診斷出第一型糖尿病幾乎等於被判了死刑，對孩子來說尤其如此。
1921 年，在多倫多大學，班廷和他年輕的助手查爾斯・貝斯特成功萃取出胰島素。1922 年 1 月，一個名叫李奧納德・湯普森的 14 歲男孩成為第一個接受注射的人，他的病情大幅好轉。
班廷與人共同獲得 1923 年的諾貝爾醫學獎。值得注意的是，發現者們只以每人一美元的價格把專利賣給了大學，希望這種藥物大家都買得起。
今天有超過五億名成年人患有糖尿病。醫生強調，規律運動和健康飲食可以降低罹患第二型糖尿病的風險。

ph.ex: The concert will be held in the school hall.
ph.exzh: 音樂會將在學校禮堂舉行。

ph.ex: Her research helped discover a new medicine.
ph.exzh: 她的研究協助發現了一種新藥。

ph.ex: He managed to finish the race.
ph.exzh: 他設法跑完了比賽。

ph.zh: 等於宣判死刑、絕望的結局
ph.ex: Long ago, this illness was a death sentence.
ph.exzh: 很久以前，得到這種病就等於被判了死刑。

ph.ex: Washing your hands lowers the risk of getting sick.
ph.exzh: 洗手能降低生病的風險。

c.title: From Death Sentence to Daily Routine
text: Few medical breakthroughs have been as immediate in their effect as insulin. Before 1922, children diagnosed with what is now called type 1 diabetes faced a grim prognosis; the most doctors could offer was a starvation diet that prolonged life by months.

The turning point came at the University of Toronto, where the surgeon Frederick Banting, born on November 14, 1891, and the student Charles Best extracted the hormone from animal pancreases in 1921. Within weeks of the first injections, emaciated patients regained their strength.

The story contains a striking gesture of idealism. Banting and his colleagues sold the patent to the university for a nominal one dollar each, wanting the treatment to belong to humanity rather than to profit.

A century later that ideal sits uneasily with reality. In some countries insulin remains expensive enough that patients ration it, and the global prevalence of diabetes, now exceeding half a billion adults, is rising fastest where healthcare is weakest.
World Diabetes Day, observed on Banting's birthday, therefore honours a discovery while posing an unfinished question: whether a cure that exists can reach everyone who needs it.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Insulin saved lives, but its founders' ideal of access is unfulfilled.
Insulin saved lives, and today every patient in the world can easily afford it.
Banting was the most important scientist of the twentieth century.
Diabetes is rising today mainly because of unhealthy modern diets.
q.why: 主旨：胰島素救命，但人人可得的理想仍未實現。

q.q: In paragraph 3, a “nominal” price is ___.
opts: far higher than most people can pay
very small, almost symbolic
set by the government
higher than expected
q.why: nominal = 象徵性的。

q.q: What does it mean that some patients “ration” insulin?
opts: They store it carefully in the fridge
They share it with other family members
They take it only at certain times of day
They use less than they need because of cost
q.why: 第四段：因為太貴，病人只好省著用。

q.q: How does the writer view the gap between the discoverers' ideal and today's reality?
opts: Optimistic that it is already solved
Indifferent
Concerned and critical
Amused
q.why: sits uneasily with reality——憂心且帶批判。

q.q: What does the final sentence add?
opts: A summary of how insulin works
An unfinished question about access
A call to give Banting more credit
A prediction that diabetes will end
q.why: 結尾提出未解問題：治療能否送到每個需要的人。

q.q: Which statistic would BEST support the writer's concern in paragraph 4?
opts: The year insulin was first used on a patient
How many Nobel Prizes Canadians have won
How many patients skip doses because of cost
How much sugar is in a can of soda
q.why: 第四段的擔憂是價格讓病人省著用；因費用而減量的病人數最能支持。

tz: 很少有醫學突破的效果像胰島素一樣立竿見影。在 1922 年以前，被診斷出現在所謂第一型糖尿病的孩子，前景十分黯淡；醫生最多只能提供一種飢餓療法，把生命延長幾個月。
轉捩點出現在多倫多大學：1891 年 11 月 14 日出生的外科醫生弗雷德里克・班廷，和學生查爾斯・貝斯特，在 1921 年從動物的胰臟中萃取出這種荷爾蒙。首批注射後短短幾週內，原本骨瘦如柴的病人就恢復了體力。
這個故事裡有一個令人印象深刻的理想主義舉動。班廷和同事以每人象徵性的一美元，把專利賣給大學，希望這種治療屬於全人類，而不是用來牟利。
一個世紀後，這份理想與現實格格不入。在某些國家，胰島素仍然貴到病人只能省著用；而全球糖尿病的盛行率——如今已超過五億名成年人——在醫療最薄弱的地方上升得最快。
因此，在班廷生日舉行的世界糖尿病日，一方面紀念一項發現，一方面也提出一個尚未解決的問題：一種已經存在的療法，能不能送到每一個需要它的人手上。

ph.ex: After a week in bed, she slowly regained her strength.
ph.exzh: 臥床一週後，她慢慢恢復了體力。

ph.ex: Moving to Taipei was a turning point in her life.
ph.exzh: 搬到台北是她人生的轉捩點。

ph.ex: Within weeks of joining the club, she made new friends.
ph.exzh: 加入社團後幾週內，她就交到了新朋友。

ph.ex: He chose to walk rather than drive.
ph.exzh: 他選擇走路，而不是開車。

ph.ex: His words sit uneasily with his actions.
ph.exzh: 他說的話和他的行為格格不入。

ph.zh: 送到每個需要的人手上
ph.ex: Clean water must reach everyone who needs it.
ph.exzh: 乾淨的水必須送到每個需要的人手上。

discuss: Banting sold the patent for one dollar. Should important medicines be cheap for everyone? Why or why not?
What healthy habits can students build to lower the risk of illnesses like type 2 diabetes?
How much sugar do you think you eat in a day? Where does most of it come from?

topic: Pandora's Box
zh: 潘朵拉的盒子
src: Hesiod · BBC · The Guardian

a.title: Don't Open It!
text: This is a story from ancient Greece. Long ago, a man named Prometheus took fire from the gods and gave it to people.
Zeus, the king of the gods, was very angry. He made the first woman, Pandora, and sent her to Earth.
The gods gave Pandora a jar and said, “Never open it.”
But Pandora was curious. One day, she opened the jar a little.
Out flew sickness, sadness, and all the troubles of the world! She quickly closed it, but only one thing was left inside: hope.
Today, people say “open Pandora's box” when one small action causes many problems.

q.q: What is this story mainly about?
opts: How Prometheus took fire from the gods
Why Zeus became the king of all the gods
How Pandora let troubles into the world
Why hope is the most important thing of all
q.why: 故事主線是潘朵拉打開罐子；其他是背景或細節。

q.q: Why was Zeus angry?
opts: Pandora opened the jar without asking him
People had forgotten to thank the gods
Pandora refused to go down to Earth
Prometheus gave the gods' fire to people
q.why: 第一、二段：Prometheus took fire from the gods。

q.q: What was left inside the jar?
opts: Hope
Sickness
Sadness
Fire
q.why: 第五段：only one thing was left inside: hope。

q.q: In the text, “curious” means ___.
opts: not caring about anything at all
wanting to know about something
afraid of something in the dark
angry about something unfair
q.why: curious = 好奇的。

q.q: What does “open Pandora's box” mean today?
opts: To find something very valuable inside a box
To give someone a present they really want
To do something small that causes many problems
To keep a secret safely locked away
q.why: 最後一段：one small action causes many problems。

q.q: Which situation is the BEST example of “opening Pandora's box”?
opts: Tom opens a birthday present and is very happy with it
Tom shares one secret, and soon rumours and fights start
Tom finds the keys he had lost inside an old box
Tom closes the window before the rain starts to fall
q.why: 一個小舉動引發一連串問題——分享祕密後謠言和爭吵接連發生。

gt.en: This is a story from ancient Greece.
gt.zh: 這是一個來自古希臘的故事。

gt.en: Zeus, the king of the gods, was very angry.
gt.zh: 眾神之王宙斯非常生氣。

gt.en: The gods gave Pandora a jar and said, “Never open it.”
gt.zh: 眾神給了潘朵拉一個罐子，並說：「永遠不要打開它。」

gt.en: One day, she opened the jar a little.
gt.zh: 有一天，她把罐子打開了一點點。

tz: 這是一個來自古希臘的故事。很久以前，一個名叫普羅米修斯的人從眾神那裡拿走了火，把它送給人類。
眾神之王宙斯非常生氣。他造出了第一個女人潘朵拉，把她送到人間。
眾神給了潘朵拉一個罐子，並且說：「永遠不要打開它。」
但是潘朵拉很好奇。有一天，她把罐子打開了一點點。
疾病、悲傷和世界上所有的麻煩都飛了出來！她趕緊把罐子蓋上，但裡面只剩下一樣東西：希望。
今天，當一個小小的舉動引發許多問題時，人們就會說「打開潘朵拉的盒子」。

ph.ex: Long ago, people did not have phones.
ph.exzh: 很久以前，人們沒有手機。

ph.ex: She gave her old books to the library.
ph.exzh: 她把舊書捐給了圖書館。

ph.ex: When I opened the box, a moth flew out.
ph.exzh: 我一打開盒子，一隻飛蛾就飛了出來。

ph.ex: One small action can change someone's day.
ph.exzh: 一個小小的舉動可以改變一個人的一天。

b.title: The Jar That Changed the World
text: In Greek mythology, the story of Pandora explains how suffering entered human life. It was first written down by the poet Hesiod around 700 BC.

When the Titan Prometheus stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans, Zeus decided to punish humankind. He ordered Hephaestus, the god of craftsmen, to shape the first woman, Pandora, out of clay.
Each god gave her a gift — beauty, charm, skill — and Zeus gave her a sealed jar, warning that it must never be opened. Pandora was sent to marry Epimetheus, Prometheus's less careful brother.
Overcome by curiosity, Pandora lifted the lid. Out rushed disease, hard work, sorrow and countless other evils, which spread across the world. Only Hope remained trapped beneath the rim.
Interestingly, the original story describes a large storage jar, not a box. The word 'box' comes from a translation mistake made by a scholar in the 1500s.
Today the phrase 'opening Pandora's box' describes an action that releases a series of unexpected problems.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Hephaestus, the craftsman god, made the first woman, Pandora, out of clay.
The word 'box' came from a translation mistake made in the 1500s.
The myth explains how suffering entered the world, and lives on in a phrase.
Zeus punished Prometheus harshly for stealing fire from the gods.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: Who shaped Pandora out of clay?
opts: Prometheus
Hephaestus
Zeus
Epimetheus
q.why: 第二段：He ordered Hephaestus … to shape the first woman。

q.q: Why do we say 'box' instead of 'jar'?
opts: Hesiod wrote 'box' in his original poem
The jar was later replaced by a box
Zeus himself called it a box
A translation mistake in the 1500s
q.why: 第五段：a translation mistake made by a scholar in the 1500s。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “sealed” means ___.
opts: tightly closed
beautifully decorated
very heavy
already empty
q.why: sealed = 密封的。

q.q: Why was Pandora sent to Epimetheus instead of Prometheus?
opts: He was the brother who had stolen the fire
He was the less careful brother, likely to accept
Prometheus had refused to take any gift from Zeus at all
He was the strongest of all the gods
q.why: 第三段：Prometheus's less careful brother——比較容易上當。

q.q: A website says: “In the ancient Greek story, Pandora opened a box.” Based on the text, how accurate is this?
opts: Partly wrong — the original story has a jar, not a box
Partly wrong — the original story has a basket, not a box
Completely wrong — Pandora never opened anything
Partly wrong — it was Epimetheus who opened it
q.why: 第五段：原文是大儲物罐，「盒子」是 1500 年代的翻譯錯誤。

tr.en: In Greek mythology, the story of Pandora explains how suffering entered human life.
tr.zh: 在希臘神話中，潘朵拉的故事解釋了苦難是如何進入人類生活的。

tr.en: When the Titan Prometheus stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans, Zeus decided to punish humankind.
tr.zh: 當泰坦神普羅米修斯從眾神那裡偷走火、交給人類時，宙斯決定懲罰人類。

tr.en: Today the phrase 'opening Pandora's box' describes an action that releases a series of unexpected problems.
tr.zh: 今天，「打開潘朵拉的盒子」這個片語，用來形容一個引發一連串意外問題的行為。

tz: 在希臘神話中，潘朵拉的故事解釋了苦難如何進入人類的生活。它最早由詩人赫西俄德在大約西元前 700 年寫下。
泰坦神普羅米修斯從眾神那裡偷了火、送給人類之後，宙斯決定懲罰人類。他命令工匠之神赫菲斯托斯，用黏土塑造出第一個女人——潘朵拉。
每位神都送她一份禮物——美貌、魅力、技藝——而宙斯給了她一個封住的罐子，警告她絕對不能打開。潘朵拉被送去嫁給普羅米修斯那位比較不謹慎的弟弟——厄庇墨透斯。
潘朵拉忍不住好奇，掀開了蓋子。疾病、辛勞、哀傷和無數其他災禍衝了出來，散布到全世界。只有「希望」被困在罐口下方，留了下來。
有趣的是，原本的故事描述的是一個大型的儲物罐，而不是盒子。「盒子」這個詞，來自一位學者在 1500 年代的翻譯錯誤。
今天，「打開潘朵拉的盒子」這句話，用來形容一個引發一連串意想不到問題的舉動。

ph.ex: The old story was written down in 1900.
ph.exzh: 這個古老的故事在 1900 年被記錄下來。

ph.ex: He made a boat out of paper.
ph.exzh: 他用紙做了一艘船。

ph.ex: She was overcome by sadness when her dog died.
ph.exzh: 她的狗死去時，她悲痛不已。

ph.ex: The news spread across the school in minutes.
ph.exzh: 這個消息幾分鐘內就傳遍了全校。

ph.ex: The word 'tea' comes from Chinese.
ph.exzh: 「tea」這個字源自中文。

c.title: The Puzzle of Hope
text: The tale of Pandora, preserved in the poems of Hesiod from around 700 BC, is usually told as a simple warning against curiosity. Read closely, it is stranger and more troubling than that.

Zeus, enraged that Prometheus had given fire to humanity, devised a punishment disguised as a gift: Pandora, fashioned from clay by Hephaestus and adorned by every god. With her came a sealed jar, a pithos for storing grain or oil, which centuries later a Renaissance translator rendered as a 'box', fixing the image in European imagination.
When Pandora lifted the lid, disease, toil and grief escaped into a world that had previously known none of them. Only Elpis, usually translated as Hope, stayed inside.

That detail has puzzled readers ever since. Is hope a blessing preserved for humanity, or simply one more evil, a deceptive expectation that prolongs our suffering? The text never settles the question.

Perhaps that ambiguity is the myth's enduring power: it does not tell us whether to cling to hope or distrust it, only that, among all the troubles of the world, it is the one that remains closest at hand.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: The myth's single lesson is that curiosity is always dangerous.
It is more than a warning about curiosity; its unresolved hope endures.
It is mainly a warning that curiosity, especially in women, always causes harm.
The myth matters today mainly because of the translation mistake.
q.why: 主旨：不只警告好奇心，「希望」意義未定才是它歷久不衰的力量。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “ambiguity” means ___.
opts: having more than one possible meaning
a clear and simple moral lesson
a strong and lasting feeling of hope
an old translation of a Greek poem
q.why: ambiguity = 模稜兩可。

q.q: Why have readers been puzzled that Hope stayed in the jar?
opts: Hesiod forgot to explain why the jar was closed
Hope is clearly the best gift, so there is nothing to be puzzled about
The jar was simply too small for hope to escape
It is unclear if hope is a blessing or another evil
q.why: 第四段：Is hope a blessing … or simply one more evil?

q.q: How does the writer approach the myth?
opts: Critically, calling it a sexist story
Simply, retelling it for children
Thoughtfully, exploring its open questions
Doubtfully, questioning whether it is really Greek
q.why: 作者細讀並探討開放問題。

q.q: What role does paragraph 2's note about the 'box' play?
opts: It shows how a translation shaped the familiar image
It introduces the main argument about hope
It describes how Prometheus was punished
It proves that Hesiod's original poem is now lost forever
q.why: 第二段說明翻譯如何塑造了「盒子」的印象。

q.q: Which real-life example best illustrates hope as a “deceptive expectation that prolongs our suffering”?
opts: Someone studies hard for weeks, hoping to pass an exam
Someone keeps trying a new medicine that doctors have shown really works
Someone keeps buying lottery tickets, sure they'll win next time
A team practises all summer, hoping to win next season
q.why: 沒有依據、反覆期待中獎而持續花錢，最符合「延長痛苦的欺騙性期待」。

tz: 潘朵拉的故事保存在赫西俄德約西元前 700 年的詩作中，通常被當成一個簡單的警告，告誡人們不要好奇。但仔細閱讀，它比這更奇特，也更令人不安。
宙斯因普羅米修斯把火給了人類而大怒，設計了一個偽裝成禮物的懲罰：潘朵拉——由赫菲斯托斯用黏土塑造、再由每一位神妝點而成。和她一起來的，是一個封住的罐子，一種用來儲存穀物或油的大陶甕（pithos）；幾個世紀後，一位文藝復興時期的譯者把它譯成「盒子」，這個形象從此固定在歐洲人的想像中。
當潘朵拉掀開蓋子，疾病、勞苦和悲傷逃進了一個原本對它們一無所知的世界。只有 Elpis——通常譯為「希望」——留在裡面。
這個細節從此一直困擾著讀者。希望是為人類保留下來的祝福，還是只是另一種災禍——一種延長我們痛苦的虛幻期待？原文從來沒有給出答案。
也許正是這種模稜兩可，造就了這則神話歷久不衰的力量：它沒有告訴我們該緊抓希望還是懷疑它，只告訴我們，在世上所有的麻煩之中，希望是離我們最近的那一個。

ph.ex: The story is often told as a lesson about honesty.
ph.exzh: 這個故事常被當成誠實的教訓來講。

ph.ex: Read closely, the poem is quite sad.
ph.exzh: 仔細讀的話，這首詩其實很悲傷。

ph.ex: The spy entered the city disguised as a farmer.
ph.exzh: 間諜偽裝成農夫進了城。

ph.ex: She has loved music ever since she was a child.
ph.exzh: 她從小就一直熱愛音樂。

ph.ex: The test results did not settle the question.
ph.exzh: 測試結果並沒有讓問題有定論。

ph.ex: He clings to the hope that his team will win.
ph.exzh: 他仍抱著他的隊伍會贏的希望。

ph.ex: Keep a dictionary close at hand.
ph.exzh: 把字典放在手邊。

discuss: Is curiosity a good thing or a dangerous thing? Give an example.
Why do you think Hope stayed in the jar? Is hope a gift or a problem?
Can you think of a real-life situation where one small action 'opened Pandora's box'?

topic: 11/11/1918: Why the World Wears Poppies
zh: 一戰停戰日：為什麼人們戴上罌粟花？
src: BBC · TIME · The Washington Post

a.title: The Day the Guns Stopped
text: More than 100 years ago, there was a terrible war in Europe. It was called the First World War.
Millions of soldiers died. Many families lost fathers, sons, and brothers.
On November 11, 1918, at 11 o'clock in the morning, the fighting finally stopped.
Today, people in many countries remember this day. At 11 o'clock, they stand quietly for two minutes.
Many people wear a red poppy flower. Poppies grew on the fields where soldiers fought.
The poppy helps us remember the people who died, and it reminds us that peace is precious.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: Why red poppies grew on the old battlefields
The end of the First World War and how we remember it
How millions of soldiers died in Europe
How the First World War started in Europe in the year 1914
q.why: 全文講一戰結束與紀念方式；其他是細節。

q.q: When did the fighting stop?
opts: At midnight on November 11, 1918
At 11 o'clock on November 11, 1919
At 11 o'clock on November 11, 1918
At 11 o'clock on November 1, 1918
q.why: 第三段：On November 11, 1918, at 11 o'clock。

q.q: What do people do at 11 o'clock on this day?
opts: They stand quietly for two minutes
They stand quietly for eleven minutes
They plant red poppies
They ring bells for one hour
q.why: 第四段：they stand quietly for two minutes。

q.q: In the text, “peace” means ___.
opts: a time to remember soldiers
a kind of red flower
a quiet place
a time without war
q.why: peace = 和平。

q.q: Why is the poppy used to remember soldiers?
opts: Poppies grew where the soldiers fought
Poppies were the soldiers' favourite flower
Poppies are red, like many national flags
Soldiers planted poppies before the war
q.why: 第五段：Poppies grew on the fields where soldiers fought。

q.q: Your school wants to remember the First World War on November 11. Which activity fits the text best?
opts: A big party with loud music and fireworks
A sports day with prizes for the winners
A sale of toy soldiers and war games
A two-minute silence at 11 and paper poppies
q.why: 文中的紀念方式是十一點默哀兩分鐘、戴罌粟花。

gt.en: More than 100 years ago, there was a terrible war in Europe.
gt.zh: 一百多年前，歐洲發生了一場可怕的戰爭。

gt.en: On November 11, 1918, at 11 o'clock in the morning, the fighting finally stopped.
gt.zh: 1918 年 11 月 11 日早上十一點，戰鬥終於停止了。

gt.en: Today, people in many countries remember this day.
gt.zh: 今天，許多國家的人都會紀念這一天。

gt.en: Many people wear a red poppy flower.
gt.zh: 許多人會戴上一朵紅色的罌粟花。

tz: 一百多年前，歐洲發生了一場可怕的戰爭，叫做第一次世界大戰。
數百萬名士兵死去。許多家庭失去了父親、兒子和兄弟。
1918 年 11 月 11 日上午 11 點，戰鬥終於停止了。
今天，許多國家的人都會紀念這一天。在 11 點時，他們會安靜地站立兩分鐘。
很多人會配戴一朵紅色的罌粟花。罌粟花曾長在士兵們作戰的田野上。
罌粟花幫助我們記住死去的人，也提醒我們和平是很珍貴的。

ph.ex: More than 30 students came to the meeting.
ph.exzh: 有超過 30 名學生來開會。

ph.ex: I always drink milk in the morning.
ph.exzh: 我早上總是喝牛奶。

ph.ex: We stood quietly while the music played.
ph.exzh: 音樂播放時，我們安靜地站著。

b.title: The Eleventh Hour of the Eleventh Day
text: At 11 a.m. on November 11, 1918, the guns of the First World War fell silent. Hours earlier, leaders had signed an armistice — an agreement to stop fighting — in a railway carriage in a forest near Compiègne, France.
The war had lasted more than four years and killed around nine million soldiers, along with millions of civilians.
Each year, many countries mark the anniversary. In Britain and the Commonwealth it is called Remembrance Day, in the United States Veterans Day, and in France and Belgium Armistice Day.
At 11 o'clock, many people observe two minutes of silence, a tradition that began in 1919.

The red poppy became the symbol of remembrance because poppies bloomed across the churned-up battlefields of Flanders. A Canadian doctor, John McCrae, wrote a famous poem about them in 1915, and the flower was soon adopted to honour the dead.
The war was once called 'the war to end all wars'. Sadly, it did not — which is one reason people still pause to remember.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The armistice was signed in a railway carriage in a forest near Compiègne.
The First World War killed around nine million soldiers on all sides.
The end of the war on 11 November 1918 is still marked with silence and poppies.
The war ended on 11 November 1918, and remembrance today mainly celebrates the winners.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: Where was the armistice signed?
opts: In a small church in Flanders, Belgium
In a royal palace in central London
In a railway carriage in central London, England
In a railway carriage near Compiègne, France
q.why: 第一段：in a railway carriage in a forest near Compiègne。

q.q: What is the day called in the United States?
opts: Remembrance Day
Veterans Day
Armistice Day
Memorial Day
q.why: 第三段：in the United States Veterans Day。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “civilians” are ___.
opts: people who are not soldiers
soldiers who were injured
leaders who signed the armistice
doctors who helped soldiers
q.why: civilians = 平民。

q.q: Why does the writer say 'sadly, it did not'?
opts: More wars came after it, so it did not end all wars
The armistice was broken by both sides the next day
People soon stopped remembering the war at all
Poppies stopped growing in the fields of Flanders
q.why: 被稱為終結所有戰爭的戰爭，可惜之後仍有戰爭。

q.q: A student says: “Remembrance Day is about celebrating who won the war.” Based on the text, what is the best response?
opts: Yes, it celebrates the victory of the winning countries
It is mainly about the long history of the poppy
It is a special holiday only for soldiers and veterans
It is mainly about remembering the dead and war's cost
q.why: 文中的默哀與罌粟花都是為了紀念逝者，而非慶祝勝利。

tr.en: Hours earlier, leaders had signed an armistice — an agreement to stop fighting — in a railway carriage in a forest near Compiègne, France.
tr.zh: 幾個小時前，領導人們在法國貢比涅附近森林裡的一節火車車廂中，簽署了停戰協定——一份停止戰鬥的協議。

tr.en: The war had lasted more than four years and killed around nine million soldiers, along with millions of civilians.
tr.zh: 這場戰爭持續了四年多，奪走了大約九百萬名士兵的性命，還有數百萬名平民。

tr.en: In Britain and the Commonwealth it is called Remembrance Day, in the United States Veterans Day, and in France and Belgium Armistice Day.
tr.zh: 在英國和大英國協，它叫做陣亡將士紀念日；在美國叫做退伍軍人節；在法國和比利時則叫做停戰紀念日。

tz: 1918 年 11 月 11 日上午 11 點，第一次世界大戰的槍砲聲安靜了下來。幾個小時前，各方領袖在法國貢比涅附近森林裡的一節火車車廂中，簽下了停戰協定——一份停止戰鬥的協議。
這場戰爭持續了四年多，奪走大約九百萬名士兵的生命，還有數百萬名平民喪生。
每年許多國家都會紀念這個日子。在英國和大英國協它叫做「國殤紀念日」，在美國叫做「退伍軍人節」，在法國和比利時則叫做「停戰紀念日」。
在 11 點時，許多人會默哀兩分鐘，這個傳統從 1919 年開始。
紅色罌粟花之所以成為紀念的象徵，是因為罌粟花開滿了法蘭德斯被翻攪得滿目瘡痍的戰場。加拿大醫生約翰・麥克雷在 1915 年寫了一首關於罌粟花的名詩，這種花很快就被用來向陣亡者致敬。
這場戰爭曾被稱為「終結一切戰爭的戰爭」。可惜它並沒有做到——這也是人們至今仍會停下來紀念的原因之一。

ph.ex: The classroom fell silent when the principal walked in.
ph.exzh: 校長走進來時，教室突然安靜下來。

ph.ex: I lost my phone, along with my keys.
ph.exzh: 我把手機弄丟了，連鑰匙也一起不見了。

ph.ex: The whole school observed a minute's silence for the victims.
ph.exzh: 全校為罹難者默哀一分鐘。

ph.ex: A new rule was adopted to keep the library quiet.
ph.exzh: 學校採用了一條新規定，讓圖書館保持安靜。

ph.ex: Sleep is one reason why some students do better in class.
ph.exzh: 睡眠是有些學生上課表現比較好的原因之一。

c.title: Remembering at the Eleventh Hour
text: There is a deliberate symmetry to the moment the First World War ended: the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month of 1918. The armistice had been signed at dawn in a railway carriage near Compiègne, yet fighting continued until the appointed hour, and soldiers were still dying in the final minutes of the war.
The conflict had killed roughly nine million combatants and devastated a generation, and the scale of loss demanded new forms of public mourning.

The two minutes' silence, first observed in 1919, turned private grief into a shared national act. The red poppy, drawn from the flowers that bloomed on the churned soil of Flanders and immortalised in John McCrae's poem, gave remembrance a simple, wearable form.

These rituals were never uncontroversial. Some feared they glorified sacrifice, while others insisted they were acts of mourning, not celebration — a debate that continues whenever symbols of remembrance are politicised.

More than a century on, the ceremonies endure partly because the hope attached to them, that this would be the war to end all wars, proved so tragically mistaken. To remember, in this sense, is not to admire war but to keep alive an argument for peace.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: The ceremonies exist mainly to celebrate the Allies' military victory.
Remembrance endures to mourn and to argue for peace, not to admire war.
The poppy is the single most important symbol of the twentieth century.
The war ended the very moment the armistice was signed at dawn.
q.why: 主旨：紀念儀式是為了哀悼與延續和平的主張。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “immortalised” means ___.
opts: made famous and remembered forever
quickly forgotten after a few short years
made into a political issue
made simple and easy to follow
q.why: immortalised = 使不朽。

q.q: What does the writer suggest by noting soldiers died in the final minutes?
opts: The armistice was signed far too early that morning
Soldiers did not believe that the war was over
Leaders secretly wanted the war to continue
Waiting for a symbolic hour had a real human cost
q.why: 為了等象徵性的時刻，最後幾分鐘仍有人喪命。

q.q: How does the writer present the debate over remembrance rituals?
opts: As a clear and complete win for the critics
As an argument that should simply be ignored
Even-handedly, giving concerns and defences
Only from the side of the rituals' defenders
q.why: 第四段同時呈現兩方看法。

q.q: How does the final paragraph connect to the phrase 'the war to end all wars'?
opts: It says the famous phrase turned out to be correct
Ceremonies endure partly because that hope failed
It explains who first used the famous phrase
It argues that the phrase should be forgotten
q.why: 結尾：the hope … proved so tragically mistaken。

q.q: A politician uses the poppy in an advertisement asking for more military spending. Based on paragraph 4, why might some people object?
opts: Paper poppies are much too expensive to give away
The First World War never really happened at all
Remembrance symbols should not be used to glorify war
Advertisements should never use pictures of flowers
q.why: 第四段：有人擔心紀念象徵被政治化、美化犧牲。

tz: 第一次世界大戰結束的那一刻，有一種刻意安排的對稱：1918 年第十一個月、第十一天、第十一個小時。停戰協定在黎明時分就已在貢比涅附近的火車車廂裡簽署，但戰鬥一直持續到約定的時刻，在戰爭的最後幾分鐘裡仍有士兵死去。
這場衝突奪走了大約九百萬名戰鬥人員的生命，重創了整整一代人；如此巨大的損失，需要新的公共哀悼形式。
1919 年首次舉行的兩分鐘默哀，把個人的悲痛變成全國共同的行動。紅色罌粟花取材自法蘭德斯翻攪過的泥土上綻放的花朵，又因約翰・麥克雷的詩而永垂不朽，讓紀念有了一個簡單、可以配戴在身上的形式。
這些儀式從來不是毫無爭議的。有人擔心它們美化了犧牲，另一些人則堅持它們是哀悼的行為，而不是慶祝——每當紀念的象徵被政治化，這場爭論就會再次出現。
一個多世紀過去了，這些儀式之所以延續下來，部分是因為人們寄託在其中的希望——這將是「終結一切戰爭的戰爭」——結果錯得如此悲慘。從這個意義上說，紀念不是為了崇拜戰爭，而是為了讓支持和平的理由繼續存在。

ph.ex: The fishermen left the harbour at dawn.
ph.exzh: 漁夫們在黎明時分出港。

ph.ex: Our team scored in the final minutes of the game.
ph.exzh: 我們隊在比賽的最後幾分鐘得分。

ph.ex: Writing a diary gives your feelings a clear form.
ph.exzh: 寫日記能讓你的感受有一個清楚的形式。
ph.m: gave remembrance a simple, wearable form

ph.ex: He never won a medal, but in this sense he was a real winner.
ph.exzh: 他從沒拿過獎牌，但從這個意義上說，他是真正的贏家。

ph.ex: Grandma keeps our family recipes alive by cooking them every year.
ph.exzh: 奶奶每年都煮，讓我們家的傳統食譜流傳下去。

ph.ex: More than a century on, people still read his books.
ph.exzh: 一個多世紀後，人們仍在讀他的書。

discuss: Why do you think people still remember a war that ended more than 100 years ago?
How are wars or historical tragedies remembered in Taiwan? Compare with the poppy and two minutes' silence.
Some say remembrance days can glorify war; others say they honour the dead and support peace. What do you think?

topic: International Day for Tolerance
zh: 國際寬容日：不一樣也沒關係
src: UNESCO · VOA · Taipei Times

a.title: Different Is OK
text: November 16 is the International Day for Tolerance. Tolerance means accepting people who are different from you.
People are different in many ways. They speak different languages, eat different food, and believe different things.
Tolerance does not mean you must agree with everyone. It means you treat other people with respect.
UNESCO, part of the United Nations, started this day in 1995.
At school, tolerance can be simple. You can listen to a new classmate, try a new food, or stop a joke that hurts someone.
When people respect each other, schools and cities become safer and happier.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to learn a new language quickly at school
Why UNESCO started this special day in 1995
Agreeing with everyone so that nobody ever argues
Accepting and respecting people who are different
q.why: 全文介紹寬容：接受並尊重和自己不一樣的人。

q.q: What does tolerance mean in the text?
opts: Agreeing with everyone about everything
Speaking many languages very well
Accepting people who are different from you
Believing exactly the same things as others
q.why: 第一段：Tolerance means accepting people who are different from you。

q.q: When did UNESCO start this day?
opts: On November 6
q.why: 第四段：started this day in 1995。

q.q: In the text, “respect” is closest to ___.
opts: a polite and kind way of treating people
a strong feeling of anger towards other people
a special kind of food from far away
a rule that every school must follow
q.why: respect = 尊重。

q.q: Which action shows tolerance, according to the text?
opts: Listening to a new classmate
Making a joke about a new classmate
Only eating your own food
Agreeing with every idea you hear
q.why: 第五段：You can listen to a new classmate。

q.q: A new student in your class speaks Chinese slowly. Some classmates laugh. Based on the text, what is the best thing to do?
opts: Laugh too, so you fit in
Stop the joke and help the new student join in
Tell the new student to speak only English
Ignore it, because tolerance means agreeing with everyone
q.why: 第五段：stop a joke that hurts someone——寬容是尊重與保護別人。

gt.en: Tolerance means accepting people who are different from you.
gt.zh: 寬容的意思是接受和你不一樣的人。

gt.en: It means you treat other people with respect.
gt.zh: 它的意思是你尊重地對待別人。

gt.en: They speak different languages, eat different food, and believe different things.
gt.zh: 他們說不同的語言、吃不同的食物、相信不同的事情。

gt.en: When people respect each other, schools and cities become safer and happier.
gt.zh: 當人們互相尊重，學校和城市會變得更安全、更快樂。

tz: 11 月 16 日是國際寬容日。寬容的意思是接納和你不一樣的人。
人們在很多方面都不一樣。他們說不同的語言、吃不同的食物，也相信不同的事情。
寬容不代表你必須同意每一個人，而是代表你要尊重別人。
聯合國的一部分——聯合國教科文組織（UNESCO）——在 1995 年設立了這個日子。
在學校，寬容可以很簡單。你可以聽新同學說話、嘗試一種新的食物，或阻止一個會傷害別人的玩笑。
當人們彼此尊重，學校和城市都會變得更安全、更快樂。

ph.ex: My hobbies are different from my brother's.
ph.exzh: 我的興趣和我哥哥的不一樣。

ph.ex: I don't always agree with my parents.
ph.exzh: 我不一定都同意爸媽的看法。

ph.ex: We should treat everyone with respect.
ph.exzh: 我們應該尊重每一個人。

ph.ex: Please listen to your classmates when they speak.
ph.exzh: 同學說話時請仔細聽。

b.title: Living Together With Our Differences
text: Every year on November 16, UNESCO marks the International Day for Tolerance. The date recalls a declaration on tolerance that its members adopted in 1995, which the United Nations had named the Year for Tolerance.
The declaration describes tolerance as respect and appreciation for the rich diversity of the world's cultures and ways of being human.
Importantly, tolerance is not the same as giving up your own beliefs. People can disagree strongly and still treat each other fairly, without insults or violence.
Intolerance often grows from ignorance and fear. When people know little about a group, rumours and stereotypes fill the gap, and those can turn into discrimination.
That is why education is seen as the most effective way to prevent intolerance. Learning other people's stories, languages and histories makes differences feel less threatening.
Online life adds a new challenge: angry posts spread quickly, so pausing before sharing has become a small but real act of tolerance.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Tolerance means agreeing with every idea, so arguments should be avoided at school.
Angry online posts are now the main cause of intolerance in the world.
Tolerance respects differences while keeping your beliefs; education helps.
People who disagree strongly cannot really treat each other fairly.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：尊重差異、不必放棄信念，教育能培養寬容。

q.q: What happened in 1995, according to the text?
opts: The United Nations itself was founded that year
The very first online posts appeared that year
UNESCO's members agreed that tolerance should have no limits
UNESCO's members adopted a declaration on tolerance
q.why: 第一段：a declaration on tolerance that its members adopted in 1995。

q.q: Where does intolerance often come from?
opts: Too much education
Ignorance and fear
Learning other languages
Disagreeing politely
q.why: 第四段：Intolerance often grows from ignorance and fear。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “stereotypes” are ___.
opts: fixed, often unfair ideas about a group
true stories about a people's history
laws that protect people from violence
friendly posts shared online by many
q.why: stereotypes = 刻板印象。

q.q: Why does the writer call pausing before sharing an act of tolerance?
opts: Online posts are always false and should be ignored
Sharing posts with others is against the law
It slows the spread of angry posts that hurt others
UNESCO asks people to stop using the internet
q.why: 最後一段：angry posts spread quickly——先停一下能減少傷害。

q.q: A headline says: “Tolerance Means Never Disagreeing.” Based on the text, is it accurate?
opts: Yes — because tolerance means accepting every single idea
No — people can disagree and still treat each other fairly
Yes — because disagreement always leads to violence
No — because the text says tolerance only matters online
q.why: 第三段：People can disagree strongly and still treat each other fairly。

tr.en: Importantly, tolerance is not the same as giving up your own beliefs.
tr.zh: 重要的是，寬容不等於放棄自己的信念。

tr.en: Intolerance often grows from ignorance and fear.
tr.zh: 不寬容常常來自無知和恐懼。

tr.en: Learning other people's stories, languages and histories makes differences feel less threatening.
tr.zh: 了解別人的故事、語言和歷史，會讓差異感覺不那麼具有威脅性。

tz: 每年 11 月 16 日，聯合國教科文組織都會舉行國際寬容日。這個日期是為了紀念它的會員國在 1995 年通過的一份寬容宣言；那一年也被聯合國定為「寬容年」。
這份宣言把寬容描述為：尊重並欣賞世界上豐富多元的文化，以及各種身而為人的方式。
重要的是，寬容不等於放棄你自己的信念。人們可以有強烈的歧見，卻仍然公平對待彼此，不用侮辱或暴力。
不寬容常常是從無知和恐懼中長出來的。當人們對一個群體了解很少，謠言和刻板印象就會填補空白，而這些可能演變成歧視。
這就是為什麼教育被視為預防不寬容最有效的方法。認識別人的故事、語言和歷史，會讓差異顯得不那麼具有威脅性。
網路生活帶來了新的挑戰：憤怒的貼文傳播得很快，所以在轉發前先停一下，已經成為一個小小卻真實的寬容行為。

ph.ex: Your answer is the same as mine.
ph.exzh: 你的答案和我的一樣。

ph.ex: Don't give up your dreams.
ph.exzh: 不要放棄你的夢想。

ph.ex: Many fights grow from small misunderstandings.
ph.exzh: 很多爭吵源自小小的誤會。

ph.ex: Online videos fill the gap when there is no teacher nearby.
ph.exzh: 附近沒有老師時，線上影片能填補這個空缺。

ph.ex: The small argument turned into a big fight.
ph.exzh: 小小的爭執變成了一場大吵。

c.title: The Hard Virtue
text: Tolerance is often mistaken for a soft virtue, a polite shrug in the face of difference. The International Day for Tolerance, held on November 16 to recall UNESCO's 1995 declaration, insists on something more demanding.

Genuine tolerance begins where comfort ends. It is easy to accept people whose habits are merely unfamiliar; it is harder to extend fairness to those whose convictions we find mistaken, even offensive.

Crucially, tolerance is not relativism. It does not require us to pretend that all ideas are equally sound. It requires that we argue with ideas while respecting the dignity and rights of the people who hold them.
Nor is it limitless. A society that tolerates the persecution of minorities in the name of open-mindedness ends up protecting the intolerant at the expense of everyone else.

Education remains the most reliable defence, because prejudice thrives where knowledge is thin. Yet the digital age, which rewards outrage with attention, makes the old discipline of listening before judging more valuable than ever.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Tolerance is demanding: respecting opponents without accepting every idea.
Tolerance is a soft and easy virtue that asks very little of us.
Tolerance means believing that all ideas are equally sound and true.
Tolerance is demanding because it requires us to accept every idea as equally true.
q.why: 主旨：寬容不輕鬆——尊重持不同信念的人，但不是相對主義，也有界線。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “prejudice” means ___.
opts: a careful and patient study of a subject
a kind of law against unfair treatment
an unfair opinion formed without knowledge
a sudden feeling of great joy
q.why: prejudice = 偏見。

q.q: Why does the writer say tolerance is “not limitless”?
opts: People eventually get tired of listening to others
UNESCO has recently changed its official rules
Some ideas are simply too unfamiliar to accept
Tolerating persecution would protect the intolerant
q.why: 第四段：容忍迫害少數，等於保護不寬容的人。

q.q: How does the writer view the common idea that tolerance is “a polite shrug”?
opts: As an exactly right description
As too simple — real tolerance is harder
As dangerous to children's education
As far too hard — real tolerance is simple
q.why: 第一段：insists on something more demanding。

q.q: What is the role of paragraph 3 (“tolerance is not relativism”)?
opts: To give a short history of UNESCO since 1945
To separate respecting people from accepting ideas
To describe the problem of online outrage
To show that respecting people means accepting all ideas
q.why: 第三段區分「尊重人」與「接受所有觀點」。

q.q: In a class debate, one student calls another's idea “stupid” and says the student is “stupid” too. Which response best follows the essay?
opts: Accept both comments, as all ideas are equally sound
Ban the topic from class so that nobody disagrees
Agree with whichever student speaks the loudest
Challenge the idea with reasons, but stop the insult
q.why: 第三段：argue with ideas while respecting the dignity of the people who hold them。

tz: 寬容常被誤認為一種軟弱的美德，好像只是面對差異時禮貌地聳聳肩。為紀念聯合國教科文組織 1995 年宣言而在 11 月 16 日舉行的國際寬容日，卻堅持寬容是一件更艱難的事。
真正的寬容，從舒適感結束的地方開始。接納那些習慣只是不熟悉的人很容易；但要對那些我們認為信念錯誤、甚至冒犯的人也給予公平，就難多了。
關鍵在於，寬容不是相對主義。它不要求我們假裝所有想法都一樣有道理；它要求我們在和想法爭論的同時，尊重持有這些想法的人的尊嚴與權利。
寬容也不是沒有限度的。一個以「心胸開放」為名，容許迫害少數群體的社會，最後保護的是不寬容的人，犧牲的是其他所有人。
教育仍然是最可靠的防線，因為偏見在知識淺薄的地方最容易滋長。然而，數位時代用關注來獎勵憤怒，讓「先聆聽、再判斷」這項古老的修養，比以往任何時候都更加可貴。

ph.ex: He is often mistaken for his twin brother.
ph.exzh: 他常被誤認成他的雙胞胎哥哥。

ph.ex: She stayed calm in the face of danger.
ph.exzh: 面對危險時，她保持冷靜。

ph.ex: The school extended its help to new families.
ph.exzh: 學校把協助延伸到新來的家庭。

ph.ex: Some people do unkind things in the name of fun.
ph.exzh: 有些人以「好玩」為名做不友善的事。

ph.ex: He finished the game at the expense of his sleep.
ph.exzh: 他犧牲睡眠打完了遊戲。

ph.ex: Clean water is more important than ever.
ph.exzh: 乾淨的水比以往任何時候都更重要。

discuss: What is one difference between you and a friend that you have learned to respect?
Can you disagree with someone and still respect them? Give an example.
How can we stop angry or unkind posts from spreading online?

topic: The Suez Canal: A Shortcut Between Seas
zh: 蘇伊士運河：連接兩片海的捷徑
src: National Geographic · The Economist · BBC

a.title: A Short Way Across the World
text: The Suez Canal is a long waterway in Egypt. It opened on November 17, 1869.
The canal connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea. Ships can travel between Europe and Asia without going around Africa.
This saves a lot of time. A trip can be thousands of kilometres shorter.
Building the canal was very hard. Thousands of workers dug it for ten years, and many of them died.
Today, many big ships pass through the canal every day. They carry oil, food, cars and clothes.
In 2021, one huge ship got stuck in the canal for six days. Hundreds of other ships had to wait!

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: A huge ship that got stuck there in 2021
The workers who lived in Egypt long ago
The Suez Canal and why it is important
How large ships carry oil and new cars
q.why: 全文介紹蘇伊士運河與它的重要性。

q.q: Which two seas does the canal connect?
opts: The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
The Red Sea and the Black Sea
The Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean
The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean
q.why: 第二段：connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea。

q.q: How long did the ship stay stuck in 2021?
opts: Ten years
Seventeen days
One day
Six days
q.why: 最後一段：got stuck in the canal for six days。

q.q: In the text, “connects” means ___.
opts: stops something moving
joins two things together
digs a deep hole
carries oil by ship
q.why: connects = 連接。

q.q: Why do ships use the canal?
opts: It makes the trip much shorter
The route around Africa is closed
The water in the Red Sea is warm
The canal is very old and famous
q.why: 第二、三段：不必繞過非洲，路程短好幾千公里。

q.q: A shop in Europe is waiting for clothes made in Asia. Based on the text, what could happen if the canal is blocked?
opts: The clothes arrive much earlier than planned
The clothes are made in Egypt instead of Asia
Nothing at all, because ships never use the canal
They arrive late, as ships wait or go around Africa
q.why: 最後一段：運河堵塞時，數百艘船都得等待——貨物會延誤。

gt.en: The canal connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
gt.zh: 這條運河連接地中海和紅海。

gt.en: This saves a lot of time.
gt.zh: 這省下很多時間。

gt.en: Thousands of workers dug it for ten years, and many of them died.
gt.zh: 數千名工人挖了十年，其中許多人死了。

gt.en: In 2021, one huge ship got stuck in the canal for six days.
gt.zh: 2021 年，一艘巨大的船在運河裡卡了六天。

tz: 蘇伊士運河是埃及的一條長長的水道，在 1869 年 11 月 17 日啟用。
這條運河連接地中海和紅海。船隻可以在歐洲和亞洲之間往來，不必繞過非洲。
這節省了很多時間，一趟航程可以縮短好幾千公里。
建造運河非常辛苦。數千名工人挖了十年，其中許多人死去。
今天，每天都有許多大船通過運河。它們載運石油、食物、汽車和衣服。
2021 年，一艘巨大的船在運河裡卡住了六天。好幾百艘其他的船都必須等待！

ph.ex: We had to go around the lake to reach the village.
ph.exzh: 我們必須繞過湖才能到村子。

ph.ex: Reading saves a lot of time later.
ph.exzh: 閱讀之後能省下很多時間。

ph.ex: My kite got stuck in a tree.
ph.exzh: 我的風箏卡在樹上了。

b.title: The Canal That Shrank the World
text: When the Suez Canal opened on November 17, 1869, it changed the map of world trade. For the first time, ships could sail directly between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea instead of making the long, dangerous voyage around the southern tip of Africa.

The project was led by the French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps, but the digging was done by tens of thousands of Egyptian workers, many of them forced to work in harsh conditions. Large numbers died from disease and exhaustion.

The canal quickly became one of the world's most valuable routes. Control over it became a source of conflict, and in 1956 Egypt's president, Gamal Abdel Nasser, nationalised it, triggering an international crisis.
Today the canal has been widened and deepened many times. In normal years, roughly a tenth of global trade passes through it.

Its importance became clear in March 2021, when a giant container ship, the Ever Given, blocked it for six days. Hundreds of vessels were trapped in a queue, and the delay disrupted supply chains around the world.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Built at great human cost, the canal became a vital, contested trade route.
Built cheaply by French engineers, the canal was soon closed because few ships used it.
The French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps dug the canal largely himself.
Most ships still sail around Africa because the canal is far too small.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：付出巨大代價建成，成為重要且引發爭奪的航線。

q.q: Who did most of the digging?
opts: Teams of French engineers and their staff
Tens of thousands of Egyptian workers
Sailors from many ships, including the Ever Given
Soldiers from President Nasser's army
q.why: 第二段：the digging was done by tens of thousands of Egyptian workers。

q.q: What happened in 1956?
opts: The canal first opened to ships
The Ever Given got stuck in it
Egypt's president nationalised it
It was widened for the first time
q.why: 第三段：in 1956 … Nasser, nationalised it。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “disrupted” means ___.
opts: made much faster than before
paid for by another country
built again from the start
caused problems and interrupted
q.why: disrupted = 擾亂、打斷。

q.q: What does the 2021 blockage show?
opts: That the canal is hardly used any more
That modern container ships are too small
How much world trade depends on the canal
That Egypt closed the canal on purpose
q.why: 最後一段：Its importance became clear——一艘船卡住就擾亂全球供應鏈。

q.q: Someone says: “The canal was a gift from France to Egypt.” Based on the text, what is the best response?
opts: Correct, because the man who led the project was French
Correct, because France still owns and runs the canal today
Correct: France planned, paid for and dug the canal as a present to Egypt
Misleading: a Frenchman led it, but Egyptians dug it, often forced
q.why: 第二段：法國人主導，但實際挖掘的是被迫勞動的埃及工人。

tr.en: Large numbers died from disease and exhaustion.
tr.zh: 大量工人死於疾病和過度勞累。

tr.en: In normal years, roughly a tenth of global trade passes through it.
tr.zh: 在正常年份，全球大約十分之一的貿易會經過這裡。

tr.en: Hundreds of vessels were trapped in a queue, and the delay disrupted supply chains around the world.
tr.zh: 數百艘船被困在隊伍中，這次延誤擾亂了全球的供應鏈。

tz: 蘇伊士運河在 1869 年 11 月 17 日啟用時，改變了世界貿易的版圖。船隻第一次可以直接航行於地中海和紅海之間，而不必繞過非洲南端，走那段漫長又危險的航程。
這項工程由法國外交官斐迪南・德・雷賽布主導，但挖掘工作是由數以萬計的埃及工人完成的，其中很多人被迫在惡劣的環境下工作，大量工人死於疾病和過度勞累。
運河很快就成為世界上最有價值的航線之一。對它的控制權成了衝突的來源；1956 年，埃及總統賈邁勒・阿卜杜勒・納瑟將運河收歸國有，引發了一場國際危機。
今天，運河已經多次拓寬和加深。在正常年份，全球貿易大約有十分之一經過這裡。
2021 年 3 月，一艘巨型貨櫃船「長賜號」把運河堵住了六天，它的重要性因此變得一清二楚。數百艘船隻被困在隊伍中，這次延誤打亂了全世界的供應鏈。

ph.ex: For the first time, I cooked dinner for my family.
ph.exzh: 我第一次為家人煮晚餐。

ph.ex: Let's walk instead of taking a taxi.
ph.exzh: 我們走路吧，不要搭計程車。

ph.ex: The team was forced to play in the rain.
ph.exzh: 球隊被迫在雨中比賽。

ph.ex: Thousands of people pass through the station every day.
ph.exzh: 每天有數千人經過這個車站。

ph.ex: Football is loved around the world.
ph.exzh: 足球受到全世界的喜愛。

c.title: A Narrow Channel, A Wide World
text: Few engineering works have compressed the planet as dramatically as the Suez Canal. Opened on November 17, 1869, it spared ships the perilous voyage around Africa and cut thousands of kilometres from the journey between Europe and Asia.

The celebrations, attended by European royalty, obscured an uncomfortable truth. The canal was conceived by the French entrepreneur Ferdinand de Lesseps, but it was dug largely by Egyptian labourers, tens of thousands of them conscripted, many of whom perished. Egypt soon fell into debt, and the canal's profits flowed mostly abroad.

That history explains why control of the waterway became a matter of national pride. When Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalised it in 1956, Britain, France and Israel intervened militarily, only to withdraw under international pressure, a turning point in the decline of European empires.
The canal's strategic weight has not faded. In March 2021 a single grounded container ship, the Ever Given, halted traffic for six days and exposed how fragile global supply chains had become.
The lesson is double-edged: shortcuts create enormous efficiency, but concentrating so much of the world's trade in one narrow channel also concentrates risk.
gloss: 被徵召的；被強迫勞動的

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: The Suez Canal was a simple engineering success with no real human costs.
The 1956 crisis left Britain and France as stronger empires than before.
It transformed trade fairly, sharing its profits equally with the Egyptians who dug it.
It transformed trade through exploitation, became a symbol, and concentrates risk.
q.why: 主旨：改變貿易、建於剝削、成為民族驕傲，也集中了風險。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “obscured” means ___.
opts: celebrated very loudly
paid for by others
hid or made less noticeable
made famous and well known
q.why: obscured = 掩蓋。

q.q: Why did control of the canal become a matter of national pride for Egypt?
opts: Egyptians dug it, but the profits mostly went abroad
Egypt designed and planned the canal all by itself
The Ever Given that later blocked it was Egyptian
Royalty from many countries attended its opening
q.why: 第二、三段：埃及人付出代價，利潤卻流向國外。

q.q: How does the writer describe the 1869 celebrations?
opts: As purely joyful and fair to everyone
As hiding a hard truth about who paid
As boring and badly organised
As unimportant to the canal's history
q.why: 第二段：The celebrations … obscured an uncomfortable truth。

q.q: What does the final sentence do?
opts: It repeats the date given at the opening
It draws a two-sided lesson about efficiency
It introduces a new canal being planned
It ends by praising de Lesseps for his vision
q.why: 結尾：shortcuts create efficiency … also concentrates risk。

q.q: A company wants to send ALL its goods through one route because it is the cheapest. Based on the essay, what is the main weakness of this plan?
opts: The cheapest route might also be a little slower
Cheap shipping routes are usually against the law
There is no real weakness in such a sensible plan
If that one route is blocked, everything is delayed
q.why: 最後一段：把貿易集中在一條窄道，也就集中了風險。

tz: 很少有工程能像蘇伊士運河那樣，大幅「縮小」這個星球。它在 1869 年 11 月 17 日啟用，讓船隻免於繞行非洲的危險航程，把歐洲與亞洲之間的旅程縮短了好幾千公里。
歐洲王室出席的慶典，掩蓋了一個令人不安的事實。運河是由法國企業家斐迪南・德・雷賽布構想的，但主要是由埃及勞工挖成——其中數以萬計是被強徵來的，許多人因此喪命。埃及很快就陷入債務，運河的利潤大多流向國外。
這段歷史說明了為什麼掌控這條水道會成為民族自尊的問題。1956 年納瑟將運河收歸國有時，英國、法國和以色列出兵干預，最後卻在國際壓力下撤軍——這成為歐洲帝國衰落的一個轉捩點。
運河在戰略上的重要性並沒有減弱。2021 年 3 月，一艘擱淺的貨櫃船「長賜號」就讓交通停擺了六天，也暴露出全球供應鏈已經變得多麼脆弱。
這個教訓有兩面：捷徑創造了巨大的效率，但把世界上這麼多的貿易集中在一條狹窄的通道裡，也讓風險跟著集中。

ph.ex: The new road spares drivers a long trip.
ph.exzh: 這條新路讓駕駛人免於長途繞路。

ph.ex: The family fell into debt after the flood.
ph.exzh: 洪水過後，這家人陷入了債務。

ph.ex: Winning the game became a matter of pride.
ph.exzh: 贏得比賽成了面子問題。

ph.ex: She works well under pressure.
ph.exzh: 她在壓力下也能做得很好。

ph.ex: Meeting that teacher was a turning point for me.
ph.exzh: 遇到那位老師是我的轉捩點。

ph.ex: Social media is a double-edged sword.
ph.exzh: 社群媒體是一把兩面刃。

discuss: The canal made trade faster, but many workers suffered to build it. How should we remember projects like this?
If one important route is blocked, how can countries or companies prepare?
Taiwan is an island that depends on shipping. How does world trade affect your daily life?

topic: Steamboat Willie: Mickey Mouse's Big Debut
zh: 《汽船威利號》：米老鼠的首次登場
src: Smithsonian · The New York Times · NBC

a.title: The Mouse Who Whistled
text: On November 18, 1928, a short cartoon was shown in a cinema in New York. It was called Steamboat Willie.
In the cartoon, Mickey Mouse drives a boat and whistles a happy song.
It was one of the first cartoons with sound that matched the pictures. People heard music and noises at the same time as the action.
Walt Disney made the voice of Mickey himself. The audience loved it, and Mickey became a star.
Almost 100 years later, Mickey is still famous all over the world.
In 2024, this first Mickey cartoon became free for everyone to use, because its copyright ended.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to whistle a happy song well
A large old cinema in New York City
The first famous Mickey Mouse cartoon
Why copyright on films comes to an end
q.why: 全文介紹《汽船威利號》與米老鼠的故事。

q.q: What does Mickey do in the cartoon?
opts: He drives a boat and whistles
He sings on stage in a cinema
He draws pictures of his friends
He builds a little wooden house
q.why: 第二段：Mickey Mouse drives a boat and whistles a happy song。

q.q: Who made Mickey's voice?
opts: A famous singer
Walt Disney himself
The audience
Ub Iwerks, the artist
q.why: 第四段：Walt Disney made the voice of Mickey himself。

q.q: In the text, the “audience” is ___.
opts: the people drawing
the boat in the film
the music in the film
the people watching
q.why: audience = 觀眾。

q.q: Why was the cartoon special in 1928?
opts: It was the longest cartoon ever
It was shown for free
It was in colour
Its sound matched the pictures
q.why: 第三段：one of the first cartoons with sound that matched the pictures。

q.q: Your class wants to show Steamboat Willie in a school video. Based on the text, what is true?
opts: You can't, because Mickey must always stay private
Since 2024, this first cartoon is free for all to use
You must first pay the old cinema in New York
Only the Walt Disney company is allowed to show it
q.why: 最後一段：In 2024, this first Mickey cartoon became free for everyone to use。

gt.en: In the cartoon, Mickey Mouse drives a boat and whistles a happy song.
gt.zh: 在卡通裡，米老鼠開著船，用口哨吹一首快樂的歌。

gt.en: Walt Disney made the voice of Mickey himself.
gt.zh: 華特・迪士尼親自為米老鼠配音。

gt.en: The audience loved it, and Mickey became a star.
gt.zh: 觀眾很喜歡，米老鼠成了明星。

gt.en: Almost 100 years later, Mickey is still famous all over the world.
gt.zh: 將近一百年後，米老鼠在全世界依然有名。

tz: 1928 年 11 月 18 日，紐約一家電影院放映了一部短短的卡通，叫做《汽船威利號》。
在卡通裡，米老鼠開著一艘船，吹著口哨唱一首快樂的歌。
它是最早幾部聲音和畫面配合在一起的卡通之一。觀眾在看到動作的同時，也聽到了音樂和聲響。
華特・迪士尼親自為米老鼠配音。觀眾非常喜歡，米老鼠就成了明星。
將近 100 年後，米老鼠在全世界仍然很有名。
2024 年，因為著作權到期，這第一部米老鼠卡通變成每個人都可以免費使用。

ph.ex: I can't read and listen to music at the same time.
ph.exzh: 我沒辦法同時看書和聽音樂。

ph.ex: People all over the world love pizza.
ph.exzh: 全世界的人都喜歡披薩。

ph.zh: 每個人都可以免費使用
ph.ex: The park is free for everyone on Sundays.
ph.exzh: 星期天公園對所有人免費開放。

b.title: How Sound Made a Star
text: On November 18, 1928, audiences at the Colony Theatre in New York watched a seven-minute cartoon called Steamboat Willie. It is remembered as the debut of Mickey Mouse, the character who would build an entertainment empire.

Mickey had actually appeared in earlier silent films that had not yet been released. What made Steamboat Willie a sensation was sound: music, whistles and noises were carefully synchronised with the action on screen.
Walt Disney voiced Mickey himself, while his partner Ub Iwerks led the animation. Audiences were delighted, and studios quickly realised that sound cartoons were the future.
Nearly a century later, the film made headlines again. In the United States, its copyright expired on January 1, 2024, so the original 1928 version of Mickey entered the public domain.
That does not mean anyone can use Mickey freely. Later versions of the character are still protected, and Disney keeps Mickey as a trademark, so people cannot pretend their products come from Disney.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Synchronised sound made Mickey a star, and the 1928 film is now public domain.
Ub Iwerks led the animation work on the cartoon Steamboat Willie.
Since 2024, anyone can freely use every version of Mickey Mouse.
Steamboat Willie was the first cartoon ever made, and Disney still owns every version of it.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：同步音效讓米奇成名，2024 年原始版本進入公共領域。

q.q: What made Steamboat Willie a sensation?
opts: It was the first film to show Mickey
It was one of the first films in colour
It lasted for almost three hours
Sound carefully matched to the action
q.why: 第二段：What made Steamboat Willie a sensation was sound。

q.q: When did the film's US copyright expire?
opts: November 18, 1928
January 1, 2024
It has not expired
q.why: 第四段：its copyright expired on January 1, 2024。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “debut” means ___.
opts: a final show before retiring
a first public appearance
a kind of theatre or cinema
a type of cartoon mouse
q.why: debut = 首次登場。

q.q: Why can't people use every version of Mickey freely?
opts: The 1928 film itself is still protected by copyright
Later versions are protected, and Mickey is a trademark
Ub Iwerks, the animator, still owns Mickey Mouse
The public domain only lasts for a single day
q.why: 最後一段：Later versions … are still protected, and Disney keeps Mickey as a trademark。

q.q: A shop sells T-shirts with the 1928 Mickey and the words “Official Disney Product.” Based on the text, what is the problem?
opts: Nothing is wrong, because the 1928 Mickey is in the public domain
T-shirts are not allowed to show any cartoon characters at all
The shop must use the later colour version of Mickey instead
The drawing is fine, but the 'official' claim misuses the trademark
q.why: 最後一段：people cannot pretend their products come from Disney。

tr.en: Walt Disney voiced Mickey himself, while his partner Ub Iwerks led the animation.
tr.zh: 華特・迪士尼親自為米奇配音，他的夥伴烏布・艾沃克斯則負責主導動畫。

tr.en: Nearly a century later, the film made headlines again.
tr.zh: 將近一個世紀後，這部影片再度登上新聞頭條。

tr.en: That does not mean anyone can use Mickey freely.
tr.zh: 這不代表任何人都能隨意使用米奇。

tz: 1928 年 11 月 18 日，紐約殖民劇院的觀眾看了一部七分鐘的卡通，叫做《汽船威利號》。它被視為米老鼠的首次亮相——這個角色後來建立起一個娛樂帝國。
其實米老鼠之前就出現在幾部尚未上映的默片裡。讓《汽船威利號》轟動一時的是聲音：音樂、口哨聲和各種聲響，都和畫面上的動作精準同步。
華特・迪士尼親自為米老鼠配音，他的夥伴烏布・艾沃克斯則負責主導動畫。觀眾欣喜不已，各家片廠也很快意識到，有聲卡通就是未來。
將近一個世紀後，這部影片再度登上新聞。在美國，它的著作權在 2024 年 1 月 1 日到期，因此 1928 年原版的米老鼠進入了公共領域。
但這不代表任何人都能隨意使用米老鼠。這個角色後來的版本仍受到保護，而且迪士尼仍把米老鼠作為商標，所以人們不能假裝自己的產品是迪士尼出品的。

ph.ex: He is remembered as a kind teacher.
ph.exzh: 他被人們記得是一位和善的老師。

ph.ex: The new song made her a sensation overnight.
ph.exzh: 這首新歌讓她一夕爆紅。

ph.ex: The lights are synchronised with the music.
ph.exzh: 燈光和音樂同步。

ph.ex: The young scientist made headlines last week.
ph.exzh: 這位年輕科學家上週登上了新聞頭條。

ph.ex: This chocolate comes from Belgium.
ph.exzh: 這種巧克力來自比利時。

c.title: A Mouse, a Whistle and the Public Domain
text: On November 18, 1928, a seven-minute cartoon premiered in New York and quietly redrew the boundaries of popular entertainment. Steamboat Willie was not technically Mickey Mouse's first film, but it was the first to be released, and its tightly synchronised soundtrack turned a cheerful, whistling rodent into a phenomenon.

Its genius was technical as much as artistic. Walt Disney, who voiced the character himself, and his animator Ub Iwerks timed every gesture to music and sound effects, persuading audiences that the drawings were genuinely making noise.

From that modest premiere grew one of the most valuable brands in history, and with it a long political struggle over how long creative works should remain private property. American copyright terms were extended more than once in the twentieth century, extensions critics nicknamed the 'Mickey Mouse Protection Act'.
Yet time eventually won. On January 1, 2024, the original Steamboat Willie entered the US public domain, free for artists and teachers to reuse and reimagine.

The limits matter. Later versions remain protected, and trademark law still prevents anyone from implying a product is made by Disney. The episode illustrates the bargain at copyright's heart: creators deserve rewards, but culture also needs a common store of works that everyone can build upon.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Steamboat Willie was the first film ever made with Mickey Mouse in it.
Sound made Mickey a phenomenon; the public domain shows copyright's balance.
Copyright on famous works like Mickey should really last forever.
Sound made Mickey a phenomenon, and copyright on him should now last forever.
q.why: 主旨：音效讓米奇爆紅；進入公共領域體現著作權的平衡。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “implying” means ___.
opts: suggesting without saying directly
proving something with evidence
drawing a short cartoon
paying a fee to use something
q.why: implying = 暗示。

q.q: Why did critics call copyright extensions the 'Mickey Mouse Protection Act'?
opts: Mickey Mouse was named as the author of the law
The law was written by Walt Disney himself to protect real mice
The law was meant to end copyright altogether
They seemed to keep Disney's famous works private longer
q.why: 第三段：延長著作權年限被批評是在保護迪士尼的米奇。

q.q: How does the writer present copyright?
opts: As completely bad for everyone involved
As unimportant to the history of film
As a balance between creators and culture
As an invention of the Disney company
q.why: 最後一段：creators deserve rewards, but culture also needs a common store。

q.q: What is the purpose of the phrase “Yet time eventually won” in paragraph 4?
opts: To mark a turn: the film finally became public
To describe a race against the clock
To explain how synchronised sound works
To show that Disney's copyright on the film will never end
q.why: Yet 表轉折：儘管一再延長，作品終究進入公共領域。

q.q: A student makes a new short video using clips of the 1928 Steamboat Willie and posts it for a school project. Based on the essay, is this acceptable?
opts: No, because Mickey can never be used by anyone
Only if the student also uses the later colour versions
Yes, as long as it doesn't suggest Disney made it
Only if Disney gives written permission for the clips
q.why: 第四、五段：1928 版已屬公共領域，但不能暗示是迪士尼出品。

tz: 1928 年 11 月 18 日，一部七分鐘的卡通在紐約首映，悄悄地重新劃定了大眾娛樂的邊界。嚴格說來，《汽船威利號》並不是米老鼠的第一部影片，但它是第一部上映的；它精準同步的配樂，把一隻愉快吹口哨的老鼠變成了一個現象。
它的天才之處既在技術，也在藝術。親自為角色配音的華特・迪士尼，和他的動畫師烏布・艾沃克斯，讓每一個動作都配合音樂和音效的節奏，讓觀眾相信那些圖畫真的在發出聲音。
從那場不起眼的首映，誕生了史上最有價值的品牌之一，也隨之展開一場漫長的政治角力：創作作品應該維持私有財產多久？美國的著作權期限在二十世紀被延長了不只一次，批評者把這些延長戲稱為「米老鼠保護法」。
然而，時間終究贏了。2024 年 1 月 1 日，原版《汽船威利號》進入美國的公共領域，藝術家和老師都可以自由地重新使用和改編。
限制仍然很重要。後來的版本仍受保護，商標法也仍然禁止任何人暗示某項產品是迪士尼製造的。這件事說明了著作權核心的那份交換：創作者應該得到回報，但文化也需要一個大家都能在上面繼續創作的共同寶庫。

ph.ex: It's not technically a holiday, but many people take the day off.
ph.exzh: 嚴格說來它不是假日，但很多人會請假。

ph.ex: Her success was due to hard work as much as talent.
ph.exzh: 她的成功靠努力，也靠天分。

ph.ex: The company grew from a small shop.
ph.exzh: 這家公司是從一間小店發展起來的。

ph.ex: I have read this book more than once.
ph.exzh: 這本書我讀過不只一次。

ph.ex: Good ideas build upon older ones.
ph.exzh: 好點子是建立在舊點子之上的。

ph.ex: Trust is at the heart of every friendship.
ph.exzh: 信任是每段友誼的核心。

discuss: Why do you think a whistling mouse became so popular in 1928?
Should famous characters belong to their creators forever, or become free for everyone after some time? Why?
If you could reuse an old story or character for a new project, which one would you choose?

topic: World Toilet Day
zh: 世界廁所日：一間廁所的大學問
src: UN-Water · WHO · VOA

a.title: Why Toilets Matter
text: November 19 is World Toilet Day. It sounds funny, but it is a serious day.
Many of us use a clean toilet every day. But billions of people in the world do not have a safe toilet at home.
Without toilets, dirty water can get into rivers and drinking water. This can make people very sick, especially children.
Some girls stay home from school because their school has no clean, private toilet.
A man from Singapore named Jack Sim started this day in 2001. In 2013, it became an official UN day.
Clean toilets protect our health, keep water clean, and help children go to school.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: A funny day full of jokes about toilets
How Jack Sim became famous in Singapore
Why toilets are a funny subject for a holiday
Why safe toilets matter for health and school
q.why: 全文說明安全廁所對健康與上學的重要。

q.q: What can happen without toilets?
opts: Rivers and lakes slowly become cleaner
More children are able to go to school
Dirty water gets into drinking water
Families save money on their water bills
q.why: 第三段：dirty water can get into … drinking water. This can make people very sick。

q.q: When did World Toilet Day become an official UN day?
q.why: 第五段：In 2013, it became an official UN day。

q.q: In the text, “private” means ___.
opts: where other people cannot see you
very large, with lots of room for everyone
very clean and smelling fresh
full of clean, fresh water
q.why: private = 有隱私的。

q.q: Why do some girls stay home from school?
opts: They are tired of doing so much homework
They have to help clean the village river
Their school has no clean, private toilet
The school is too far away to walk to
q.why: 第四段：their school has no clean, private toilet。

q.q: Your school wants to help more girls in a poor village go to school. Based on the text, what is a good plan?
opts: Give each of the girls a new school bag only
Ask the girls to drink more water from the river
Start a fun day of toilet jokes at the school
Build clean, private toilets at the school
q.why: 第四段：沒有乾淨、有隱私的廁所會讓女孩不去上學。

gt.en: It sounds funny, but it is a serious day.
gt.zh: 聽起來很好笑，但這是一個嚴肅的日子。

gt.en: This can make people very sick, especially children.
gt.zh: 這會讓人生重病，特別是兒童。

tz: 11 月 19 日是世界廁所日。聽起來很好笑，但這是一個嚴肅的日子。
我們很多人每天都使用乾淨的廁所。但世界上有好幾十億人，家裡沒有安全的廁所。
沒有廁所，髒水就會流進河川和飲用水裡。這可能讓人病得很重，尤其是孩子。
有些女孩待在家裡不去上學，因為她們的學校沒有乾淨、隱密的廁所。
一位來自新加坡、名叫沈錫賢（Jack Sim）的人在 2001 年發起了這個日子。2013 年，它成為聯合國正式的紀念日。
乾淨的廁所保護我們的健康、讓水保持乾淨，也幫助孩子去上學。

b.title: The Invention That Saves Millions of Lives
text: World Toilet Day, held every November 19, began in 2001 when the Singaporean campaigner Jack Sim founded the World Toilet Organization. In 2013 the United Nations made it an official observance.

The topic makes some people giggle, but the numbers are sobering. According to UN figures, around 3.5 billion people still lack safely managed sanitation, and hundreds of millions have no toilet at all.

When human waste is not safely contained, it contaminates rivers, fields and drinking water. That spreads diseases such as cholera and diarrhoea, which remain major causes of death for young children in poorer countries.
Toilets also affect education and safety. Girls are more likely to miss school if there are no private, hygienic facilities, and women who must go outside at night can face danger.
Experts stress that building toilets is only the first step. Waste must also be collected and treated, or the problem simply moves downstream.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Safe sanitation, still missing for billions, is vital for health and school.
Jack Sim founded the World Toilet Organization in Singapore in 2001.
Toilets are an awkward subject that people would rather not discuss.
Safe sanitation now reaches almost everyone, so the day mainly celebrates success.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：數十億人缺乏安全衛生設施，而它攸關健康、教育與安全。

q.q: About how many people lack safely managed sanitation?
opts: 3.5 million
Everyone in poorer countries
Around 3.5 billion
q.why: 第二段：around 3.5 billion people。

q.q: Which diseases are mentioned as spreading from unsafe waste?
opts: Flu and colds
Cholera and diarrhoea
Diabetes and cancer
Polio and measles
q.why: 第三段：cholera and diarrhoea。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “sobering” means ___.
opts: funny, silly and light
funny, silly and easy to forget
serious and making you think
very small and minor
q.why: sobering = 令人警醒的。

q.q: What does “the problem simply moves downstream” mean?
opts: Toilets should always be built close to rivers
Rivers flow much faster once toilets are built
The problem simply disappears once toilets exist
Untreated waste still pollutes places further along
q.why: 最後一段：廢物沒處理，汙染只是移到下游。

q.q: A charity says: “We built 1,000 toilets, so the village's water is now safe.” Based on the text, what should you ask first?
opts: Is the waste collected and treated?
What colour are all the new toilets?
How many of the girls like the toilets?
When did Jack Sim start his organisation?
q.why: 最後一段：building toilets is only the first step. Waste must also be collected and treated。

tr.en: The topic makes some people giggle, but the numbers are sobering.
tr.zh: 這個主題讓一些人忍不住偷笑，但數字卻令人警醒。

tr.en: Toilets also affect education and safety.
tr.zh: 廁所也影響教育和安全。

tr.en: Experts stress that building toilets is only the first step.
tr.zh: 專家強調，蓋廁所只是第一步。

tz: 每年 11 月 19 日的世界廁所日，始於 2001 年，那一年新加坡的倡議人士沈錫賢創立了世界廁所組織。2013 年，聯合國把它定為正式的紀念日。
這個話題會讓有些人偷笑，但數字卻令人警醒。根據聯合國的資料，大約有 35 億人仍然缺乏安全管理的衛生設施，還有數億人根本沒有廁所。
當人類的排泄物沒有被安全地處理，就會污染河川、田地和飲用水。這會散播霍亂和腹瀉等疾病，而這些疾病仍是貧窮國家幼兒死亡的主要原因。
廁所也影響教育和安全。如果沒有隱密、衛生的設施，女孩比較可能缺課；而晚上必須到戶外上廁所的女性，可能會遇到危險。
專家強調，蓋廁所只是第一步。排泄物還必須被收集和處理，否則問題只是被移到下游而已。

c.title: The Unglamorous Revolution
text: Few inventions are less celebrated or more consequential than the humble toilet. World Toilet Day, observed each November 19 and adopted by the United Nations in 2013, exists precisely because the subject is so easy to laugh off.

The scale of the shortfall is striking. Roughly 3.5 billion people lack safely managed sanitation, and hundreds of millions still have no facility at all. Where waste is not contained and treated, it seeps into water supplies and fuels diseases that kill hundreds of thousands of young children every year.

Historians of public health often argue that sanitation saved more lives than almost any medical breakthrough. The sewers built in nineteenth-century cities, prompted by deadly cholera outbreaks, transformed life expectancy long before modern drugs existed.
The consequences extend beyond disease. Without private, safe facilities, girls drop out of school and women face harassment; dignity itself is at stake.

Yet the solution is not merely to install more toilets. Without systems to collect and treat waste, sanitation simply relocates the problem. The real revolution is unglamorous infrastructure, quietly maintained.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Sanitation is an overlooked problem that installing more toilets will completely solve.
Nineteenth-century sewers were the original cause of cholera in cities.
Sanitation is an overlooked foundation that needs whole systems, not just toilets.
Installing more toilets is the complete solution to the sanitation crisis.
q.why: 主旨：衛生設施影響重大卻被忽視，而且需要完整系統。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “consequential” means ___.
opts: very small and minor
having important results
easy to laugh at
very expensive to build
q.why: consequential = 影響重大的。

q.q: Why does the writer mention nineteenth-century sewers?
opts: Old sewers spread cholera, so modern cities should remove them
It explains exactly how cholera first began
It shows that toilets are a modern invention
Sanitation improved health even before modern drugs
q.why: 第三段：下水道在現代藥物出現前就大幅提升平均壽命。

q.q: Why does the writer call the revolution “unglamorous”?
opts: Its success depends on dull, unnoticed systems
Toilets are ugly and largely useless objects
Toilets are always dirty and unpleasant places
The United Nations does not support it at all
q.why: 最後一段：unglamorous infrastructure, quietly maintained。

q.q: How does the essay move from paragraph 2 to paragraph 3?
opts: From present-day numbers to history
From history to predictions about the future
From disease to the world of sport
From examples in Asia to examples in Africa
q.why: 第二段講現況數字，第三段用歷史證據支持。

q.q: A city has money for ONE project. Which choice best matches the essay's view?
opts: A famous new hospital full of the latest machines
Sewage collection and treatment for poor areas
A large statue celebrating the first flush toilet
Free toilet paper for every family for one year
q.why: 第三、五段：衛生系統（收集與處理）比單一醫療突破救更多人。

tz: 很少有發明像不起眼的廁所這樣，既不受讚揚、影響卻又如此深遠。每年 11 月 19 日、並在 2013 年獲聯合國採納的世界廁所日，正是因為這個話題太容易被一笑置之而存在。
缺口的規模令人震驚。大約有 35 億人缺乏安全管理的衛生設施，還有數億人至今完全沒有任何設施。在排泄物沒有被收集和處理的地方，它會滲進水源，助長每年奪走數十萬名幼兒生命的疾病。
公共衛生史學家常說，衛生設施拯救的生命，幾乎比任何醫學突破都多。十九世紀的城市在致命霍亂爆發的推動下興建下水道，早在現代藥物出現之前，就已大幅改變了人們的平均壽命。
影響不只在疾病。沒有隱密、安全的設施，女孩會輟學，女性會遭受騷擾；連人的尊嚴本身都受到威脅。
然而，解決方法並不只是多裝一些廁所。沒有收集和處理排泄物的系統，衛生設施只是把問題搬到別處。真正的革命，是那些不起眼、默默維護著的基礎建設。

topic: Edwin Hubble and the Growing Universe
zh: 哈伯：發現宇宙正在變大的人

a.title: The Man Who Saw Other Galaxies
text: Edwin Hubble was born on November 20, 1889, in the United States. He became a famous astronomer.
An astronomer studies stars and space. Hubble used a very big telescope on a mountain in California.
Long ago, people thought our galaxy, the Milky Way, was the whole universe. Hubble showed that there are many other galaxies far away.
He also found that most galaxies are moving away from us. This means the universe is getting bigger!
Today, a space telescope has his name: the Hubble Space Telescope. It has taken amazing pictures since 1990.
Hubble's work changed how we see our place in space.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The pictures taken by the Hubble Space Telescope
Edwin Hubble and what he found out about space
A tall mountain with a telescope in California
How a young person can become an astronomer
q.why: 全文介紹哈伯和他的發現。

q.q: What did people think long ago?
opts: That all galaxies were moving closer to us
That telescopes were not useful for science
That the Milky Way was the whole universe
That the universe was slowly getting bigger
q.why: 第三段：people thought our galaxy … was the whole universe。

q.q: When did the Hubble Space Telescope start taking pictures?
q.why: 第五段：It has taken amazing pictures since 1990。

q.q: In the text, an “astronomer” is a person who ___.
opts: builds tall mountains
takes photos of people
flies a spaceship to the Moon
studies stars and space
q.why: 第二段：An astronomer studies stars and space。

q.q: Why does the text say the universe is getting bigger?
opts: Most galaxies are moving away from us
The telescope on the mountain is very big
There are more new stars every single year
Hubble was born a long time ago, in 1889
q.why: 第四段：most galaxies are moving away from us. This means the universe is getting bigger!

q.q: Your friend says, “The Milky Way is everything in space.” Based on the text, what can you tell your friend?
opts: You are right — Hubble agreed with you
Hubble showed there are many other galaxies
The Milky Way is really a kind of telescope
Only scientists at NASA know the answer
q.why: 第三段：Hubble showed that there are many other galaxies far away。

gt.en: An astronomer studies stars and space.
gt.zh: 天文學家研究星星和太空。

gt.en: Hubble used a very big telescope on a mountain in California.
gt.zh: 哈伯在加州一座山上使用一架非常大的望遠鏡。

tz: 愛德溫・哈伯在 1889 年 11 月 20 日出生於美國。他成為一位有名的天文學家。
天文學家研究星星和太空。哈伯在加州一座山上使用一架非常大的望遠鏡。
很久以前，人們以為我們的銀河系就是整個宇宙。哈伯證明了在很遠的地方還有許多其他的星系。
他也發現大多數星系正在遠離我們。這表示宇宙正在變大！
今天，有一架太空望遠鏡以他的名字命名：哈伯太空望遠鏡。它從 1990 年起就拍下了許多驚人的照片。
哈伯的研究改變了我們看待自己在太空中位置的方式。

ph.ex: My grandparents live far away.
ph.exzh: 我的爺爺奶奶住得很遠。

ph.ex: The puppy gets bigger every week.
