tr.en: The strip grew into books, toys and television specials such as A Charlie Brown Christmas in 1965.
tr.zh: 這部漫畫後來延伸成書、玩具和電視特別節目，例如 1965 年的《查理布朗的聖誕節》。

tz: 查爾斯・M・舒茲 1922 年 11 月 26 日生於明尼亞波利斯，創作了史上最受歡迎的連環漫畫之一。《花生》在 1950 年 10 月 2 日首次刊登在報紙上，連載了將近五十年。
很不尋常的是，將近 18,000 則漫畫，每一則都是舒茲自己編寫、繪圖和寫字，沒有任何助手。
他的角色是小孩，但他們的煩惱卻非常像大人。查理・布朗孤單又倒楣；露西很愛管人；奈勒斯一邊抱著他的安全毯，一邊思考深奧的問題。讀者在這些小小的角色身上，看到了自己的恐懼和失望。
查理・布朗的米格魯獵犬史努比則負責提供幻想。牠躺在狗屋屋頂上，想像自己是戰鬥機飛行員，或是一位知名小說家。
這部漫畫後來發展成書籍、玩具和電視特別節目，例如 1965 年的《查理布朗的聖誕節》。
舒茲在 2000 年 2 月過世，就在他最後一則週日漫畫刊出的前幾個小時。今天，他那種揉合了淡淡哀傷與幽默的風格，仍然影響著世界各地的漫畫家。

ph.ex: The show ran for ten years.
ph.exzh: 這個節目播了十年。

ph.ex: Every one of my friends came to the party.
ph.exzh: 我的朋友每一個都來參加派對了。

ph.ex: Lying in the grass, he likes to think deep thoughts.
ph.exzh: 他喜歡躺在草地上思考深奧的問題。

ph.ex: The small club grew into a big school team.
ph.exzh: 這個小社團發展成了學校的大型校隊。

ph.ex: The rain stopped just hours before the parade.
ph.exzh: 雨就在遊行前幾個小時停了。

c.title: The Comedy of Failure
text: Few artists have built a global empire on disappointment. Charles Schulz, born on November 26, 1922, spent nearly half a century chronicling the defeats of Charlie Brown, a boy who never wins a baseball game, never talks to the little red-haired girl and is always, inevitably, tricked by Lucy into missing the football.

That persistent failure was the strip's genius. Peanuts, launched in 1950, gave children the anxieties of adults, insecurity, loneliness and existential doubt, and allowed readers to laugh at feelings they rarely admitted to themselves.

Schulz's craftsmanship was stubbornly personal. He drew, wrote and lettered almost 18,000 strips without assistants, and the deliberate simplicity of his line concealed careful timing within the four panels.

Against Charlie Brown's realism stood Snoopy's boundless fantasy. The beagle who imagined himself a First World War flying ace or a struggling novelist offered an escape that complemented, rather than cancelled, the melancholy.

Schulz died in February 2000, hours before his final Sunday strip appeared, a coincidence his admirers found almost unbearably fitting. His enduring lesson is that resilience need not look heroic; sometimes it simply means trying to kick the football one more time.
gloss: 存在的；關於人生意義的

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Peanuts succeeded because Charlie Brown always won.
Snoopy's fantasies were the only reason people read Peanuts.
Schulz turned failure and adult anxieties into gentle comedy, showing that resilience can be quiet rather than heroic.
Schulz used Snoopy's fantasies to cancel out Charlie Brown's sadness, so readers never felt any melancholy at any time.
q.why: 主旨：把失敗與焦慮化為溫柔喜劇，韌性不必英勇。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “inevitably” means ___.
opts: rarely
in a way that cannot be avoided
happily
by accident, only once and without warning
q.why: inevitably = 不可避免地。

q.q: Why does the writer call Charlie Brown's persistent failure “the strip's genius”?
opts: Because failure is funny only for children
Because it made the strip shorter and easier for children
Because Schulz could not draw winners
Because it let readers laugh at feelings they rarely admit
q.why: 第二段：allowed readers to laugh at feelings they rarely admitted。

q.q: How does the writer describe Snoopy's role?
opts: As complementing the melancholy with escape
As cancelling the sadness
As the main source of anxiety
As the main source of the strip's sadness
q.why: 第四段：complemented, rather than cancelled, the melancholy。

q.q: How does the final sentence connect to the opening?
opts: It introduces a new character
It explains why Charlie Brown finally kicked the football at the end after many years
It describes Schulz's childhood
It returns to the football image to turn failure into a lesson about resilience
q.why: 開頭與結尾都用踢足球的意象，把失敗轉為韌性的啟示。

q.q: A student says, “Stories about losers are a waste of time; we should only read about winners.” Based on the essay, what is the strongest response?
opts: Agree, winners teach more
Stories about failure can help us face our own feelings and keep trying
Agree, because Charlie Brown never improved
Agree, because Charlie Brown never improved and readers felt sad in the end
q.why: 第二、五段：失敗的故事讓人笑看自己的感受，並學會再試一次。

tz: 很少有藝術家能靠著「失望」建立起一個全球帝國。1922 年 11 月 26 日出生的查爾斯・舒茲，花了將近半個世紀記錄查理・布朗的一次次挫敗：這個男孩從沒贏過一場棒球賽、從沒跟紅頭髮的小女孩說上話，而且總是、無可避免地，被露西騙得踢空那顆足球。
那份持續不斷的失敗，正是這部漫畫的天才之處。1950 年開始連載的《花生》，讓孩子背負大人的焦慮——不安全感、孤單和存在的懷疑——也讓讀者能笑看那些他們很少對自己承認的感受。
舒茲的手藝頑固地屬於他個人。他在沒有助手的情況下，繪製、編寫並寫字完成將近 18,000 則漫畫；他刻意簡單的線條，隱藏著四格之內精心安排的節奏。
與查理・布朗的寫實相對的，是史努比無邊無際的幻想。這隻把自己想像成一次大戰王牌飛行員、或是一位不得志小說家的米格魯，提供了一種逃離——它補足了那份憂鬱，而不是抵銷它。
舒茲在 2000 年 2 月過世，就在他最後一則週日漫畫刊出的前幾個小時——這個巧合讓他的崇拜者覺得貼切到幾乎難以承受。他留下的長久啟示是：堅韌不一定看起來很英勇；有時候，它只是再試一次去踢那顆足球。

ph.ex: She built her business on great customer service.
ph.exzh: 她靠著優質的客戶服務建立起事業。

ph.ex: He was tricked into buying a fake watch.
ph.exzh: 他被騙買了一支假錶。

ph.ex: It's hard to admit to yourself that you were wrong.
ph.exzh: 要對自己承認自己錯了很難。

ph.ex: It's better to ask rather than guess.
ph.exzh: 與其用猜的，不如開口問。

ph.ex: Let's try one more time.
ph.exzh: 我們再試一次吧。

ph.ex: Being brave need not mean being loud.
ph.exzh: 勇敢不一定要大聲。

discuss: Charlie Brown fails again and again but keeps trying. Do you admire him? Why or why not?
Why do you think people enjoy stories that are both funny and a little sad?
If you created a comic character, what would they be like, and what would they always do?

topic: Black Friday: Why We Shop Till We Drop
zh: 黑色星期五：為什麼大家瘋狂購物？
src: NBC · The Economist · Taiwan News

a.title: The Biggest Shopping Day
text: Black Friday is the day after Thanksgiving in the United States. This year it is on November 27.
On Black Friday, many shops have big sales. Some people wait outside before the shops open to get cheap TVs and toys.
Today, many people also shop online. Black Friday sales now happen in many countries, including Taiwan.
Why is it called 'Black' Friday? Long ago, police in the city of Philadelphia used the name because the streets were so busy and crowded.
Some people do not like Black Friday. They say we buy too many things we do not need, and this is bad for the Earth.
Before you buy something on sale, ask yourself: Do I really need it?

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: Black Friday and how people think about it
How to buy a cheap TV
Police in Philadelphia
Why police in Philadelphia closed the shops
q.why: 全文介紹黑色星期五與人們對它的看法。

q.q: When is Black Friday?
opts: The day before Thanksgiving
The day after Thanksgiving
On Thanksgiving
At the end of December
q.why: 第一段：the day after Thanksgiving。

q.q: Who first used the name 'Black Friday'?
opts: Shop owners in Taiwan
Online shoppers
People who love the Earth
Police in Philadelphia
q.why: 第四段：police in the city of Philadelphia used the name。

q.q: In the text, “crowded” means ___.
opts: very clean
very quiet
full of people
closed for the day
q.why: crowded = 擁擠的。

q.q: Why do some people not like Black Friday?
opts: The shops are too far
The TVs are too cheap
People buy too many things they don't need, which is bad for the Earth
They have to wait outside the shops all night in the cold weather at night
q.why: 第五段的說明。

q.q: You see a toy at half price on Black Friday, but you already have three like it. Based on the text, what should you do?
opts: Buy it because it is cheap
Ask yourself if you really need it, and probably not buy it
Buy it quickly before other people take it from the shop
Wait outside the shop all night
q.why: 最後一段：Do I really need it?

gt.en: On Black Friday, many shops have big sales.
gt.zh: 在黑色星期五，很多商店會有大特價。

gt.en: Today, many people also shop online.
gt.zh: 現在很多人也會在網路上購物。

gt.en: They say we buy too many things we do not need, and this is bad for the Earth.
gt.zh: 他們說我們買了太多不需要的東西，這對地球不好。

gt.en: Before you buy something on sale, ask yourself: Do I really need it?
gt.zh: 在你買特價品之前，問問自己：我真的需要它嗎？

tz: 黑色星期五是美國感恩節的隔天。今年是 11 月 27 日。
在黑色星期五，很多商店會舉辦大特賣。有些人會在商店開門前就在外面等，想買到便宜的電視和玩具。
今天，很多人也會上網購物。黑色星期五的特賣現在出現在許多國家，包括台灣。
為什麼它叫做「黑色」星期五呢？很久以前，費城的警察用這個名字，是因為街上非常繁忙、擁擠。
有些人不喜歡黑色星期五。他們說我們買了太多不需要的東西，這對地球不好。
在你買特價商品之前，先問問自己：我真的需要它嗎？

ph.ex: We went to the beach the day after the test.
ph.exzh: 考完試的隔天，我們去了海邊。

ph.ex: Please wait outside until your name is called.
ph.exzh: 請在外面等到叫你的名字。

ph.ex: There are too many cars on this road.
ph.exzh: 這條路上車太多了。

ph.ex: Before you post something, ask yourself if it is kind.
ph.exzh: 發文前，先問問自己它是否友善。

b.title: From Traffic Jams to Global Sales
text: Black Friday falls on the day after Thanksgiving in the United States, which this year is November 27. For decades it has marked the unofficial start of the Christmas shopping season.

The name has a surprisingly gloomy origin. In the 1950s and 60s, police in Philadelphia called it 'Black Friday' because of the traffic jams and crowds of shoppers. Retailers later promoted a cheerful explanation: it was the day their accounts finally moved from loss ('in the red') to profit ('in the black').

What began as an American tradition has spread worldwide. Online shopping has stretched it into a long weekend that ends with Cyber Monday, and many shops in Taiwan now run their own Black Friday promotions alongside Singles' Day sales.

Not everyone is celebrating. Critics argue that huge discounts encourage impulse buying, debt and waste. In response, some people mark Buy Nothing Day, which started in Canada in the 1990s, by refusing to shop at all.
Economists also note that some 'deals' are not as good as they look, because prices are sometimes raised before being cut.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Philadelphia police invented online shopping.
Buy Nothing Day started in Taiwan.
Black Friday grew from a US shopping day into a global event, but it is criticised for encouraging waste and debt.
Black Friday started as a cheerful day for shops in Philadelphia, and now every country has the same sales on that day.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：從美國擴散到全球，也受到批評。

q.q: What is the cheerful explanation of the name?
opts: The police were happy
Police in Philadelphia were happy with the traffic
It was the darkest day of the year
Shops moved from loss to profit on that day
q.why: 第二段：accounts finally moved from loss … to profit ('in the black')。

q.q: Where did Buy Nothing Day start?
opts: In the United States
In Canada
In Taiwan
In Philadelphia
q.why: 第四段：started in Canada in the 1990s。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “impulse buying” means ___.
opts: buying something suddenly without planning
buying online
buying for a friend
buying something after planning for weeks
q.why: impulse buying = 衝動購物。

q.q: Why do economists warn that some deals are not as good as they look?
opts: Because online shops are closed
Because deals only last one minute
Because shops sometimes raise prices before cutting them
Because shops always sell old products on Cyber Monday
q.why: 最後一段：prices are sometimes raised before being cut。

q.q: An ad says: “70% off — today only! Was $100, now $30!” Based on the text, what is the smartest thing to check first?
opts: Whether the item really cost $100 before the sale
Whether the shop is in Philadelphia
Whether the item is cheaper on Cyber Monday instead
Whether the ad is in English
q.why: 最後一段：先漲後降——應查看原價是否真實。

tr.en: The name has a surprisingly gloomy origin.
tr.zh: 這個名稱有個出乎意料陰暗的由來。

tr.en: What began as an American tradition has spread worldwide.
tr.zh: 原本是美國的傳統，如今已傳遍全世界。

tr.en: Critics argue that huge discounts encourage impulse buying, debt and waste.
tr.zh: 批評者認為，大幅折扣會助長衝動購物、負債和浪費。

tz: 黑色星期五落在美國感恩節的隔天，今年是 11 月 27 日。幾十年來，它一直被視為聖誕購物季的非正式開端。
這個名字的由來出人意料地灰暗。在 1950 和 60 年代，費城的警察因為塞車和擁擠的購物人潮，把這天叫做「黑色星期五」。後來零售商推廣了一個比較開心的解釋：這是他們的帳目終於從虧損（「赤字」）轉為獲利（「黑字」）的一天。
這個原本屬於美國的傳統已經擴散到全世界。網路購物把它延長成一個長週末，最後以「網購星期一」作結；台灣現在也有許多商店，除了光棍節特賣，還會推出自己的黑色星期五促銷。
不是每個人都在慶祝。批評者認為，大幅折扣會鼓勵衝動購物、負債和浪費。作為回應，有些人會響應 1990 年代起源於加拿大的「無購物日」，乾脆完全不消費。
經濟學家也指出，有些「優惠」並沒有看起來那麼划算，因為商品有時會先漲價、再打折。

ph.ex: My birthday falls on a Sunday this year.
ph.exzh: 我今年的生日剛好在星期天。

ph.ex: The weather moved from sunny to rainy in an hour.
ph.exzh: 天氣在一小時內從晴天轉為下雨。

ph.ex: They stretched the party into a whole weekend.
ph.exzh: 他們把派對延長成整個週末。

ph.ex: In response, the school added more buses.
ph.exzh: 作為回應，學校增加了更多公車。

ph.ex: The test was not as hard as it looked.
ph.exzh: 這次考試沒有看起來那麼難。
ph.m: not as good as they look

c.title: The Ritual of the Bargain
text: Black Friday, which falls this year on November 27, has become a secular ritual of modern capitalism, complete with pilgrimages to shopping malls, nocturnal queues and the devotional refresh of online carts.

Its name reveals how marketing can rewrite history. The phrase was originally a complaint from Philadelphia police in the mid-twentieth century, who dreaded the gridlock the day produced. Retailers later rebranded it with a tidier story about ledgers turning from red to black, an explanation that sounds plausible but appeared long after the original usage.

The event's expansion is a case study in cultural export. Carried by multinational brands and e-commerce platforms, it now competes in Asia with home-grown festivals such as Singles' Day, and it has lengthened into a 'Cyber Week' of near-continuous promotion.

Behavioural economists are sceptical of its benefits. Urgency, scarcity and countdown clocks exploit predictable biases, nudging shoppers towards purchases they would not otherwise make, while some advertised discounts are calculated from inflated reference prices.
Movements such as Buy Nothing Day offer a counter-ritual, though their influence is modest. Perhaps the most useful response is simpler: treating the bargain not as an obligation but as a decision.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Black Friday is a religious holiday.
Buy Nothing Day has ended Black Friday.
Black Friday began as a celebration of shops' profits, and Buy Nothing Day has now replaced it in most countries around the world.
Black Friday is a marketing-shaped ritual that exploits shopping biases, so we should treat deals as choices, not duties.
q.why: 主旨：被行銷塑造的儀式，利用偏誤，應把特價當作選擇。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “plausible” means ___.
opts: clearly false
seeming reasonable or likely
very old
official and widely accepted
q.why: plausible = 看似合理的。

q.q: What does the writer suggest about the 'red to black' explanation?
opts: It was a later marketing story that replaced a less flattering origin
It is the original meaning
It was the police's original name, used since the mid-twentieth century
It is about traffic lights
q.why: 第二段：rebranded … appeared long after the original usage。

q.q: How does the writer describe Black Friday with words like “pilgrimages” and “devotional”?
opts: Seriously, as a true religion
Angrily, as a crime
Ironically, comparing shopping to religious ritual
Seriously, as proof that shopping is a real religion
q.why: 第一段以宗教詞彙反諷購物行為。

q.q: What does paragraph 4 add to the essay?
opts: Evidence from behavioural economics about how shoppers are pushed to buy
A history of Philadelphia
A comparison of Black Friday with Singles' Day and other festivals in Asia
A description of Buy Nothing Day
q.why: 第四段提供行為經濟學的證據。

q.q: A shopping app shows a countdown clock: “Only 3 left! Offer ends in 5:00!” Based on the essay, why should you be careful?
opts: Countdown clocks are always broken
The app is from Philadelphia
The app is probably lying, because shops always have plenty of items in stock during sales
Urgency and scarcity are tactics that push people to buy things they might not otherwise buy
q.why: 第四段：Urgency, scarcity and countdown clocks exploit predictable biases。

tz: 今年落在 11 月 27 日的黑色星期五，已經成為現代資本主義的一種世俗儀式，有前往購物中心的朝聖、通宵的排隊，還有虔誠地一再刷新的網路購物車。
它的名字顯示了行銷如何改寫歷史。這個詞原本是二十世紀中葉費城警察的抱怨，他們很怕這一天造成的交通癱瘓。零售商後來用一個更整齊的故事重新包裝它，說這天帳目從赤字轉成了黑字——這個解釋聽起來合理，卻是在原本的用法出現很久以後才出現的。
這個活動的擴張，是文化輸出的一個案例。在跨國品牌和電商平台的推動下，它如今在亞洲和光棍節等本土購物節競爭，還延長成一整個幾乎不間斷促銷的「網購週」。
行為經濟學家對它的好處抱持懷疑。緊迫感、稀缺感和倒數計時器，利用了可以預測的人類偏誤，把消費者推向他們原本不會買的東西；而有些廣告宣傳的折扣，是用灌水過的原價計算出來的。
像「無購物日」這樣的運動提供了一種反向的儀式，雖然影響有限。也許最有用的回應更簡單：不要把便宜貨當成一種義務，而要把它當成一個需要自己做的決定。

ph.ex: The new phone comes complete with a case.
ph.exzh: 這支新手機附帶一個手機殼。

ph.ex: Winners often try to rewrite history.
ph.exzh: 勝利者常常想改寫歷史。

ph.ex: The song stayed popular long after the singer retired.
ph.exzh: 這首歌在歌手退休很久之後仍然受歡迎。

ph.ex: Her success is a case study in hard work.
ph.exzh: 她的成功是努力的一個實例。

ph.ex: Good teachers nudge students towards better habits.
ph.exzh: 好老師會引導學生養成更好的習慣。

ph.ex: It's not a problem but a chance to learn.
ph.exzh: 這不是問題，而是學習的機會。
ph.m: not as an obligation but as a decision

discuss: Have you or your family ever bought something just because it was on sale? Was it a good choice?
Why do you think shopping festivals like Black Friday and Singles' Day have spread around the world?
What could people do with their money or time instead of shopping on Black Friday?

topic: Venice: The City on the Water
zh: 威尼斯：水上之城
src: UNESCO · The Guardian · Taipei Times

a.title: A City Without Cars
text: Venice is a beautiful city in Italy. It is built on more than 100 small islands.
In Venice, there are no cars. People walk across bridges or travel by boat on the canals.
The famous boats are called gondolas. A gondolier stands at the back and moves the boat with a long oar.
The old houses stand on wooden poles pushed deep into the mud. Some have stood for hundreds of years!
But Venice has problems. Sometimes high water floods the streets, and millions of tourists make the city very crowded.
Now some visitors must pay a small fee to enter the old city on busy days.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to row a gondola
Why there are no cars or bridges in Italy
Wooden poles in the mud
Venice, a city on water, and its problems
q.why: 全文介紹水上城市威尼斯與它的問題。

q.q: How do people get around in Venice?
opts: By car and bus
By car on the bridges between islands
By walking across bridges or by boat
By bicycle
q.why: 第二段：People walk across bridges or travel by boat。

q.q: What do the old houses stand on?
opts: Stones on the islands
Wooden poles in the mud
Boats
Bridges
q.why: 第四段：wooden poles pushed deep into the mud。

q.q: In the text, a “fee” is ___.
opts: money you pay for something
a kind of boat
a small boat for one person
a bridge
q.why: fee = 費用。

q.q: Why must some visitors pay a fee?
opts: To control the large number of tourists on busy days
To buy a gondola
To pay the gondoliers who row the boats on the canals
To fix the canals in one day
q.why: 第五、六段：遊客太多，所以熱門日子要收費。

q.q: Your family plans a day trip to Venice on a busy holiday. Based on the text, what should you check before going?
opts: Where to park your car near the canals that day
Whether you need to pay an entry fee that day
Which bridge sells cars
How to swim in the canals
q.why: 最後一段：some visitors must pay a small fee … on busy days。

gt.en: It is built on more than 100 small islands.
gt.zh: 它建在一百多座小島上。

gt.en: In Venice, there are no cars.
gt.zh: 在威尼斯沒有汽車。

gt.en: Some have stood for hundreds of years!
gt.zh: 有些已經屹立好幾百年了！

gt.en: Now some visitors must pay a small fee to enter the old city on busy days.
gt.zh: 現在在熱門的日子，有些遊客必須付一小筆費用才能進入舊城區。

tz: 威尼斯是義大利一座美麗的城市，建造在一百多個小島上。
在威尼斯沒有汽車。人們走過橋，或搭船在運河上移動。
那些有名的船叫做貢多拉。船夫站在船尾，用一支長長的槳划船。
古老的房子立在深深打進泥巴裡的木樁上。有些已經屹立了好幾百年！
但是威尼斯也有問題。有時候高漲的海水會淹沒街道，而數百萬名遊客讓城市變得非常擁擠。
現在，在人多的日子裡，有些遊客必須付一小筆費用才能進入古城。

ph.ex: The house is built on a hill.
ph.exzh: 這棟房子建在山丘上。

ph.ex: We walked across the old bridge.
ph.exzh: 我們走過那座老橋。

ph.ex: The temple has stood here for hundreds of years.
ph.exzh: 這座廟已經在這裡好幾百年了。

ph.ex: The market is crowded on busy days.
ph.exzh: 人多的日子市場很擁擠。

b.title: Beauty, Water and Too Many Visitors
text: Venice is one of the most extraordinary cities on Earth. Spread across more than a hundred small islands in a lagoon off Italy's northeast coast, it is connected by canals and hundreds of bridges, and there are no cars at all.

The city was founded by people seeking safety in the marshes, and it grew into a rich trading republic. Its builders drove millions of wooden piles into the mud to support stone palaces, churches and the famous St Mark's Square.

Today Venice faces two serious threats. The first is water: exceptionally high tides, called acqua alta, regularly flood the streets. In 2020 a system of movable barriers known as MOSE began rising from the seabed to protect the lagoon during dangerous tides.
The second is overtourism. Millions of visitors arrive each year, while the number of people living in the historic centre has fallen below 50,000.
In 2024 the city began charging day-trippers an entry fee on busy days, an experiment that divides opinion among residents and visitors.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: St Mark's Square is the centre of Venice.
Venice is an extraordinary city on water that now faces flooding and overtourism.
Venice was founded in the marshes, and the MOSE barriers have now solved its problems with tourists.
More people live in Venice than ever.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：獨特的水上城市，面臨淹水與過度觀光。

q.q: What is acqua alta?
opts: A famous boat
A square in Venice
An entry fee for day-trippers on busy days in the city
Exceptionally high tides that flood the streets
q.why: 第三段：exceptionally high tides, called acqua alta。

q.q: What happened to the number of residents in the historic centre?
opts: It rose above 100,000
It stayed the same
It fell below 50,000
It doubled in 2024
q.why: 第四段：has fallen below 50,000。

q.q: In paragraph 5, “residents” are ___.
opts: people who live in a place
tourists on a day trip in the city
people on a day trip
barriers
q.why: residents = 居民。

q.q: Why might falling numbers of residents be a problem for Venice?
opts: Because boats need more drivers
Because MOSE needs people to lift it
Because fewer residents means nobody is left to raise the MOSE barriers in an emergency
Because the city could become more of a museum for tourists than a living home
q.why: 第四段：遊客暴增、居民減少——城市失去生活的樣貌。

q.q: Someone says: “The MOSE barriers mean Venice will never flood again.” Based on the text, is this a fair claim?
opts: Yes, the text says they solved flooding forever
Yes: the text says MOSE began rising in 2020, so the streets will never flood again for anyone living in the city
Not supported: the text says MOSE protects the lagoon during dangerous tides, not that floods will never happen
No, because MOSE was removed in 2024
q.why: 第三段只說在危險潮汐時保護潟湖，並未保證永不淹水。

tr.en: Today Venice faces two serious threats.
tr.zh: 如今威尼斯面臨兩大嚴重威脅。

tr.en: The second is overtourism.
tr.zh: 第二個是過度觀光。

tr.en: In 2024 the city began charging day-trippers an entry fee on busy days, an experiment that divides opinion among residents and visitors.
tr.zh: 2024 年，這座城市開始在熱門日子向一日遊旅客收取入城費，這項實驗讓居民和遊客意見分歧。

tz: 威尼斯是地球上最非凡的城市之一。它散布在義大利東北海岸外一片潟湖中的一百多個小島上，由運河和數百座橋連接起來，完全沒有汽車。
這座城市是由到沼澤地尋求安全的人建立的，後來發展成一個富有的貿易共和國。建造者把數百萬根木樁打進泥裡，用來支撐石造的宮殿、教堂和著名的聖馬可廣場。
今天，威尼斯面臨兩個嚴重的威脅。第一是水：異常高漲的潮水，叫做「高水位（acqua alta）」，經常淹沒街道。2020 年，一套名為 MOSE 的活動式閘門開始在危險的大潮時從海底升起，保護潟湖。
第二是過度觀光。每年有數百萬名遊客到訪，而住在歷史中心區的居民人數卻已跌破五萬人。
2024 年，這座城市開始在人多的日子向當日來回的遊客收取入城費，這項實驗讓居民和遊客意見分歧。

ph.ex: The two towns are connected by a bridge.
ph.exzh: 這兩個小鎮由一座橋連接。

ph.ex: The small village grew into a busy city.
ph.exzh: 這個小村莊發展成一座熱鬧的城市。

ph.ex: The workers drove poles into the ground.
ph.exzh: 工人們把柱子打進地裡。
ph.m: drove millions of wooden piles into

ph.ex: Temperatures fell below zero last night.
ph.exzh: 昨晚氣溫跌破零度。

ph.ex: The new school rule divided opinion among parents.
ph.exzh: 新校規在家長之間引起意見分歧。

c.title: A City That Should Not Exist
text: By any sensible engineering standard, Venice should not exist. A city of marble and brick rests on soft lagoon mud, supported by forests of wooden piles that, starved of oxygen beneath the waterline, have hardened rather than rotted over the centuries.

It was improbability that made the city great. Refugees from the mainland settled the marshy islands for protection, and their descendants built a maritime republic that dominated Mediterranean trade for centuries, leaving behind the palaces and churches that now fill guidebooks.

Two pressures now threaten that inheritance. Rising seas and a slowly sinking city make the acqua alta floods more frequent; the MOSE barriers, operational since 2020, can seal the lagoon during extreme tides, but at great cost and with ecological side effects.

Tourism poses a subtler danger. As short-term rentals replace homes, the resident population of the historic centre has dwindled below 50,000, while visitors number in the millions. Critics warn of a 'Disneyfication' in which Venice survives as a stage set rather than a city.
The entry fee for day-trippers introduced in 2024 is an admission of the dilemma: how do you protect a place that everyone loves to death?

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Venice is a well-engineered modern city.
MOSE has fully solved Venice's problems.
Venice, an improbable triumph, is threatened by rising water and by tourism that risks turning it into a stage set.
Venice is a well-engineered modern city whose only problem, flooding, has been fully solved by the MOSE barriers.
q.why: 主旨：不可思議的城市，面臨水患與把它變成布景的觀光。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “dwindled” means ___.
opts: suddenly grown
gradually become smaller
stayed the same
moved to the mainland
q.why: dwindled = 逐漸減少。

q.q: Why have the wooden piles lasted so long?
opts: They are painted every year
They are made of metal
They are replaced every few years with new piles by the city
Without oxygen under water, they hardened instead of rotting
q.why: 第一段：starved of oxygen … have hardened rather than rotted。

q.q: What does the writer mean by 'Disneyfication'?
opts: Venice becoming a theme-park-like set for visitors rather than a real place to live
Disney buying Venice
Venice making cartoons
Venice building theme-park rides and hotels for the many visitors in the old centre
q.why: 第四段：survives as a stage set rather than a city。

q.q: How is the essay organised?
opts: A tourist's diary of a day trip → the entry fee → a list of hotels and cruise ships
The improbable origins → the city's greatness → two modern threats → a closing dilemma
A tourist's diary
A comparison of Venice and Rome
q.why: 結構：起源 → 輝煌 → 兩大威脅 → 結尾的兩難。

q.q: Which policy would BEST address the writer's concern about 'Disneyfication'?
opts: Building more hotels in the centre
Raising the MOSE barriers every day
Limiting short-term rentals so more homes stay available for residents
Welcoming more cruise ships and day-trippers to bring extra money to residents
q.why: 第四段：short-term rentals replace homes——限制短租能留住居民。

tz: 以任何合理的工程標準來看，威尼斯都不應該存在。一座由大理石和磚塊構成的城市，立在潟湖柔軟的泥土上，靠著一片片木樁林支撐；這些木樁在水面下缺乏氧氣，幾個世紀以來不但沒有腐爛，反而變硬了。
正是這種不可能，讓這座城市變得偉大。來自本土的難民為了安全定居在沼澤島嶼上，他們的後代建立了一個稱霸地中海貿易好幾個世紀的海上共和國，留下了如今填滿旅遊指南的宮殿和教堂。
如今有兩股壓力威脅著這份遺產。海平面上升，加上城市本身緩慢下沉，讓「高水位」淹水越來越頻繁；自 2020 年啟用的 MOSE 閘門能在極端大潮時封住潟湖，但代價高昂，也帶來生態上的副作用。
觀光則構成一種比較隱微的危險。隨著短租民宿取代住家，歷史中心區的居民人數已減少到五萬人以下，而遊客卻以百萬計。批評者警告一種「迪士尼化」：威尼斯以舞台布景、而不是一座城市的樣子存活下去。
2024 年推出的當日遊客入城費，等於承認了這個兩難：一個人人都愛到幾乎要被愛死的地方，你要怎麼保護它？

ph.ex: By any standard, it was a great match.
ph.exzh: 以任何標準來看，那都是一場精彩的比賽。

ph.ex: She chose to listen rather than argue.
ph.exzh: 她選擇傾聽，而不是爭辯。

ph.ex: Broken glass poses a danger to young children.
ph.exzh: 碎玻璃對幼兒構成危險。

ph.ex: They saved the old building at great cost.
ph.exzh: 他們付出很大的代價保住了這棟老建築。

ph.ex: As phones replace cameras, fewer people buy cameras.
ph.exzh: 隨著手機取代相機，買相機的人越來越少。

ph.ex: Tourists are loving this beach to death.
ph.exzh: 遊客多到快把這片海灘愛死了。

discuss: Would you like to live in a city without cars? What would be good and bad about it?
Should popular tourist places charge visitors an entry fee? Why or why not?
Is there a place in Taiwan that has too many tourists? How could it be protected?

topic: Pangu Creates the World
zh: 盤古開天闢地
src: Chinese mythology · National Palace Museum · BBC

a.title: The Giant Who Made the World
text: This is an old Chinese story about how the world began.
Long, long ago, everything was mixed together inside a huge egg. Inside the egg, a giant named Pangu was sleeping.
One day, Pangu woke up and broke the egg. The light parts floated up and became the sky. The heavy parts sank down and became the earth.
Pangu stood between them and pushed the sky up. Every day he grew taller, and the sky went higher. This went on for 18,000 years.
When Pangu died, his body became the world. His breath became the wind, his eyes became the sun and moon, and his blood became the rivers.
Many cultures have stories like this to explain where the world came from.

q.q: What is this story mainly about?
opts: How eggs are made
How the giant Pangu created the world
Why rivers and the wind are blue in China
How Pangu fell asleep
q.why: 全文講盤古開天闢地。

q.q: What happened to the light parts of the egg?
opts: They floated up and became the sky
They sank and became the earth
They became the rivers
They broke apart and became the stars
q.why: 第三段：The light parts floated up and became the sky。

q.q: How long did Pangu push the sky up?
opts: 18 days
1,800 years
18,000 years
Forever
q.why: 第四段：This went on for 18,000 years。

q.q: In the text, a “giant” is ___.
opts: a small egg
a river
a very large egg or cloud in the sky
a very large person or creature
q.why: giant = 巨人。

q.q: What did Pangu's eyes become?
opts: The rivers
The wind
The sun and moon
The mountains
q.why: 第五段：his eyes became the sun and moon。

q.q: Your class is comparing creation stories from different cultures. Based on the last sentence, what is the main purpose of these stories?
opts: To teach people how to cook
To explain where the world came from
To prove that eggs are dangerous
To show that giants are real people
q.why: 最後一段：to explain where the world came from。

gt.en: Inside the egg, a giant named Pangu was sleeping.
gt.zh: 在蛋裡面，一個名叫盤古的巨人正在睡覺。

gt.en: The heavy parts sank down and became the earth.
gt.zh: 重的部分往下沉，變成了大地。

gt.en: Every day he grew taller, and the sky went higher.
gt.zh: 他每天長高，天也跟著升得更高。

gt.en: Many cultures have stories like this to explain where the world came from.
gt.zh: 許多文化都有像這樣的故事，用來解釋世界從哪裡來。

tz: 這是一個關於世界如何開始的中國古老故事。
很久很久以前，所有的東西都混在一顆巨大的蛋裡。蛋裡面睡著一個名叫盤古的巨人。
有一天，盤古醒來，打破了這顆蛋。輕的部分往上飄，變成了天；重的部分往下沉，變成了地。
盤古站在天和地之間，把天往上推。他每天長高一點，天也就升高一點。就這樣過了一萬八千年。
盤古死後，他的身體變成了這個世界。他的氣息變成了風，他的眼睛變成了太陽和月亮，他的血變成了河流。
許多文化都有像這樣的故事，用來解釋世界是從哪裡來的。

ph.ex: All the colours were mixed together.
ph.exzh: 所有的顏色都混在一起。

ph.ex: I woke up early this morning.
ph.exzh: 我今天很早就醒了。

ph.ex: The balloon floated up into the sky.
ph.exzh: 氣球飄上了天空。

ph.ex: The rain went on all night.
ph.exzh: 雨下了一整夜。

b.title: From Chaos to Mountains and Rivers
text: Before there was heaven or earth, according to Chinese myth, the universe was a dark, shapeless chaos contained in something like a cosmic egg. Inside it, the giant Pangu slept and grew for 18,000 years.

When Pangu finally awoke, he split the egg apart. The light, clear elements rose to form the sky, while the heavy, cloudy elements settled to form the earth, an image often linked to the ideas of yin and yang.

Afraid that the two might join again, Pangu stood between them, holding the sky up with his hands and pressing the earth down with his feet. Each day he grew taller, pushing them further apart, until they were fixed in place.

Exhausted, Pangu lay down and died, and his body was transformed into the natural world. His breath became the wind and clouds, his voice the thunder, his eyes the sun and moon, his blood the rivers, and his hair the stars and plants.

Written versions of the story appear in texts from the third century, but it was probably told aloud long before. Its message is striking: the world we live in was made from a single act of self-sacrifice.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Pangu slept for 18,000 years.
The story was first written in the twentieth century.
Pangu slept for 18,000 years inside an egg until yin and yang created the sky and the earth for him to live in.
In Chinese myth, Pangu separated sky and earth and his body became the natural world through self-sacrifice.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：盤古分開天地、身體化為萬物、自我犧牲。

q.q: Why did Pangu stand between the sky and the earth?
opts: He was afraid they might join again
He wanted to rest
He wanted to see the stars more closely
He was looking for the egg
q.why: 第三段：Afraid that the two might join again。

q.q: What did Pangu's voice become?
opts: The wind
The rivers
The thunder
The stars
q.why: 第四段：his voice the thunder。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “chaos” means ___.
opts: a bright, clear light in the sky
a state of complete disorder
a kind of egg
a river
q.why: chaos = 混沌、混亂。

q.q: Why does the writer call the story's message “striking”?
opts: Because Pangu was very strong
Because the world came from one being giving his whole body
Because Pangu was strong enough to hold up the whole sky
Because it was written down
q.why: 最後一段：made from a single act of self-sacrifice。

q.q: A website claims: “The Pangu story was invented by a writer in the third century.” Based on the text, is this accurate?
opts: Yes: the text says the story first appeared in writing in the third century by Xu Zheng
Yes, because myths are always written first
No, it was invented last century
Not quite: written versions appear then, but it was probably told aloud long before
q.why: 最後一段：written versions … third century, but it was probably told aloud long before。

tr.en: When Pangu finally awoke, he split the egg apart.
tr.zh: 盤古終於醒來時，他把蛋劈開了。

tr.en: Exhausted, Pangu lay down and died, and his body was transformed into the natural world.
tr.zh: 精疲力竭的盤古躺下死去，他的身體化為自然萬物。

tr.en: Its message is striking: the world we live in was made from a single act of self-sacrifice.
tr.zh: 它傳達的訊息令人震撼：我們生活的世界，來自一次自我犧牲。

tz: 根據中國神話，在天地出現之前，宇宙是一片黑暗、沒有形狀的混沌，被包在像是一顆宇宙之蛋的東西裡。巨人盤古在裡面沉睡、生長了一萬八千年。
盤古終於醒來時，把蛋劈開。輕而清的元素上升形成了天，重而濁的元素下沉形成了地——這個意象常和陰陽的概念連結在一起。
盤古怕天地會再合起來，就站在天地之間，用雙手撐住天、用雙腳踩住地。他每天長高一些，把天地推得更遠，直到它們固定在各自的位置。
筋疲力盡的盤古躺下死去，他的身體化成了自然世界。他的氣息成了風和雲，他的聲音成了雷，他的眼睛成了太陽和月亮，他的血成了河流，他的頭髮成了星星和草木。
這個故事的文字版本出現在三世紀的典籍中，但它很可能在那之前就已經被口耳相傳了很久。它傳達的訊息很令人印象深刻：我們所生活的世界，是由一次自我犧牲創造出來的。

ph.ex: He split the log apart with an axe.
ph.exzh: 他用斧頭把木頭劈開。

ph.ex: Good sleep is linked to better grades.
ph.exzh: 睡得好和成績好有關聯。

ph.ex: The pillars hold the roof up.
ph.exzh: 柱子撐著屋頂。

ph.ex: The old factory was transformed into an art space.
ph.exzh: 這座舊工廠被改造成藝術空間。

ph.ex: People told stories long before they could write.
ph.exzh: 人類早在會寫字之前很久就開始說故事了。

c.title: A Body Becomes a World
text: Creation myths reveal what a culture considers fundamental. In the Chinese story of Pangu, recorded in texts from around the third century but almost certainly older, the cosmos begins not with a command but with gestation: undifferentiated chaos, enclosed like an egg, slowly nurtures a giant.

When Pangu awakens and cleaves the egg, the cosmos sorts itself by weight and clarity. The light and pure ascend as heaven; the heavy and turbid descend as earth, a division that later thinkers readily associated with the complementary forces of yin and yang.
Pangu's role is less that of an all-powerful creator than of a labourer. For eighteen millennia he braces the sky apart from the earth, growing with the task until the separation holds.

His death completes the work. In a striking act of transformation, his breath becomes wind, his eyes sun and moon, his limbs mountains and his blood the rivers, so that the familiar landscape is, in effect, his body redistributed.
The myth thus suggests an intimate kinship between humanity and nature: the world is not a machine assembled from outside, but the remains of a being who gave everything to make it.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Pangu was an all-powerful god who commanded the world into being.
Pangu is shown as an all-powerful creator who commands heaven and earth into being, like a builder assembling a machine outside.
Yin and yang are the same as heaven and earth.
The Pangu myth presents creation as slow growth, labour and sacrifice, suggesting a close kinship between people and nature.
q.why: 主旨：創世是孕育、勞動與犧牲，暗示人與自然的親緣。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “turbid” means ___.
opts: bright and clear
cloudy and unclear
light and pure
hot and dry
q.why: turbid = 混濁的。

q.q: Why does the writer describe Pangu as “a labourer” rather than an all-powerful creator?
opts: Because he works for eighteen millennia holding the sky up
Because he gives orders to other gods
Because he builds the world like a machine assembled from outside
Because he sleeps all the time
q.why: 第三段：he braces the sky apart … growing with the task。

q.q: How does the writer contrast the Pangu myth in the final sentence?
opts: With Greek myths in which gods command the world into being
With modern science, which disproves it
With the idea of the world as a machine assembled from outside
With yin and yang
q.why: 最後一段：not a machine assembled from outside。

q.q: What does the opening sentence do for the essay?
opts: It gives a date
It sets up the idea that creation myths show what a culture values, which the essay then applies to Pangu
It describes the egg
It lists the dates of other creation myths around the world, which the essay then compares with Pangu in detail
q.why: 首句提出「創世神話反映文化價值」，全文據此分析。

q.q: A student argues that the Pangu myth could encourage people to protect the environment. Which detail from the essay BEST supports this?
opts: Pangu slept for a long time
The egg was dark
The landscape is described as Pangu's own body, suggesting a close bond between people and nature
The light and heavy parts of the egg separated by weight, just like the forces of yin and yang in the story
q.why: 第四、五段：大地是盤古身體化成，暗示人與自然的親緣——支持愛護環境。

tz: 創世神話顯示出一個文化認為什麼是最根本的。在大約三世紀的典籍中記載、但幾乎可以確定更加古老的中國盤古故事裡，宇宙並不是從一道命令開始，而是從孕育開始：混沌未分、被包覆得像一顆蛋，慢慢地孕育出一個巨人。
當盤古醒來、劈開這顆蛋，宇宙便依照輕重與清濁自行分類：輕而清的上升成為天，重而濁的下降成為地——後來的思想家很自然地把這種劃分和互補的陰陽之力聯想在一起。
盤古的角色，與其說是一位全能的創造者，不如說是一位勞動者。一萬八千年來，他把天撐開、離開地面，隨著這份工作一起長大，直到天地的分離穩固下來。
他的死亡完成了這項工作。在一次驚人的轉化中，他的氣息化為風，眼睛化為日月，四肢化為山嶽，血液化為江河；因此，我們熟悉的山川大地，實際上就是他被重新分配的身體。
這則神話因此暗示人類與自然之間有一種親密的血緣關係：世界不是一台從外面組裝起來的機器，而是一個為了創造它而付出一切的生命所留下的遺骸。

ph.ex: Success comes not from luck but from practice.
ph.exzh: 成功不是來自運氣，而是來自練習。
ph.m: not with a command but with gestation

ph.ex: Red is associated with luck in Taiwan.
ph.exzh: 在台灣，紅色和好運聯想在一起。

ph.exzh: 她與其說是老闆，不如說是團隊的一員。

ph.exzh: 這條新規定實際上就是禁用手機。

ph.ex: The coach gave everything to his team.
ph.exzh: 教練為他的球隊付出了一切。

Do you know other creation stories from different cultures? How are they similar to or different from Pangu?
Why do you think so many cultures tell stories about how the world began?

topic: Thanksgiving: A Holiday of Gratitude and Memory
zh: 感恩節：感謝與記憶
src: Smithsonian · NPR · The New York Times

a.title: A Day to Say Thank You
text: Thanksgiving is a big holiday in the United States. It is on the fourth Thursday of November. This year, it is on November 26.
On Thanksgiving, families get together for a big dinner. They often eat turkey, potatoes and pumpkin pie.
Many people say what they are thankful for, like family, friends or good health.
The holiday remembers a harvest meal in 1621. English settlers called the Pilgrims and Native American people called the Wampanoag ate together for three days.
But some Native Americans feel sad on this day, because later their land was taken away. They remember their history too.
Canada also has Thanksgiving, but it is in October.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to cook a turkey, potatoes and pumpkin pie at home
Canada's holidays in October
Thanksgiving: how people celebrate it and its history
The Pilgrims' ship
q.why: 全文介紹感恩節的慶祝方式與歷史。

q.q: When is Thanksgiving in the United States?
opts: The first Monday of October
The fourth Thursday of November
The second Monday of October
On November 1
q.why: 第一段：on the fourth Thursday of November。

q.q: How long did the 1621 harvest meal last?
opts: Three days
One hour
One day
One week
q.why: 第四段：ate together for three days。

q.q: In the text, “thankful” means ___.
opts: feeling hungry before a big dinner at night
feeling angry
feeling sleepy
feeling glad and grateful for something
q.why: thankful = 感謝的。

q.q: Why do some Native Americans feel sad on Thanksgiving?
opts: Their land was later taken away
They do not like turkey
They were not invited in 1621
The holiday is in October
q.why: 第五段：because later their land was taken away。

q.q: Your class wants to start a 'thankful wall' at school. Based on the text, what could students write?
opts: Things they want to eat, like turkey, potatoes and pie at dinner
Things they are thankful for, like family, friends or good health
The price of turkey
The date of Canada's Thanksgiving
q.why: 第三段：say what they are thankful for, like family, friends or good health。

tz: 感恩節是美國一個重要的節日。它在十一月的第四個星期四，今年是 11 月 26 日。
在感恩節，家人會聚在一起吃一頓豐盛的晚餐。他們常吃火雞、馬鈴薯和南瓜派。
很多人會說出自己感謝的事，像是家人、朋友或身體健康。
這個節日紀念 1621 年的一頓豐收大餐。被稱為「清教徒」的英國移民，和被稱為萬帕諾亞格族的美洲原住民，一起吃了三天的飯。
但有些美洲原住民在這一天會感到難過，因為後來他們的土地被奪走了。他們也會記住自己的歷史。
加拿大也有感恩節，不過是在十月。

ph.exzh: 我們家每年過年都會團聚。

ph.ex: I am thankful for my friends.

b.title: More Than Turkey
text: On the fourth Thursday of November, which this year falls on November 26, tens of millions of Americans travel home for Thanksgiving. It is one of the busiest travel periods of the year.

The holiday is usually traced to 1621, when English colonists in Plymouth, often called the Pilgrims, shared a three-day harvest feast with around ninety men of the Wampanoag nation led by Massasoit. The two groups had formed an alliance, and the Wampanoag had helped the newcomers survive their first year.

Thanksgiving became a national holiday much later. In 1863, during the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln proclaimed a day of thanks to help unite the country, and in 1941 Congress fixed it on the fourth Thursday of November.
Today traditions include turkey dinners, parades, American football and the President 'pardoning' a turkey at the White House.
For many Native Americans, however, the day is a reminder of the land, lives and cultures they later lost. Since 1970, some have gathered on Thanksgiving for a National Day of Mourning.
In this way, the holiday holds both gratitude and painful memory.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Thanksgiving celebrates gratitude and a 1621 feast, but for many Native Americans it also recalls painful loss.
Thanksgiving is the busiest travel time of the year.
Lincoln held the first Thanksgiving feast in 1621.
Thanksgiving is the busiest travel time of the year because Lincoln held the first feast with the Wampanoag in 1621.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：感恩的節日，也承載原住民的傷痛記憶。

q.q: Who helped the Plymouth colonists survive their first year?
opts: President Lincoln
Canadian farmers
The Wampanoag
Congress
q.why: 第二段：the Wampanoag had helped the newcomers survive。

q.q: When did Congress fix the date as the fourth Thursday of November?
q.why: 第三段：in 1941 Congress fixed it on the fourth Thursday of November。

q.q: In paragraph 2, an “alliance” is ___.
opts: a big meal
a kind of ship
a holiday parade or feast in the town
an agreement to work together
q.why: alliance = 同盟。

q.q: Why did Lincoln proclaim a day of thanks in 1863?
opts: To help unite the country during the Civil War
To celebrate the end of the Civil War
To honour the Wampanoag who helped in 1621 in Plymouth
To start football season
q.why: 第三段：to help unite the country。

q.q: A poster says: “Thanksgiving is a happy day for everyone in America.” Based on the text, what is a fair response?
opts: Agree: the President pardons a turkey, so the whole country celebrates together every year
It's not true for everyone: some Native Americans mark it as a National Day of Mourning
Agree, because the President pardons a turkey
Disagree, because nobody celebrates it
q.why: 第五段：some have gathered … for a National Day of Mourning。

tr.en: It is one of the busiest travel periods of the year.
tr.zh: 這是一年中旅行最繁忙的時段之一。

tr.en: Thanksgiving became a national holiday much later.
tr.zh: 感恩節是很久以後才成為全國性節日的。

tr.en: In this way, the holiday holds both gratitude and painful memory.
tr.zh: 這樣一來，這個節日同時承載著感恩與痛苦的記憶。

tz: 在十一月的第四個星期四——今年是 11 月 26 日——數千萬名美國人會返鄉過感恩節。這是一年之中交通最繁忙的時期之一。
這個節日通常被追溯到 1621 年：在普利茅斯的英國殖民者，也就是常被稱為「清教徒」的一群人，和由馬薩索伊特帶領、約九十名萬帕諾亞格族的男子，一起享用了為期三天的豐收大餐。兩個群體當時結成了同盟，萬帕諾亞格族也曾幫助這些新來的人度過他們的第一年。
感恩節成為全國性的節日要晚得多。1863 年南北戰爭期間，林肯總統宣布設立一個感恩日，希望幫助國家團結；1941 年，國會把它固定在十一月的第四個星期四。
今天的傳統包括火雞晚餐、遊行、美式足球，還有總統在白宮「特赦」一隻火雞。
然而，對許多美洲原住民來說，這一天提醒著他們後來失去的土地、生命和文化。自 1970 年起，有些人會在感恩節聚集，舉行「全國哀悼日」。
就這樣，這個節日同時承載著感恩和痛苦的記憶。

ph.ex: Millions of people travel home for Lunar New Year.
ph.exzh: 數百萬人在農曆新年返鄉。

ph.ex: The custom can be traced to the 1800s.
ph.exzh: 這個習俗可以追溯到 1800 年代。

ph.ex: Warm clothes help animals survive the winter.
ph.exzh: 溫暖的衣物幫助動物度過冬天。

ph.ex: Much later, he found out the truth.
ph.exzh: 很久以後，他才知道真相。

ph.ex: This photo is a reminder of our summer trip.
ph.exzh: 這張照片讓人想起我們的夏日旅行。

c.title: Gratitude and Its Shadows
text: Few holidays are as cherished or as contested as Thanksgiving, which Americans celebrate this year on November 26. For most families it is an uncomplicated ritual of travel, food and gratitude; for many Native Americans it is an annual reminder of dispossession.

The popular origin story centres on 1621, when the Plymouth colonists and members of the Wampanoag nation shared a harvest feast. The meal was real, but its later depiction as a harmonious beginning obscures the context: an alliance forged partly out of mutual need, after epidemics had devastated Wampanoag communities, and followed within decades by war and land seizures.

The holiday's national form owes more to the nineteenth century than to the seventeenth. Lincoln's 1863 proclamation sought unity in the middle of civil war, and the image of the 'first Thanksgiving' was popularised afterwards as a story about national identity.
Since 1970, some Native activists have marked the day as a National Day of Mourning, insisting that memory include those for whom colonisation was catastrophe.
These perspectives need not cancel each other out. Gratitude may be most honest when it acknowledges the costs on which a shared present was built.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Thanksgiving's origin story is entirely false.
Thanksgiving is both a cherished celebration and, for many Native Americans, a reminder of loss, and honest gratitude can include both views.
The holiday began in 1941.
The 1621 feast was a harmonious beginning, so Native American mourning on Thanksgiving is based on a misunderstanding of history and its true meaning.
q.why: 主旨：珍貴的節日也是失去的提醒；誠實的感恩能包含兩種觀點。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “dispossession” means ___.
opts: winning a prize
going on holiday
sharing a harvest feast with friends
having land or property taken away
q.why: dispossession = 被剝奪土地或財產。

q.q: What does the writer mean by saying the harmonious picture “obscures the context”?
opts: It hides the mutual need, epidemics and later conflict surrounding the feast
The meal never happened
It was painted in dark colours
It shows that the feast was invented by Lincoln in the nineteenth century
q.why: 第二段：掩蓋了互相需要、瘟疫肆虐與之後的戰爭和土地掠奪。

q.q: What is the writer's tone in the final paragraph?
opts: Angry — insisting that only one view is right and strongly critical
Joking
Reconciling — suggesting the views can exist together
Uninterested
q.why: 最後一段：These perspectives need not cancel each other out。

q.q: What does paragraph 3 add to the essay?
opts: A recipe for turkey
A description of 1970 protests
A list of modern traditions such as parades, football and the President pardoning a turkey across the country
Evidence that the national holiday and its origin story were shaped later, in the nineteenth century
q.why: 第三段：國定節日與起源故事其實成形於十九世紀。

q.q: A school wants to celebrate Thanksgiving in English class. Which plan best reflects the essay's view?
opts: Only cook a turkey dinner and say thank you, because the holiday is simply about food, family and football
Share what students are grateful for, and also learn about Native American perspectives on the day
Cancel the topic because it is controversial
Teach that the 1621 feast started a peaceful friendship forever
q.why: 最後一段：誠實的感恩能承認代價——同時表達感謝並了解不同觀點。

tz: 很少有節日像感恩節一樣，既受人珍愛，又充滿爭議；美國人今年在 11 月 26 日慶祝它。對大多數家庭來說，它是一個單純的儀式，關於返鄉、美食和感恩；但對許多美洲原住民來說，它是每年一次的提醒，提醒他們被奪走一切的歷史。
流行的起源故事以 1621 年為中心，當時普利茅斯的殖民者和萬帕諾亞格族的成員一起享用了一頓豐收大餐。這頓飯是真實的，但後來把它描繪成一個和諧的開端，卻掩蓋了當時的背景：這個同盟有一部分是出於彼此的需要——在傳染病重創萬帕諾亞格族社群之後才結成的——而且在幾十年內，就接著發生了戰爭和土地掠奪。
這個節日的全國性形式，與其說源自十七世紀，不如說源自十九世紀。林肯 1863 年的宣言，是想在內戰之中尋求團結；「第一次感恩節」的形象，是後來才作為一個關於國家認同的故事而流行起來的。
自 1970 年起，一些原住民運動人士把這一天定為「全國哀悼日」，堅持這段記憶也必須包含那些把殖民視為浩劫的人。
這些觀點不一定要互相抵消。當感恩承認了我們共同的現在是建立在什麼代價之上時，它或許才是最誠實的。

ph.exzh: 這個故事以一個勇敢的女孩為中心。

ph.ex: The town owes its fame to its hot springs.
ph.exzh: 這個小鎮的名氣歸功於它的溫泉。

ph.ex: My phone rang in the middle of the class.
ph.exzh: 我的手機在上課中響了。

ph.exzh: 她堅持要我們留下來吃晚餐。

ph.ex: The good and bad news cancelled each other out.
ph.exzh: 好消息和壞消息互相抵消了。
